The next morning, he again attended the Sāgara feast, which must have been something never before seen in the human world. The mountain heights were indeed climbable, yet the waters were truly deep.
Difficult to cross. Below lies an unfathomable abyss; treading upon it, the dragon-king rages. When supernatural powers are not employed, the emotions of joy and aversion are fully exposed.
Is there no place for a brief rest? It is not yet a place where one may find true peace. Do not harbor thoughts of having already crossed over; you must take the one behind as your model.
Turn your head quickly toward the cloud-rooted crevices of the rock; the sun’s orb shines directly upon the high mountain peak.

Riding on emptiness—whom can one call "falling into the void"? Crossing the waters, one naturally relies on wet feet. Though the palaces of the Dragon Kings are deep, the offerings to the Arhats are not meager.
Whether known or unknown in the heavens and among men, the yakṣas hold up double horns upon their heads.
Seizing the mist and grasping the clouds, he rages wildly at will; suddenly, upon level ground, the waves overturn like a surging river. From what honored one has he come, and from where?
Within the sound of a single snap of the fingers, he is immediately subdued.
A single roar stirs the stinking winds across the hundred valleys; with heads bowed and tails tucked, they face the Arhat. To those looking on, there is no need for much astonishment:
if a person is without a malicious heart, even a tiger will become tame.
The three clarities and six supernormal powers; throughout the heavens above and the earth below, a single drop of ink transforms in a thousand ways and ten thousand changes.
The morning sun faces the moon, and the frozen day harbors spring. The frosty wind is as swift as a splitting arrow; this is the dense and continuous work of bamboo needles and hemp thread.
Half-extended and half-retracted, as if dull-witted or dazed; with a single laugh, one understands for oneself.

When the moon fills the jade terrace, four sleepers close their brows and shut their eyes—man is like a tiger, crouching with claws hidden and fangs concealed; the tiger is like a man. Within the world of dreams, there is no "other."
I see the green mats of wild grass spread out like carpets.
Alas, Fenggan! You embrace a tiger and sleep. Shide and Hanshan are right there within your dream.
How pitiful that even those who are wide awake cannot laugh at you.
The Great Master Bodhidharma (5) looked down from India upon China, treating it with equal disdain. Pointing directly and transmitting alone, he brandished his staff wildly;

with his three-inch tongue he swept away the six schools like a flash of lightning, and treading upon a single stalk of reed, he stirred the wind on both shores. He summoned the springtime radiance beyond the kalpas.

Return! Five leaves and a thousand petals—how brilliantly they blaze. Holding his iron staff upside down, he wears golden rings askew at his waist. He possesses the skill of a dragon-slayer, yet lacks the stripes of a tiger.
Had it not been for Song Yun’s easy capture, who would have known that with but a single sandal, he had finally returned to the West?
Ripples arise at present; wind is born beneath one's feet. It may be accommodated in the Western Heavens, yet it is difficult to contain within this Eastern Land.
Where the wild sheep hang their horns, throughout the entire world there are no tracks left behind.

The blue-eyed barbarian has no peer beneath heaven; with his two red feet, he treads upon the reeds. Because he loves the spring colors of Luoyang, the Great River takes no account of the coarseness of its waves.
Teeth missing, yet unafraid of the wind; eyebrows coarse, his spirit and courage bold. A single word once touched upon a taboo; he had no face left to show in Jiangdong.
The Pine-Planting Wayfarer set down his long spade to continue the ancestral lamp; returning again, he met Neng of Lingnan. With a single strand, he drew back a thousand-jin weight.
Important! Tell it to your children and grandchildren; how many will listen?
An eighty-year-old elder with the heart of a seven-year-old child—within this single pivot, all past, present, and future are exhausted. How much do you know of the matter at the edge of the mattock?
It is not like the profound exertion of a *dhūta* practitioner.

An old man with a hoe beneath Mount Pòtóu—within his bamboo hat lies a world unlike any other in this age. If only that bearded lord could grant him a mere inch of soil, he would have no worry that there is no place for the spring breeze to settle.
Planting pines and gathering firewood for porridge— The setting sun casts a yellowish glow as the path grows dim. With a heavy load of firewood on his shoulders, he turns his head again and again.
Does the one who speaks while wielding the hoe know this? "When I emerge with my head, you shall use me."
Li Xizhi saw Master Yaoshan: "Clouds in the azure sky, water in the pitcher;
guests arrive with no fire, so one must strike the ice. On the stringless lute lies the song of non-arising;
it is not easily heard unless one is a true connoisseur."

When Bai Juyi visited Master Niaoke, he forgot the difference between the level and the steep as he sat upon the tree; boundless wind and moon were his only neighbors. When the Prefect asked about the Dharma, the Master did not express surprise;
he spoke of it only when one had practiced it oneself.

When Commander Li saw Master Guishan repairing a dilapidated wall by applying mud himself, he did not realize that an official was approaching from behind. Observe how he turned his ritual tablet to bring about a perfect accord;
it was enough to make the void itself smile broadly across its cheeks.
Lü Dongbin beheld the Yellow Dragon Chan Master’s "Trap for Tigers" before Mount Mumu;
there was neither thunderous force nor wind-swept speed. Not merely did he split the gourd asunder, but he also retrieved the twin precious swords to return home.

In the *Three Laughs* painting, they knit their brows, refusing to become members of the society; yet upon seeing each other off, they once again crossed the Tiger Brook. A single laugh from these three men nearly made them collapse in laughter.
Mount Lu towers high, pressing the heavens of the Southern Sky low.
Before De Shan Heshang left Xichuan, he had some handle to hold; by the time he reached the South, he had nothing left to say.

With a single swing of his white staff, from the heavens above to the earth below, Buddhas were rebuked and Patriarchs were reviled; gods saw him and loathed him, ghosts saw him and feared him. This was no ordinary man.
Yantou pierced through him: "How could he have passed away after only three years?
The Boatman Monk, with his single raincoat and straw hat, leads an old life; He goes alone to the riverbank to set up his fishing line, Willing to let the boat return empty, carrying nothing at all.
The moon: the tip of the straight hook does not lie in fish or shrimp.
When Master Puhua’s wooden clapper resounds and his rush-leaf fan stirs the wind, he performs a somersault—where can one seek his traces?
From the First Patriarch to the late Baoning, there were twenty-eight generations.
Dayong Shouzhuang requested a eulogy for each of them to take back and depict in paintings.
Engraving these at Lengqia Temple was also a laborious task. One stroke against the dragon’s scales and one turns the body; nine years facing the wall—what was accomplished?
The matter: when the five-petaled flower blooms, it is spring beyond the kalpas.

When the mind is sought and nowhere to be found, the mind itself is at peace. The great earth, mountains, and rivers are but a single lump of iron; a single melody of the huqia flute cannot be fully played out.
The tune is left for later generations to behold.
A jewel among men beneath Mount Huánggōng; the fragrant leaves of jade joined in succession, continuing the severed arm.
Having received a novice monk at the age of fourteen, he was able, even with white hair, to welcome a monk returning for a second life.

For more than sixty years, his side never touched the bed. Nine times he received imperial summons from the heavens, yet he remained aloft in flight. Purple clouds sealed off the peaks of the Twin Mountains;
at the age of seven, a man arrived to entrust him with the alms-bowl bag.
At the head of the muddy river, the dream has not yet returned; atop Huangmei Peak, the white lotus blooms.
The transmission of the robe was but a child’s play, which enticed the hunter from Xinzhou to come.

Securing the Daxi Qianquxun robe, Caoxi swallows the sea as a hundred rivers return; universally responding to all capacities throughout the three thousand worlds, a flake of snow flies within the furnace of ten-thousandfold forging.
Sitting in meditation to achieve Buddhahood is like driving in a wedge to secure the root; making a mirror by polishing a brick is a trap for tigers.
Once the two eyes in the skull are made to live, one no longer strikes the ox when the cart moves.
The Buddha is the very mind; the Buddha is not the mind. Amidst clear and cool clouds, the lightning-flash sweeps by. This very function is detached from this function.

A swift thunderclap splits the mountains, and the waters of the sea surge. Deafening the ears and making one stick out the tongue, the ancestral wind is revealed. The wind follows the tiger; the clouds follow the dragon.
The head is jagged and craggy; the ears stand out sharply. A cry falls once; a laugh falls once. Measuring the ancient against the present, they fashioned rites and composed music.
Such extraordinary matters are difficult to depict. Sitting alone upon the Great Hero Peak, the wheel of the Dharma grows eight-sided.
Beneath Mount Daxiong dwells a winged tiger; its variegated markings are vivid, its fangs and claws bared. Alas for those who encounter its single bite!
Tell those bystanders they must look out for themselves. *Du du du!* *Xu xu xu!* It is this very one who insults the ancestral wind.
This little servant is a pickpocket; instead of going to Henan, he went to Hebei.
Together with Ke-fu and Pu-hua, he established the Huangbo lineage, deceitfully mocking San-sheng and the Blind Donkey, and utterly destroying the clan of the Old Barbarian.
Let it be practiced in Wu and Yue and entrusted to sons and grandsons. Six times six remains thirty-six.
True pearls are scattered within the purple silk curtains. An octagonal millstone turns in the void. Thunderous and wind-swift upon the field of Dharma.
With staffs in hand and fines paid, they are driven out of the monastery.
The Eight-Flower Nine-Cracked Seamless Stupa; the thousand-fathom sheer cliff, the raw ball of flesh. The starving tiger leaps from the precipice, ghosts scramble for the buckets.
Blind shackles and blind staffs—how utterly groundless!

The great function manifests before one; one does not cling to minor details. Riding the mechanism of the iron ox, like thunder rushing and lightning flashing, when the wooden cock crows, its resonance issues forth from the azure heavens;
when the straw dog barks, its light swallows the bright moon. This is his personal encounter with a master;
with a single roar, the demons' hearts shatter.
Before the hall of Baizhao, the grass-thief was captured; seizing him with his loot, it was no mere trifle. With a single word, he cut off the mouths of a thousand rivers;
only atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak does one attain the profound mystery.
The dragon-sleeve sweeps aside, and the whole body is revealed; where the Elephant King walks, foxes and hares hide away. Monks who indulge in wine and meat cannot endure the Teacher’s Dharma;
they bring calamity upon their deceased parents for no other reason. When skin and flesh have fallen away entirely, the Ocean Seal (Sāgarāmudrā) emits its light.
The six men who reached the very bottom became great vessels; truly, their lineage stands preeminent among all quarters.
The lion’s roar and stretch of the Master of the West River: Buddha and sentient beings swallow it in a single mouth. Those with iron brows and copper heads have never understood it;
the Yellow River flows in nine bends from Kunlun.
Old Yangqi has no core meaning. He plows his fields to buy rice, inviting others to eat. He hurls the golden ring and casts the thorn-bush;
he sells flour with the bran still on it, creating a total mess. A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves; a ten-shaded divine colt cannot catch up.
Leaving the Chaling Gate, one enters the chamber of Yangqi. There, the little is diminished and the much is added; the much is empty and the little is real.
When emotion is exhausted, there is a single, perfectly luminous, cold pearl. Having obtained money, one buys a fried oil-cake to eat.
Pungent and acrid; harmonious and agreeable. He employs the expedients of Lu Gong to receive [the guest], singing the folk songs of Mianzhou in the dialect of Shu.
A colored phoenix in the crimson heavens; an iron snake on the ancient road. Because he so perfectly mimics [the master], he brings about the destruction of the lineage and the ruin of the household.
This is the true, rugged mountain man; his application is not a mere imitation. He ruins the family laws of Dongshan and extinguishes the orthodox lineage of Linji.

With a single blow from his staff he captures tigers and rhinoceroses; with a single shout he distinguishes serpents from dragons. Standing alone beyond heaven and earth, who would notice that ten thousand horses are empty?

The flesh of the *yǔtù* is so intoxicating that one calls out but remains unaware; a pungent wind whistles through, shaking the forests and ravines. On the roads of Chang’an, the passage of people is severed;
the golden bells beneath its chin fall away only when it is no more.

Leaving home to travel as a wandering monk is the true cause. Swallowing Buddhas and patriarchs with one’s breath, covering heaven and earth with one’s eyes—Master Taibai of Jingshan in Miaoxi, uncle and nephew, gaze upon one another.
The two gates of ambrosia now have a place for the patched robes; the Buddha-sun shines once more.
Examining this from the perspective of the future, what has it become? A foul monkey in a village of three households;
a broken sand-pot as the Eye of the True Dharma. It overturns the celestial order and cuts through the earthly foundations: the nine locks of the green mountains, with the central peak towering high.
The opening of the mouth is not on the tongue; the man with clear eyes falls into the well. A bare broom stirs the vast ocean; fish and dragons alike beg for their lives.
Grasping Yangqi’s soiled black robe, his two ears grow deaf and he does not answer when called.
Throughout my life, I have tasted only the yellow sprout; it does not build a home, but only destroys one. The father is deaf and the son is stammering;
where in the eye can one distinguish gold from sand?
Mount Mao rises loftily, establishing the fundamental principles; in a single moment, he recovers the ancient wind of ten thousand ages.
The lion’s blood is truly capable of being transformed into donkey’s milk—how many can share this same mind?
With empty space as his mouth and the myriad phenomena as his tongue, he entrusts wondrous eloquence to the winds and thunder, bringing those yet to come to the clarity of ice and snow.
Casting his body across the ranks of diverse species, where can one seek his traces? Turning his body, he tramples and breaks the Great Dragon Bridge;
for a thousand ages, the Phoenix Terrace stands high and towering.
Master Pang has sucked the Western River until it is utterly dry. To speak of "difficult" or "easy" is utterly groundless. The eldest son stands leaning on his long spade;
a single note of the "rare sound" need not be plucked.

Where Lingyun and Yuanming met by chance, they discussed their hearts without deceiving themselves. After Yongjia became the governor of the commandery, and when Pengze composed his "Return" poem, it was granted that only those of refined understanding could comprehend this;
it was difficult for common folk to know. There is a monk worthy of joining the society, yet without wine, one can only knit the brows in frustration.
When Huang Shangu visited Master Huìtáng, the fragrance of the aged cassia blew away his nostrils.

On the road through Qian-nan, he opened his eyes only to find himself dreaming; from then on, he rode backward upon the green stone ox, scattering his *guànhuā* flowers as offerings for the celestial maidens.
Gu Kāiyuán and Lu Táng could not capture this with all their clever brushwork; it is the yellow of the sixth month.
The river’s bottom was frozen solid;
within the room of Chan Master Dahuì Zhantang,
his mouth was like a gong and his tongue was boiling with activity, until he encountered Qín Bā, who found no place to draw breath— like a cooling breeze amidst the palace pavilions.
White sweat flows freely; he captures the tiger by its neck alive and seizes the serpent by its head. With a bamboo switch as black as lacquer, he overturns the seas and mountains.

Amidst the bright sun and clear sky, there is thunder, lightning, snow, and hail. This is the very lifeblood of the Buddhas of the past and the fundamental principles of the Buddhas of the future—the fodder for those of true substance.
In Meiyang at Hengyang was Chan Master Hongzhi,

who inherited the legacy of Danxia and was a true companion to Xie Wei. He manifested the dynamic of sovereign and subject facing one another, fully embodying the principles of the orthodox and the deviant without transgressing either.
With hands that level the high and reach down to the low, he knows that the pure tax is not poverty; by discarding the short and following the long, he loves the wine atop Mount Cao-shan.
This is what is called the ancient Buddha of Xizhou rising through laughter and talk, and the school of Dongshan shattering the nests of heterodox masters with a single glance.
Chan Master Chao of Qu’an lies like a withered pine in a ravine; he is both a cloud-stone and a slender pine. He is a second-coming ancient Buddha who presides over both mountains;
a two-legged bookshelf within the assembly at Xizhou. By day he calls back the dream of the void kalpa; it turns out his nostrils hang down from a large head.
Chan Master Yuan’an Xuan propagated the Great Teaching, molding future generations like clay. He felt for the void and probed for bone, hewing at water to seek its traces.
From Dayang to Dayue, his fame resounded across mountains and seas. Having entered both the demonic and the Buddha, his Way filled heaven and earth. As for his final word: [if...]
This is the discourse. At midnight, the cold moon emerges from the sea gate.
Wuzhun Shifan is the reincarnation of Zhongfeng;
he is the direct successor of Po’an, whose lineage is thorough and whose insight is vivid. He mirrors the earth and illuminates heaven; he is truly the authentic standard of Sichuan.

The colors are variegated; for seven lifetimes as a patched-robed disciple, he has created enmity. Though the Dragon Gate of ten thousand fathoms is steep and perilous, there is no hindrance to standing with hands in sleeves and gazing upon the wind and smoke. —Master Baoning (Xian) *Note:
"Lai-za" (藞苴) is a transliteration of the Sanskrit term *lajjā*, meaning shame or modesty; here it functions as a phonetic or descriptive marker within the verse.*
Non-abiding is the foundation; wondrous existence is the function. Entering the Buddha-realm and entering the Mara-realm, one hits the mark every hundred times.

Shattering the cluster of akṣa fruits, one plants the vajra banner. Without departing from the primordial limit, one universally responds to all directions. A single pillar supports the heavens; the three barriers are grandly opened.
Song of the East Mountain Tile Drum. The Unpierced Flute of Shaolin (in praise of Wuzhu’s residence at Tiantzhu).
"Tsk! How can you depict Xiuju? With this three-foot bamboo staff, he is the Maitreya of the World Above and Below.
You must examine him thoroughly before striking. This very broken sand-pot fetches a price as high as the heavens. Autumn Forest.
A hundred thousand should not learn from him; to learn from him is to suffer the insults of others (in praise of Doushuai Hanging the Autumn Forest).
He extinguished the Eye of the True Dharma; throughout his life he acted willfully like a blind man. Facing south, he looked at the Big Dipper; at midday, he struck the third watch.
This decree was not issued because of a deficiency; the discourse at West Hill spread far and wide. Behold it from the eastern edge of Fusang:
the sun’s orb shines across the myriad nations. (Composed for Japan upon the manifestation of the Nine-Stone Chamber).

A rainbow light pierces the earth, its vapor surging toward heaven; beneath his ribs, a true fist is well-suited to deal a painful blow. With his lacquer-black bamboo whisk, he overturns the seas and mountains;
the True Lineage was extinguished at the side of the blind donkey (a eulogy for Xingsheng Qi Yuanpu).

The four characters "Great Luminous Treasury" (Dà guāngmíng zàng) were calligraphed by the Emperor for the Confucian Temple; the monk Guang obtained one character, "Ming" (Luminous). I seek a eulogy for it:

Sun and moon join like a pair of jade disks, their radiance shining through the nine heavens. From the tip of a single hair-stroke, all phenomena are brought forth, each vying in its beauty. With this luminosity, he continues the lineage of luminosity.
Enlightenment is ultimately inexhaustible. By what means is this achieved? It lies in being steadfast in self-confidence. One’s sagely wisdom and civil brilliance surpass those of the sun and moon;
even beneath overturned basins, there is nothing that is not clearly illuminated. When the sovereign is enlightened, the ministers are virtuous, and all affairs are tranquil.
How could he possibly be compared to the sun and moon?
High Peak Huanzhu, Qianyan, and Sanweng share one portrait; Monk Fu requests a eulogy. His eyes gaze at the clouds and the sky;
his mind is empty of Buddhas and Patriarchs. Without leaving the "dead gate," it is entirely a living path. Lion Rock has swallowed him whole.
At Fulong Mountain, at midnight the sun’s disc rose as high as at noon.

Venerable Xugu and Elder Zhenmei requested a eulogy that shook like thunder and swallowed the universe with its breath. Closing his eyes to test others, he nodded in self-assurance; his "Four Cane Whip" command.
Not acting in vain. These three turns of speech are all living words. At the summit of Mount Lingxiao, white waves surge to the heavens;
within the lion’s den, descendants fill the earth.
A portrait eulogy for the Venerable Master Tánfāng: A true iron Buddha whose lamp shines of itself at the request of Zì Míng.
A majestic exemplar with a stern and formidable bearing; his realization accorded with the King of Liáng, and he inherited the robe from Tiěfó.
He brandished the precious vajra-pestle of the Vajrarāja to shatter the dens of the wild fox spirits, and swept away the kalpa-dust of Zhōngfù and Lónghé. An illusion of jade...
The palace towers and jade pavilions loom toweringly; from the Ninth Heaven, the smoke of the imperial incense burner descends. From all eight directions, the pure breeze wafts with a fragrant scent.
This is the true likeness of Master Bieyuan Shouchang. Tian Tong Xiangming requests this eulogy.

Now, as for Ciyuan, he rendered great service to the Buddhist teachings: he swept away heterodox doctrines and opened the way for the True Path. When the Elder retired to his secluded dwelling, he remained at peace.

Different melodies, the same tune; bending and extending through a thousand ages. With a single smile, they look up and down; distinct sources, yet excellently emerging. Sharing a seat at Jade Peak, like the moon and its horn, the thunder and the elephant;
like the wind and the tiger, the clouds and the dragon. Lofty is the Terrace of Flutes; vast are the Twin Streams. A needle is cast into the water of the bowl.
The long star spans the dawn; the wondrous nature is primordially luminous, free from all names and signs. I compose these words of praise, reaching for echoes by feeling the void.
A Portrait Eulogy for the Venerable Monk Yinyou of Jingde Yunhai Temple:

His divine mechanism is peerless; his noble bones stand apart from the herd. Seated grandly upon the porch, he brings all to submission like the wind blowing over the grass. He brandishes his short whisk with effortless ease.
Like lightning and thunder in their rush, he emerged from Tianquan to appear at Dongping, acting as a tiger of righteousness for the two Zhe provinces.
He shared half his seat with Yunhai, just as Yunmen did with Lingshu. He flaunted the "Black Bean" teaching and shattered the sand pot with a resounding crash;
he was truly the authentic son of E’feng Yong’ou and the direct grandson of Jingwu Xuzhou.
The True Portrait of National Teacher Nanchu. For Yan Sheng Gangzhong’s eulogy of the Faceless Man:
before the likeness was even sketched, there was the black-lacquered bamboo staff; one could not draw near it.
Everyone says that Gangzhong was struck with such pain, yet they do not realize he was scratched where it itched. It would have been better to seize it and break it in two; let us see!
What skill does this old fellow possess? Since he has let it pass, how should one act? Burn deep incense of sandalwood as an offering;
the antelope horn hung on its branch is nowhere to be found. Lofty and towering above the five peaks of Dragon Gate.
A Portrait of the Monk Guānghéng of Làngyī. At the request of his junior disciple, the Head Seat Yúnmǎo, I offer this eulogy:

Vast and boundless like the deep blue ocean, his capacity of mind is overflowing. To approach him is like basking in the warmth of the sun without the need for spring; to stir him is like the roar of thunder without the display of anger.
He builds great halls to harbor idle men; he opens a vast mouth to swallow Buddhas and patriarchs. Those who know him call him a true-born "white-thief";
those who do not know him call him a reincarnation of Beidu. A long sword between his brows leans against the cold heavens;
an iron serpent in his hand lies across the ancient road.
Kai Fu, Old Monk Yue’an, Yue Lin, Wu Men, Fa Deng, and Gao Shan—these were seven generations.
The Abbot Jiu of Ritsu-ji painted their portraits and requested inscriptions to take back home.
On a spring day when the rain has cleared, three or four wisps of white cloud drift by; a yellow bird sings once or twice. What a display!
The ancestral tradition of Dongshan: amidst the clamor, he opens the gate of Fuku. *Pah!* Great Compassion does not extend its hand; his entire body is eyes.
When Xi Zhong fashioned a chariot with a hundred spokes, he removed both ends and discarded the axle—this was simply because he mistook the fixed platter for the truth.
The stars. Their true sounds often have no one to continue them; no one continues them. Six times six remains thirty-six.
Controlling the great pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, expanding the true eye of humans and devas. A catfish climbs a bamboo pole;
a python enters a reed flute—*Duḥ!* Since the nature of things is fundamentally non-existent, what use is there for severing?

Transcending through a single gate is the "Returning Crow. A shout downward once caused the seas and mountains to crumble. It was not transmitted from the land of Chu, yet it is believed in the land of Tang.
The fragrant breeze blows, causing the cassia flowers to bloom.
Under the bright sun and clear blue sky, with thunderclaps and flashing lightning, all phenomena go deaf and empty space reels. Mount Sumeru leaps and dances through the three stages;
for the first time in a thousand ages, the gateless barrier has opened its eight characters.

His orthodox eye was profoundly clear and his true style was preeminent; having personally realized the Gateless Barrier, his discourse spread throughout the world. For eighty-two years, he did not rest his side upon a bed.
More than three hundred people entered the great furnace and bellows; their hair, fur, nails, and teeth shook the earth as they emitted radiance.
Those clad in blue, purple, black, and yellow robes prostrate themselves upon seeing his dust; this is the so-called National Teacher Fǎdēng of ninety-nine years from the Kingdom of Japan.
Like a *maṇi* jewel that remains unbroken even when struck by an iron hammer after a conflagration, he is one whom the high mountains look up to and whose exemplary conduct one follows.
Under a great name, one cannot remain for long. As a guest, be fully a guest; as a host, be fully a host.
Three thousand miles away, misunderstandings are certain. Break the mirror and come to see me!
The Portrait of Master Zhongmou of Xianyan: Requested by Librarian Jing to provide a eulogy:
In the Chamber of Ambrosia, he struck away his nostrils; Beside Phoenix Terrace, he exchanged his eyes. He sat firmly, cutting off all traces at Ducheng.

He widely propagated the Great Teaching, overturning all that had come before; he extinguished the true lamp, yet at the tips of the hundred grasses he fully exercised the Right Command, and atop the Three Maidens’ Pond he rolled forth thunder and lightning.
In self-praise, I say:

when I met with Elder Dayun Zhi, who requested this eulogy, we reached a silent accord before a word was spoken. He is like a great cloud that universally covers all things, yet can roll them up and store them away within itself.

Though it begins as no more than a skin-thickness or a cubit, when dispersed, it fills the six directions. How could this be called exceeding its proper measure? Sometimes it becomes wind and thunder; sometimes it becomes drenching rain.
The myriad transformations stir and multiply, each finding its proper place. Although such manifestations arise, their source is without intention. Clouds, oh clouds!
Only you and I are able to take this Way upon ourselves. Elder Changlu Yi has requested a eulogy for his assembly, which takes the dust-motes of all lands as its monastic community;
yet your body remains unbound. He seeks to broaden the ten voids as a gateway for salvation; yet your mind finds no satisfaction therein.
When the conditions were ripe, he came with great enthusiasm; when his spirit was fully spent, he departed.
Deshan’s staff had not yet broken, and Linji’s shout was not yet exhausted. By this, he upholds the orthodox lineage of Bodhidharma; by this, he guides those of Mahayana capacity.
It is much like the distance from Zhenzhou to Changlu—more than ninety li. Alas! How haughty and disdainful!
All things wander freely upon a single mound; fragrances link and flames connect throughout the land of Zhongguo.

At the request of the Elder Qingshan Hao, I offer praise for the three turning-words within the chamber of Songyuan. From antiquity to the present, no one has dared to insert a word; suddenly, Weyu emerges.

Mountains. To swallow up the waters of the West River in a single gulp—there is no handle to grasp, yet there is a reason for it. Turning over the vast ocean, he readjusts the hook for catching the giant turtle.
Written by Shishouzuo as a request for praise.
The Great Void is its substance; the myriad phenomena are its function. When the sun shines and the moon descends, when the wind blows and the thunder rolls—this is seeing Lingyan.
To carve at the waves in search of cracks and seams is to see Lingyan apart from this. To call a bell a jar is to see Lingyan apart from this.
When both "not apart" and "not identical" are forgotten, the magpie’s nest gives way to the phoenix soaring from Mount Dan.

Chan Master Gaō requests a eulogy for the Great Elephant hidden within the formless and the Great Sound concealed within the rarefied silence. It reveals the traces of the undifferentiated primordial chaos;
it blinds the eyes at the Vajra-summit gate. To hold fast, the empty chamber gives birth to white light; to let go, the hundred rivers flow forth.
Boiling over! He shatters the Heart-Mind Seal of Shaolin; the bright sun hangs high in the azure sky.
Chan Master Shou invited me to praise his lifelong, unrestrained discourse on Zen—what evidence could there possibly be for it? He unravels Linji’s Three Mysteries and sweeps away [all obstructions].
Dongshan’s Five Ranks were compiled by my nephew Shou and published by my nephew Shan;
they should have been buried in a single pit to avoid mutual frustration. How could one bear to further use brush and ink to paint out such a face?
Though the lands of the Great Yuan are vast, where could they possibly contain you? *Pfft!* Hang it toward Fusang in Japan to the east;
you shall surely ensure its radiance illumines heaven and earth.
The Abbot Du invited [the Master] to offer a eulogy;
throughout the entire day he preached the Dharma, yet there was no dharma to be preached. Throughout his life he saved sentient beings, yet there were no sentient beings to be saved.

He overturned the secondary gate of meaning; there is a separate path that transcends it. Sitting atop a solitary peak, his true command is exercised: when the dragon appears, the clouds follow; when the wind arises, the grass bends.
From Hu: The Abbot Shuo requests a eulogy for one whose greatness is peerless.
Vast and profoundly luminous, he operates alone, cutting across all capacities; he blends with the myriad transformations while forgetting his own form.
To say that he poured forth his innermost thoughts to propagate the Great Teaching is surely to forget one’s own flaws out of affection; such praise for his reputation exceeds the facts.

To say that he withdrew into seclusion to settle his final years in peace is, when compared with those who sacrificed their lives to bring calamity upon their ancestors, perhaps a journey of half a month [in distance].
Both cases are ranked as inferior. True beauty arises from within; it must pass through the shallow current to emerge.
Thirty thousand *li* away, the sun rises over the sea and the night tide is calm.
Elder Mingyan Kang requested a eulogy for Deshan’s nostrils, Linji’s eyes, and Yunmen’s piercing glance; they were not alert from the start—so who would call them Hanshan and Shide?
Flowing streams take different paths yet meet at the same ford—how extraordinary! Alas, there is nothing with which it can be compared;
how am I to describe it? Elder Xing of Lizhou requests a eulogy:
His mouth is like a wooden mallet; his eyes resemble drumsticks. He hangs up sheep while selling dogs, seeking every possible advantage and utterly extinguishing the ancestral style.
Who is it even more so? A pair of red apricots exchanged for a persimmon.

Clearly, when the Elder Mingyin invited him to praise the Way, [Zhaozhou] said, "The Way is not outside of things; that which is outside of things is not the Way. Not a single word fit. The stone was whipped and thunder roared; the wind cleared over Lake Lishi.
The moon is bright atop Lion Peak; sitting firmly, he brings the true command of all Wu to bear. What need is there to hide one's body within the Northern Dipper?

Treasure Master, please offer a verse of praise for "One Treasure of the Central Plains. As for its price: how laughable is Emperor Tongguang, who tried to deceive Xinghua with empty flattery. Heaven is eternal, and earth is everlasting.
The mountains are high and the waters are deep; fundamentally, there is nothing. Where can one seek the mind? Lift up the broken sand-pot and employ the method of black beans.
When you roll out with a dusty head upon the surface of the earth, the four modes of birth and the nine realms of existence are uprooted together.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Liaoyuan, Volume Five.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Liaoyuan, Volume Six:
Verses and Eulogies.
Compiled by the monk Sāṅxué, Rǔxiàn, Yuánbǎo, Huìlǎng, and others, this work on the rhyme of Zhòngmóu of Wúxiǎng is respectfully sent to the Head Seat Jiǎo.

From the secret transmission at Mount Ling, the single-lineage succession of Shaoshi, essence and function are non-dual, and phenomena and principle are clearly manifest; they are distinguished at the tip of the staff.
The Great Flower is opened; beneath the hood of the *kaṣāya*, the three thousand worlds are covered. Whether light comes or darkness comes, one points at the locust tree and scolds the willow;
going east or going west, one turns the Kun hexagram and rotates the Qian hexagram. The spark of flint and the falling star are not yet urgent; the silver mountains and iron walls—how firm they are!
Xu Liu’s wooden board suddenly drops; Dou Ba’s shirt is once again torn through. Cease dwelling on the heels not touching the ground—who says this has already been brushed past the era before Wiyin?
Seven years of four round-trips: digging in the earth to seek the blue sky. Having moved the boat, one leaves the water;
raising the oars, one finally encounters the source. With whose backbone shall I make a stabilizing pillar? I shall use your nostrils as the pivot.
The Southern Pointer: Turning over on the heavenly shore to watch the rising sun, its radiance illuminates the myriad phenomena, distinguishing the beautiful from the ugly.
Following the rhyme of my Dharma-brother Zhongmou to see off Attendant Zhao, [I reflect upon] the World-Honored One’s samādhi;
Kāśyapa did not know it, yet he broke into a smile. Measuring with a ladle and peering through a tube, I have seized the heavy barrier.
The lush yellow flowers are fundamentally not Prajñā; let go of the path. The verdant green bamboos are all True Suchness (Tathatā).
Amidst the thorny forest, the boundless vastness is revealed; upon the level ground, the towering majesty of ten-thousand-fathom heights stands steep.

Where knowledge cannot reach, the mind may yet contemplate. To act contrary to the ordinary is to accord with the Way; to grasp the mainstay and pull the ropes—this is the "Poreless" [Koan] of Shaolin.
Flute. For you I go; let me blow it but once. From east to west, it shall mend the long with the short;
from south to north, it shall level the high by following the low.

Sending off the Abbot Huizang—there isn't a single word. What could possibly be said? Casting it here and there, playing with the real and the false; the whole body is clearly manifest when one can bring it forth in its entirety.
The thatched hut sheds its lapis lazuli tiles; picking up a black bean to exchange for the eyes of a ghost; pushing aside empty space.
Seeking the needle’s eye through the seam: before me there is no you; before you there is no me. North, south, east, and west—opened wide like the eight characters.
Where there is light, there is darkness; where there is darkness, there is light. Birth, abiding, decay, and emptiness are all simultaneously rent asunder.
Deshan and Linji are like children at play; they topple over the Western Barbarian Bodhidharma.

They send the superior man Cheshang to the very peak of his faculties, where a blow from the staff brings him through. The wordless youth prattles on; neither Miaode nor Śāriputra has ever known this.
Kauṇḍinya extends his tongue; one tap, two strikes, and ice-cold droplets arise. He lets go twice and hurls it three times—thunder rolls and lightning flashes.
Resting? Not resting; never ceasing. Xuefeng rolling the ball is too solitary and remote;
were it not for Xuansha who knew how to split the wooden tablet, how could the pure breeze fill the vast void? From what direction have you come, son? Your spiritual capacity is truly transcendent.

With wondrous realization, you continue the ancestral lineage; be careful not to follow the beaten tracks. Moreover, having personally inherited from the Ancient Phoenix Terrace, act as my "nail" to pin down the void.
Presented to the Chief Seat Holder.
The void is his mouth, the myriad phenomena are his tongue; he speaks of the dust-motes, he speaks of the lands, he speaks with blazing intensity.
Yet upon reaching the end, there is not a single character. To the eyes of a patch-robed monk, this only adds more dross. Pearls turn and jade revolves as the subtle mysteries are distinguished;
look at how they are upheld through the staff and the shout. Suddenly treading upon the aperture of the crown, who can know that one throw beyond the heavens? At times he gathers them in.
At that moment he releases it; light and darkness are both transcended—truly a peerless song. Hands and face are separated across a ten-thousand-fathom cliff;
before one's eyes, waves a thousand fathoms high surge forth. Like sparks struck from stone or a flash of lightning, how could those with copper heads and iron jaws withstand it?
Sweeping away the old fox dens of the past, he is just right to reveal the Vajra King. Beyond the four propositions and free from the hundred negations—Kauṇḍinya!
Chewing raw iron; administering poison, medicine, or clarified butter as a single path. Earth grows old and heaven wastes away—who can distinguish them?
Xuefeng fully possessed the way of the guest;
Zujue fully possessed the dharma of an ordinary person. Turning a stone mortar in mid-air, he fully possessed the dharma of a sage. Facing south, he looked at the Big Dipper.

When the three balls roll out, forty-nine strikes at once. The trident in Bimā’s hand, the dog beneath Zihu’s gate—conquering the enemy and startling the multitude, returning the lion’s roar. Lifting up a winnowing basket to pound grain elsewhere:
from the great Huai north and south, the Jiangxi east, eighty-four men, all so bewildered. Their skulls chant the pine wind day and night.
Baizhang Qing, the Abbot, sits alone atop Mount Daxiong.
What is so extraordinary about this? Having turned over the entire Tripitaka, he naturally transcends both speech and silence.

The wondrous hand of supernormal powers is presented before one’s face; shifting the constellations and displacing the stars, it is unfathomable to both sages and commoners. Even a swift hawk swooping through the void treats it as a mere trifle;
yet by the time it lifts its head, it has already passed beyond the kingdom of Silla.
To the Abbot Sòngmào:
The Tathāgata-garbha of the three thousandfold world-systems—whether spoken or silent, all deliberation is slander.

To overturn Mount Sumeru and look at the Southern Pointer, even a splitting rock or crumbling cliff cannot come near it. The Master Yāngxiāng is truly extraordinary; with a single stroke of his hand, he deceives the world.
Yangqi: At that time, there were three or five hundred people at a single assembly. Who was it that could penetrate the golden dust?

This mountain monk has a mouth but no leisure to speak; you too must seek resolution on the road ahead. Striking down the white phoenix chick from the edge of heaven, my seven-foot black staff is as cold as iron.
I have a phrase to give you as you, Attendant Zu, return to Wenzhou:
"On level ground, a raging storm rises without wind. If there were not even a single phrase for you, it would be like "the barefoot Persian entering the bustling marketplace.
It is better to cast away both existence and non-existence, opening wide both eyes over the entirety of the land of Wu. An iron ox.
What is this mechanism? A snowflake pierces the furnace where gold is smelted. If you do not see it, the old man of Heishan knows how to beat the drum;
every beat accords with Daowu’s dance. The myriad phenomena of the universe clamor and chatter, yet they fundamentally distinguish the paths of earth and water.
On the river the wind blows, beneath the pines the moon shines; the many-year-old nails and wedges are pulled out. Yongjia saw it for himself.
Taking up the legacy of Nanquan, this is precisely the present moment. The melody of Shaolin and the song of Xinfeng—throughout ten thousand miles, who knows its true sound?
Returning to the western mountains to sweep the misty mat, try threading the jade thread through the golden needle.

I present to Attendant Lin this "Vajra Circle" and "Iron Sour Filling. Add where there is too little; subtract where there is too much. When an attendant attains Zen, one blow cuts through everything:
mountains, rivers, and the great earth do not appear as even a speck of dust; grasses, trees, thickets, and forests radiate their luster and brilliance. Strike it!
Striking oneself, one knows the pain; holding fast or letting go is like a shadow or an echo. Śākyamuni and Maitreya are still his servants;
what skill do Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have? Seizing the heavens and earth to distinguish the orthodox from the heterodox, they reach out their hands yet remain unaware of their own palms.
*Duḥ!* (A shout of realization)
Seeing off Attendant Cheng:
For a son to study the Way, success is what matters most. With every step, he ought to transcend the ordinary path. Upon the peak of Mount Sumeru, the sun and moon blaze;
from the depths of the great ocean, thunder rolls. Taking up a single arrow of thistle and mugwort, even upon the battlefield—must one not strike?
A hundred battles. In the five ranks, ruler and minister are arrayed as both orthodox and deviant; the trident of the three mysteries and armor shift according to the occasion.

Sometimes there is release—wholly killing and wholly giving life, who can share in this? Sometimes there is seizure—the ocean of lands in the ten directions is swept across and leveled. Have you not seen?
Before Master Wenyuan raised his staff, he once contended with Zhaozhou over who was superior or inferior.

As the Abbot Ming is sent to Eastern Zhejiang to expound the *Vajracchedikā Sūtra*, the myriad phenomena listen with bated breath. He turns the pivot of the ultimate barrier and strips away the sickness of Buddhas and patriarchs.
Going east or going west, three before and three behind; coming from the south or coming from the north, head straight and tail straight.
To invert one and explain it by matching another—how can the hawk’s eye and the dragon’s pupil distinguish them? Leveling the high and conforming to the low, seizing one device with another;

revealing the Real and opening the Provisional; using a wedge to extract a wedge. Eloquence yet reticent, skillful yet seemingly clumsy; whether moving against or with the current, or traversing vertically and horizontally, it is truly marvelous. You, sir, do not...

Behold! Upon the eyelashes of a tiny gnat, the earth is vast and people are rare; amidst the flash of a stone flint, frost gathers and freezes solid. Throughout the hundred Yue and three Wu regions, the True Command is being enacted.
Who would say that those traveling the same road take different paths?

I send this poem for the Abbot Yacang, Daochun, who departs tomorrow for Longxiang. He requested that I write these long lines before the lamp. The wind and rain fill the heavens, creating a Mid-Autumn scene;
it is as if the waters of a thousand rivers flow eastward. I myself have never mastered Zen; I simply speak from the mouth, fitting together the profound mysteries.
The profound mystery of the Middle Way: Śākyamuni did not know it existed; how could the Great and Small Tripitakas possibly explain it?

Do you not see? The blind donkey extinguished the Eye of the True Dharma; in the end, he became nothing more than a man carrying a wooden board. How laughable that Dongshan released what he had gathered!
Skillful means remain devoid of skillful means; now this Way is like mud and earth. Blocking valleys and filling ditches—of what account is it?
Beyond the Seven Golden Mountains, one seeks a kindred spirit; at midnight, a gnat swallows a tiger.
A Gift to Elder Puguang (Inscription for the Fundraising for the Lotus Sutra at the Dharma Site of National Teacher Shao, the Buddha Hall) The National Teacher did not reveal his crown;
this phrase flows forth as a single drop from the Cao River source. It drenches the sun and floods the heavens—there is no help for it.
How many times has it soaked and rotted empty space? At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this world; he severs the golden lock and opens the gates.
A heavy barrier. At the top of a hundred-foot pole, one displays their skill; the second, third, fourth, and seventh all show their faces.

The *puṇḍarīka* flower appears but once in a while; its halls and pavilions soar loftily, piercing the clouds and heavens. If you wish to plant the *pīpala* tree, you must wait for the phoenix to perch;
the seal of the Universal Radiance Mind must be held high.
Neng, the Abbot, has been sent to Jinling;

he came directly from the site of the Dharma assembly. Upon meeting, what did you have to say? To use the capable to question the incapable—how truly "skillful" it is, yet how utterly like clumsiness!
Stirring the jewels within the Vairocana-treasury, divine light shoots across ten thousand miles to the heavens. How many throughout past and present have merely toyed with their spirits?
Emerging from the weeds at times, they return once more to the weeds. The mountains and rivers of Jinling are all a former kingdom;
its heights are unclimbable, its depths unfathomable. The autumn wind blows old upon the cassia branches; beneath one’s feet, iron shoes sprout two wings.
Dezang, the Abbot of Mount Jiangshan, has come from the east of the river.
The weather is cold and the year draws to a close; why such haste? Whether held horizontally or used in reverse, it is always sufficient of itself;
from the root of his tongue, rolling thunder and wind arise. From within the treasury, he occasionally hurls the *maṇi* jewel, its five-colored radiance piercing through.
The sky is azure-green; the nostrils of the Persian from the South Sea are deep, while the face of the Śūnyatā-deva is black.

As I contemplate the Buddhas and Patriarchs, they have originally possessed nothing else; it is like a celestial city suddenly arising from the waves of a mirage. Xuanzang Sengyao did not recognize the reflection in the mirror;

this meaning often falls into neglect. Outside the gate, a startling gale sweeps up yellow leaves; the frost is white, the long embankment stretches on, and the water meets the sky. The Celestial Gate—
The axis of the earth is overturned in its entirety; Han could not reclaim it, and Qin could not contain it.
Sent to Jingci as the Abbot Xing:
"Deep within Mount Mao, we once met face-to-face. With a single squeeze, empty space was split into eight pieces; though it may be patched back together, it remains so."
Complete! Yet one cannot avoid having three heads and two faces. You speak of Chan, I speak of the Way; why do our discussions fall so perfectly into place?
The autumn wind blows the celestial fragrance of the aged cassia tree; the mountains and rivers of the great earth shine with brilliant clarity.

Do you not see? Chaling stepped until he broke the bridge over the stream; the lame donkey leaped forth, soaring into the clouds and mists. To this day, the myriad phenomena reveal their very bone and marrow.
The low remain low, the high remain high. Before the Xili Pavilion, they clasp hands once more. Having grasped the nostrils, they lose the mouth.
Laughing, they take up the pearl within the Tathāgatagarbha and scatter it toward those of this age who do not know it exists—*phuṭ*.
As the attendant Dudo is sent forth, before his eyes there is no acharya; the iron whip strikes and shatters the coral branches. Amidst the assembly there is no aged monk;
the charred-tailed dragon soars directly upon the clouds and thunder. A hundred thousand samādhis enter the palm of one’s hand—how could the true knower lie solely with Zichqi? You do not...
Behold! When the Ancient Sovereign, the Venerable Master, held up the flower, a single smile broke open his golden face.

For two thousand years, they have received the empty and taken up the resonance, shouldering the burden on their backs and racing one another in haste. The drum of Mount He is not easily struck; who dares to blow the flute of Shaolin?
Thus, the stream of Caoxi remains clear and rippling for ten thousand ages; yet when touched, its waves suddenly surge and crash.

Floods reaching the heavens and drenching the sun, with great whales and sea-monsters rampant; now, for a time, let us rejoice that the winds have settled. The profound, cold radiance soaks the reflections in the void.
A single boat rides the current as one seeks the way across; in this age of Great Peace, there is no need for the commands of generals.
Sending off Master Chushang:

At the very beginning, before the primordial chaos had yet divided, a single phrase already constitutes seeing. When the occasion arises, it is presented face-to-face: the sun’s face and the moon’s face.
A sharp and discerning monk would not even know they exist. Last night at the third watch, it was as bright as day. Where was the embroidered banner won?

At that moment, a single stroke from the pestle severed the mouth of the suspended hook. If you wish to practice Zen, you must be fiercely introspective; when you enter the path of the heterodox, you shall return to the orthodox.
On Mount Mao, deep-locked in azure clouds and cold, you will surely realize the state of cutting off the summit of Vairocana.
Next, following the rhyme of Master Juezhao’s verse on sending off his junior attendant, Zao:
The myriad realms are in turmoil, yet there is no need to dispel them; In speech or silence, examine them with equanimity.

That which lies beyond the limit of Vipaśyin is right here and now; Who does not see its manifestation in daily life? Its essence is fundamentally unborn and utterly devoid of movement; The body and mind of the rākṣasa are themselves Bodhi.
The face of the Bodhisattva. The descendants of Jibei will not necessarily [attain it]. Once the staff is taken up and the fine paid, one must leave the monastery.
To send [the teaching] like the Chan Patriarch Rulai, one drags out the nostrils and threads them from the beginning. When the wise encounter the opportune moment, they should extract it with vigor.
A missed opportunity lies right at the edge of the eyebrows. Did Lingyan lack the staff of Xinghua? Disregarding peril and ruin, one is fit to draw near.
When a practitioner personally encounters a master, their spirit grows ever more resolute through seven releases and seven captures.
With such a staff always by one's side, they are willing to share both life and death. Again, carrying the bright moon across the Double Creek, a single sheet of cold clouds.
Reflecting upon the autumn waters, I see Master Ning departing for Shanglan.

Throughout his life, Old Hu has been prolific with his verbal karma; yet, it is a joy that his descendants have no further connection to it. In this place where there is no connection, he suddenly turns over the page.
The body itself has attained but a single flower opening into five petals. Do you not see how Master Mazu’s “This very mind is Buddha” was a vast and expansive pivot?
At Xiongpeng, he rolled up his mat and displayed his heroic strategy; startling the multitudes and overcoming all adversaries, he transcended the profound and subtle.

At that moment, he pulled out the nostrils [of the patriarchs] and was utterly liberated—much like one who has returned to life from the dead. Yet he further remarked, "For three days my ears were deaf. This makes the mountain clouds laugh to their downfall.
Together with the sea moon, the practitioner enters deeply into the Tathāgatagarbha; the divine blade within the sleeve is difficult to approach.
To tear open its lair and spy upon its tracks—saying, "My words here are truly accurate"—how magnificent! To suck dry the Western River in a single gulp, even Pánggōng would not have known it.
Simply let one encounter him everywhere; what need is there to hide one's body within the Big Dipper? *Shang* (The First Part)
The Blue Dharma Seat is a marvel under heaven; it is the true forge and hammer that smelts the mundane and refines the holy. Upon entering the gate, we meet and exchange inquiries:
"How long has it been since you left the Yuanyang Lake?"
Seeing off the Venerable Wei as he returns home to visit his parents at Wanshou Huaguo:
A single pivot is employed to reveal a single realm; cut through the entanglements and you must wake up with a start. Three thousand miles away, errors are certain to arise.
Dongping shattered the mirror of Guishan; it belongs neither to the profound nor to the wondrous. Devouring and incinerating heaven and earth, it shines forth in total clarity.
The Sea God lost his "Night-Bright" curtain; Changting clapped his hands and laughed aloud. Grasping the golden drumstick upside down, he struck the golden drum;
the wooden man and the stone man danced together. The eight-armed Nala smashed the Imperial Bell; at every household door, it rings on long.
Peaceful road. This fine Buddhist hall deserves your prostrations. One who splashes foul water on others never regrets it. Outside the gate, the frosty wind cuts across the face;
on this long journey through the lands of the Hundred Yue, you should take care of yourself.
When Zhencangzhu asked Wuguan for an explanation, he replied with this verse:

"If one has awakened, there is nothing more to seek; what need is there for words? If one speaks, there is nothing more to say; one must rely on awakening. After awakening, it is just the same as before one was awakened.
Whether one speaks or not, what is there to concern oneself with? The Great Way has no gate—enter from here! The five-colored auspicious qilin has shed its skin."
Breaking free from all fetters, he shatters the jewel within the Tathāgatagarbha; even Master Sheng was startled into a fall, and the ghosts and spirits wept.

He knows nothing of what lies beyond the hermitage; like a slumbering tiger, he conceals his majesty. Having mastered the golden bell, he shakes his head and departs; under the azure sky, the bright moon spreads its autumnal radiance.
Sending Attendant Ming to visit Master Zhuyuan: If you wish to study Chan, you must attain wondrous enlightenment.
If you wish to propagate the school, you must contemplate the successive patriarchs; all the patriarchs came from wondrous enlightenment.

They upheld and established the True School throughout the ages. As for Deshan and Linji—what sort of people were they? They overturned heaven and struck the earth, following [the Way] wherever it led.
Transverse and vertical: the white staff raised high, sun and moon fall; the shout issued swiftly, thunder rolls. Sometimes the guest is complete, sometimes the host is complete;
shifting the pivot, they distinguish self from other. At the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, they let go and turn back—this is truly a cub of the golden-maned lion.
In the past, when I followed my teacher to study, I struck at empty space until it resounded with a *pò-pò*. Not only ten thousand...
The elephants laugh as they respond to one another; gathering iron, they have carelessly cast errors. This Way has been difficult to speak of in recent years;
when you meet a person of true penetration, try to discern it. The Peak of Purple Sheaths is high and the leopard’s mist is deep; take up your black staff and wield it lightly.

While escorting an attendant, he encountered a man who had attained the Way; he did not respond with either speech or silence, but instead picked up an iron caltrop, saying, "The void must be pulverized."
Thunder rolls and stars fly; with a fierce grasp, the oceans of lands in the ten directions are swept away. Letting go of the whole body, look at what happens:
one who knows how to handle a dead snake will surely bring it back to life. "O practitioner, O practitioner, do not question me; to question me is to waste your efforts in vain.
It is better to roll up your robes and return to your old cottage—who does not have servants and slaves?"
A Short Poem on the Departure of Attendant Huì: A New Song from Xīnfēng. To mend a broken string, one must use *luánjiāo* glue; Yùwáng’s words on this matter are most clear.
Why need one seek divination again toward the east or west? Rolling the iron drum and tossing the golden bell— The birds sing and flowers bloom as spring flows harmoniously.
Carrying dried wood upon my person, where shall I go? Amidst emerald cliffs and crimson crags lies the palace of the Golden Immortal. I too shall ride the wind to the east;
gazing at the clouds, I shall plant a rootless tree. Its lush branches and leaves will cover my tracks, so that even when you come, there will be no place to find me.

The staff sends out the mechanism; the mechanism seizes the mechanism, the wedge drives out the wedge. The true eye is extinguished by the blind donkey. To break through the barrier, first strike the hammer upon the crown of the head;
the hundred layers and thousand folds must burst asunder. In those days, Xinghua did not know there was anything else; amidst the field of dharma-battle, he let fall but a single [blow].
Hand. It is but ordinary for Ke-bin to be discharged from the hospital; it is enough to make the void open its smiling mouth. The auspicious qilin snaps the golden chain.
Whether in heaven or among men, who is there but I? Having scrutinized all quarters and returned once more, the bright pearl worth a carriage is reduced to a single spit.

A Parting Verse for Chan Master Xian Sent to Jinling for the Sake of the Matter of the Way of Non-Action and the Ultimate Teaching: One draws out three, and two adds four. The fierce tiger before the mountain chases the hare;
The venomous snake in the grass swallows the turtle’s nose. From the crown of the head, the eye of Mahesvara protrudes— This too is cleared away; it is not.
It is also scraped away; the partridge cries as the hundred flowers of spring come to an end. At evening, the clouds return as Zhongshan stands overturned.
The five thousand scrolls of the Dragon Treasury’s caskets—every single line is a melody from Xin’feng. The river flows on without ceasing as the land of Chu stretches wide;
who, after all, shall continue this true sound?
Seeing the attendant Ming off as he returns to his place of practice:
One is all; all is one. With total clarity, the gate of dhāraṇī is flung open; all phenomena do not intersect.
The towering peak does not reveal its summit; across a thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks, the spring day is long.
Deep in the bottom of the sea, the feet remain dry: Li Gong is drunk while Zhang Gong is sober. "I shall not betray you; you shall not betray me.
Let pass National Teacher Zhong of Nanyang; seize firmly the Broken Stove Ascetic of Songshan. Alas! No one knows it. Peach blossoms.
The willow blossoms have fallen away and drift on the wind. I wish to play my jade flute at the Yáo Pí Pond, yet I fear the phoenixes will descend and trample the branches of the wú tóng trees.
—Sent to Huá-zàng Xìng, the *Vyanāyaka*.

The nature of awareness is wondrously luminous; fundamental awareness is luminously wondrous. It dries up the waves of thirty-six thousand *qing* and reveals seventy-one or seventy-two islands of mist.

One might well laugh at old Linji, who three times asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma and three times was struck with sixty blows of the black staff—how much more ignorance and affliction did he add! Even granted that...
Upon reaching Gaoyuan Beach, he immediately realized his error; he then went against the current to probe the dragon’s jaw and pull back the tiger’s whiskers.

Judging by the facts, how does this compare to eating when one encounters food and putting on a coat when one meets the cold? Fully releasing and fully gathering, rising by oneself and falling by oneself.
This extraordinary bearing stands out from the crowd; it is precisely as it should be. As for this vast tradition of the lineage, upon whom shall it rely for succession?
Within the shadow of the golden mallet, quickly turn your head back—surely you must wonder why this mountain monk has entered the wild weeds.
I bid farewell to the attendant: all dharmas lack a real characteristic;
skillful eloquence cannot describe them. Having swept away the clouds of views and knowledge, what use is the tongue of a thunderbolt?
Vimalakīrti remained silent for three thousand years; the waters of the Yellow River flow on, reaching the heavens. Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva could not grasp it;
his praise falls short, leaving him but with earnest devotion. How can this compare to Deshan and Linji, who skillfully employed the matter?
Their staffs and shouts responded to circumstances like wind and rain. How many know this matter today? Entrust it to you, O Acharya; look into it for yourself.
Seeing Attendant Yun return to Yunmen Xialin—formerly he entered the chamber of Shao Yang. His paper robe has grown dark with age, black as lacquer;

I have not uttered a single word until now, so as to spare later generations from debating gain and loss. Do you not see? Upon the Ruoshui River, clouds pile up like thousands of mounds—a single point...
Unattached to the dust of the human world, what is there in these towering transformations? Silver palaces and golden terraces—cool winds blow from the west, sweeping over you with urgency.
Shatter the dark barrier and seek the path within; the tides of the Zhejiang River rise like mountains.
When crossing water, do not let your two feet get wet.

[This was written] by Song Dàchéng Jué, the Head Seat, upon his second visit to Master Sōngyue, to recognize one's own original mind and see one's own original nature. Whether light comes or darkness comes, the head is upright and the tail is upright. Great Vehicle Bodhisattva.

Faith is beyond doubt; how could a petty-rooted son of Māra ever know it? He holds a hundred suns and moons aloft in his palms, and from the tip of a single hair, a thousand Mount Sumerus surge forth.
Do you not see? The stream of Caoxi is no stagnant pool; were even a single drop not to flow, waves would arise.
This speech from Nanyue (Ruyi) is by no means ordinary; it truly matches his father’s three-inch beak. The Head Seat has his own strengths.
This is why I have come here. Rubbing my two eyes against the western wind, the white clouds have all rolled away and the sky is free of taint.
With composure, he drew near and spoke to me: "I seek a long verse as a compass for my further study.
Suddenly, from the top of a tree, he pushed down a fragrant cluster of golden grain, its filaments trailing down. Clapping his hands with a laugh, he said, "You surely know this."
The *Song* (Verses) for the First Attendant Yangshan:
The initial pivot and the final realization. Zhaozhou’s stone bridge is no mere footbridge; at the tip of the staff, the true eye opens.
This profound realm and sacred domain require no locks or keys. Do you not see how Yangshan releases the light from his four gates, illuminating heaven and earth?

How resplendent is the earth! The Yellow River flows clear, piercing through the azure sea; Mount Hua rises abruptly, brushing against the heavens. The Southern Dipper is in the west, the Northern Dipper is in the east;
by the side of the cliff, empty space gives birth to flowers layer upon layer. Though the young jade maiden calls out repeatedly with intent, the lover recognizes that she leaves no trace at all.
Cease all thought and do not attempt to deliberate; the wrathful Nātha holds aloft his iron pillar, sitting and cutting off all paths.
At the Eighteen Rapids of Jiangxi, dense clouds spread across the cool, shady trees.
As I see off the Venerable Ang for Jiang and Xiang, I open the window only to dread the bitter cold;
I close the door, hindered from gazing at the snow. Sitting cross-legged, ten thousand anxieties fall silent; my single nature naturally transcends them.
A man of the Way comes treading through the snow to knock at my door; his skeletal vigor is like iron and stone, his spirit as cold as ice and frost.
He laughs at me for covering my head with heavy paper quilts; his gentle words bring the warmth of spring. Tomorrow he will tread the snow away toward Jiangdong;
by nature he possesses the equipment for such a journey. From the nine rivers he shall gaze upon Mount Lu; returning to the mountain peak, he shall look back at the river waters. The lake of Poyang—
A solitary corner of heaven; the exquisite beauty of Lake Dongting floats over Mount Heng. When the white clouds have flown away, the sun is cool and desolate.
A few drops of foam fall into the mirror-like water. In my life, have I not had the aspiration for rivers and seas? Yet, being old, there is no way to pursue them.
With my mind darkly fixed beyond all things, I wander only in spirit. At such a fine place, I merely nod my head and understand it within myself. Do you not see? Ke-bin did not enter this—

Baoshan: Thoroughly able to support the aged and promote transformation; twenty times the black staff drove him out of the mountains, yet the fragrance of his steamed rice fills all under heaven. —In Commemoration of Chan Master Qi Assistant: Baoshan: Thoroughly able to support the aged and promote transformation; twenty times the black staff drove him out of the mountains, yet the fragrance of his steamed rice fills all under heaven.
—In Commemoration of Chan Master Qi
One saying is overturned by another; the Yellow River is silent and the ocean waters run dry. The three thousandfold world-system is level and smooth;
the profound path of the eighty thousand Dharma gates is cut off. The intent of the Patriarchs and the Chan of the Tathāgata—take it from either side, and you encounter its source.
Right now, sitting and cutting off the pinnacle of the thousand sages—what need is there to manifest the Real and reopen the Provisional? Sometimes fully gathering in, sometimes fully letting go;
whether moving against or with the flow, transverse or vertical, one cannot come near. Upon the flames of a red furnace, ice flowers form; atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak, snow waves overturn.
Song cannot reach its end, laughter cannot reach its end; the shrimp and frog at the bottom of the sea swallow the moon. The enraged Nalakūvara strikes the Emperor of Heaven.
The Bell: "A piece of cast iron added to the back of a vajra.
Sent to attendant Peng to return to Yunmen:
"Peng uses a good friend; Yong uses a beneficial friend. Beneficial friends and good companions are difficult to find. How high is that above? Why do you not climb it?"
How deep below is it that you do not immediately reach? To climb and to reach—high and deep. Above and below—ancient and present.
One by one, investigate thoroughly from the very beginning; then come and listen to my stringless lute. The stringless lute possesses its own musical laws:
the Yangyang River flows on, the mountains rise steeply. Pang Gong and Ma Gong—their bones have long since rotted away, yet the ears of the vulgar still desire to hear them.
My ears do not penetrate; Yunmen has long been a cave of mountains and waters. Its people possess the fine features of snow-boned and ice-tempered character.

Ten thousand valleys and a thousand crags dwell within my dreams; with cloth socks and green shoes, I wander aimlessly through them. The spring wind blows vast and free over the clear waves; for your sake, I shall sing one song of Yunmen.
Tomorrow, when you see your old friends at Yunmen, they will surely laugh at me for having become so dilatory.
Master Qi requests a *jingce* (exhortation):
"You wish to practice Chan and seek an exhortation; I am currently forgetting words to savor the flavor of true bliss. True bliss is boundless and known only by oneself;
the many methods of exhortation await your study. Empty yet spiritual, silent yet wondrous—ten thousand doors and a thousand gates are all [open]."
A single illumination. Aside from the *dhūta* practitioner who understands the laughing flower, who is it that treads upon the aperture that penetrates heaven?

The felt clappers and the holeless flute—how clearly manifest are the "White Snow" and "Yangchun" melodies! If one hears them truly at the tips of the hundred grasses, what limit can there be to this wind one carries down?

I present to the Secretary of the Assembly this single phrase from the summit of Yunju Mountain: "At the head of Dulong Ridge, it is not like anything else. Turning the body, one treads upon Lingxiao Peak;
from the bottom of the well, dust and mist rise to touch the heavens. A thousand seven hundred elephants and dragons are startled into collapse; with ease, the coiled serpent is shattered.
Peach kernels. In the texts and writings outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles, not a single character has ever been inscribed with a stroke.
Jiyin is muddled; Qianzi is a fool. He cooks riceless porridge to satisfy his morning hunger. His body is like a coconut, yet his gallbladder is as large as a bushel.
Opening his mouth, he wishes to swallow Mount Sumeru. As for me, I hide like a tortoise in the ancient hills and ravines; from where does this knocking at the door come? Raising my eyebrows...
Closing one's eyes to test the wind that has come—it is truly believed that the Cinnabar Mountains abound with phoenixes. The Yellow River’s nine bends must surely have already cleared;
at the Aru Pavilion in Qiyang, they sing as they please. The grand music of the Heavenly Court is precisely what should be heard; what use are the sounds of zithers and flutes for these two ears?
Seeing off Chan Master Chuzang as he returns from Zhongshan to Tiantai to visit his parents:
"The Hundred-Foot Wild Fox. I myself do not understand it. A single phrase cuts off the flow; for a thousand ages there has been no match.
Cast away the delusions before the skull; where birds sing and flowers bloom upon a thousand peaks, who is it that holds heaven and earth in check? A fierce flame extends...
Heavenly white waves fly; what has the Vulture Peak and Jetavana to say? Let us test and distinguish the Sanskrit from the Tang language:
the old barbarian’s flat teeth lack the vital breath of the Dharma. For nine years at Shaolin, he leaked the secret; yet how can he compare to the mad Baozhi of Jinling?
With his staff, he still possesses a field of leisure; before people, he tears open the golden face-skin. Thus, he was able to realize the meaning of the Westward Journey.
In the long forest, fallen leaves swirl as the west wind blows fiercely. With a single song of high melody, where can one find solace? One’s white-haired parents lean against the gate in longing;
do not say that traveling to study under masters yields nothing. *Du!* (A shout of realization)

Master Zhizang of the Dharma-eye treasury shatters the sand-bowl; the golden sun beats its wings as dawn breaks over Fusang. To mend a broken string with animal glue—is this a trivial matter? Only one whose breast can swallow heaven and earth may undertake it.

Have you not seen how Master Zeng’s backbone is as hard as iron? Upon the Snowy Mountain of the Tortoise, *Note: The final line "Aoshan Xue" (鼇山雪) likely refers to a specific verse or title associated with the master's realization, though the full context is incomplete.*
Deeply frozen and on the verge of breaking—were it not for Yantou exerting all his strength to support him, how could such radiance fill the vast void?
Furthermore, do you not see how Gautama abandoned the station of the Golden Wheel-turning King and soared off to the Snowy Mountains at midnight?

For six years he refined his practice in the forest of myriad deeds, and in a single day he brought the Bodhi tree to a standstill. A true man of great character ought to be thus; how cramped and confined is the cage of the common world!
They are not comparable. When the golden bell is struck atop the five Sumeru peaks, how can the bright moon and clear wind be compared?

Sending forth Attendant Ming to see Elder Songyue, at that moment when light and dark are paired together, this mountain monk has a mouth but finds it difficult to explain. The attendant personally ascended Mount Emei.
Come! It is like asking about the pine-moon at Songjiang: the bright moon shines directly upon the pines by the river; when the white clouds have all dispersed, one merely devours the void.
When not a single mechanism is borrowed, the myriad phenomena are extinguished; with empty hands, one can personally achieve complete mastery.
The tradition of the Jibei school is truly like this; it is surely not unlike that of Jiangxi. One must trample to death the celestial horse-foal before one may be called a man.
In the preceding discourse on guest and host: Deep is the autumn air of Jiangnan and the two Zhe regions; the great river rolls on and the mountains loom heavy.
One melody, two melodies of the stringless lute—Heaven grows old, Earth grows old; who knows this music?
Seeing off Attendant Qi as he first retires from Shoushan Monastery. The attendant speaks of his travels: "I struck my toe, and a clear breeze stirred across the vast void.
At Tiantai and Yanwang, the springtime is deep; a hundred flowers vie for beauty beneath the shade of spring clouds. A single glance at Jian Lake reveals eight hundred [miles of] scenery."

Li He, old man, you do not compose; who knows your music? The six temples of Yunmen may be depicted in painting, but the years since the Cave of Yu have been so long that the weeds must surely choke it.
This old man has feet but cannot walk; he is thus guilty of defaulting on his debt for straw sandals in the Eastern Province.
The Abbot Che delivers a statement from beginning to end that the entire Great Canon cannot encompass. Mañjuśrī exhausts his eloquence yet forgets words;
Vimalakīrti blocks his speech—how could he truly remain silent? Do you not see? The Gandharva King performs celestial music, and the great earth...
The mountains and rivers all responded in unison. Kāśyapa was skilled at dancing but not at listening. From amidst the grass emerged the horn of the auspicious qilin.
The man from Fusang is truly magnificent; coming ten thousand *li* from the east, he has revealed the profound mysteries. Like an elephant king treading the earth, he stirs up a heroic wind.
The lion’s roar and stretch are beyond all fear; now that I am old, I shall retire to leisure. Let this man of the Way return for now to his home mountain.
When the crimson sun bathes the vast blue ocean in the night of the coming day, I know you will stand upon the mast, smiling with understanding.
To the Abbot Jue of Tiantong:
What thing are the Buddhas of the three periods? What words are the entire Great Canon? Directly pointing and single transmission reveal the orthodox lineage;
the radiant flowers of awakening bloom upon the tip of the pestle. Since the sages of antiquity could not recognize them, how could those of middling or inferior capacity?

It can be fathomed: the eyes of the *Cakṣu-māheśvara* demon are as pitch-black as the mountains, rivers, and earth. Within that blackness, a white light shines radiantly; striking the void produces sound to dispel ignorance.
This is the meaning of the true nature pointed out by an empty fist—its concealment and manifestation, its appearance and disappearance, transcend the profound and subtle.
To explain one way and then to explain it another in opposition: how many people throughout past and present have been able to discern this? It is all in great confusion.
Falling into shadows and glimmers, much like a macaque reaching for the moon in the water. How marvelous is the author from whence he comes;
