he wanders through the ancient temple by the riverside village. Raising the vajra mallet to shatter the old molds, he employs the "black bean" method to drive forth the gifted.
When opening both hands, there is a smile; illumination within function, and function within illumination. The North Star concealing its body—how could this be accidental?
Rain falling on the Southern Mountain is in harmony with the same tune. Tomorrow we shall part and return to the pines of Lu; the iron boat has been forged, yet it is done in haste.
Calling across the mountain, they understand the resonance; take it for granted that the command of Makara will be executed in reverse.
I bid farewell to Zen practitioner Hui as he pays homage to the Patriarchs.
Smash the skull! Lift off the cranial cap! The "four sevens and two threes"—lumps of clay and clods of earth—are found by raking through a heap of green grass.
Mirroring the earth and illuminating the heavens, the light flashes and glows. Beneath the knees of a man of great capacity lies gold; grasp the essential principle right here.
How very mistaken is your chest! Mistaken or not? Exercise good judgment. The Great Statue of Jiazhou turns its body over;
the Iron Ox of Shanfu breaks its horns.
A verse in the same rhyme presented to Attendant Xin.
The National Teacher called out three times; he lost his money and incurred punishment. The attendant responded three times; he mistook a thief for his own son.
What is the use of saying, "His teeth are like sword-trees and his mouth is like a blood-basin"? When scrutinized, these are all merely matters of necessity.

If one casually passes beyond the ultimate barrier, one naturally no longer stands upon level ground. As for spitting at me, let it be—forgive you for splashing water. As for reviling me, let it be—forgive you.
You take up the point. If you understand, then let it go entirely and gather it back entirely; if you do not understand, then you will fall down by yourself and rise up by yourself.

To clarify the mind through form, to manifest principle through phenomena, to sift through fire to seek bubbles, and to strike at emptiness to extract the marrow—having brought all this forth with full sincerity for you to see:
even so, if you recognize it, it is still not it. You must personally learn how to ride a bull backward; who am I to govern you?

To the Abbot Huan, I present the Eight Auspicious Symbols, the Six Supreme Merits, and the entirety of the Great Canon—head upright and tail upright. The old barbarian’s tongue was once long, yet now it is short;
he has exhausted his preaching of the partial and the perfect, the half and the full. To pick it up is indeed good for wiping away sores and scars, but to let it go, how could one ever ascend?
The other shore. Dongshan spoke of "Pralāṇa"; with bowl and tray in hand, who can take it up? A master hand has never had a rival since ancient times.
To catch a thief, one must first seize the stolen goods. The mani-jewel shines with brilliant light; Yongjia’s acquisition of it is truly worthy of praise.
He scattered it before people, yet none knew it; how many pebbles are there to be picked up in the spring pond?
Sending Master Cóng to pay his respects at the residence of Scholar Jìnqīng to request a stupa inscription for Venerable Zhūyuán;
the Elder Huíguīn reveals True Quiescence. The grasses, trees, and groves all lose their luster; the eyes remain unimpaired and the teeth are preserved.

After the fire, the stalks of reed sweep away the azure void. Throughout his life, his preaching was like spring thunder, startling the hibernating dwellings and dispelling the delusions of the world.
The clouds part. His lofty character and brilliant integrity stir the wavering and the weak. He was haughty toward the world and severed from the mundane, leaving behind the dust of worldly affairs.

Five years have passed since the Master who followed him retired; seventeen years have elapsed since the Master who preceded him entered extinction. The monastic communities have not yet deeply lamented their desolation, for it was still hoped that the Master remained in the southeast.
Now that the Master has departed, what can be done? The mountains crumble, the seas dry up, and the rivers are without waves. The patch-robed disciples...
They beat their breasts, competing in bitter wailing; tears fell like rain, incessantly forming a river in the void. Do you not see?

That final chapter from the end of Master Zhantang’s life—its brilliant radiance remains inscribed in the annals of the monastic history. Jinjing is none other than the present-day Master Wujin; who would know that he was not Miaoxi himself?
With Mount Sumeru as his brush and the heavens as his monument, he has recorded it in great characters, repeatedly inscribed—not just once. Nanquan has passed on.
Transforming the correct, not the evil: the neighbor to the east makes a horse, the neighbor to the west a donkey.
Having seen the written record sent, he returned to Mount Xiang;
once they had met, incense was burned and tea exchanged, yet not a single word was uttered. Both were masters of the craft; without cause, he raised it up.
A brush of five colors drenches half the void; it casts forth the Perfect Circle of Yangshan. Like lightning flashing and stars racing, the waters of the sea stand still.
Yet I rejoice that this old monk’s heart-eye is upright; the iron wheel spins upon my crown, yet my breath remains composed.
Sitting, I watch as the black winds from beyond the heavens subside; I perceive only the placid lake, pure as a mirror. Leisurely, he points toward the mountains beyond the lake—how wondrous!
In conversation, they clapped their hands and opened joyful smiles; with a sweep of the sleeves, they returned to Jiyun. A single arrow straightaway shattered a thousandfold barriers.

Sending off Attendant Cao back to his place of practice: when he acts, he exists; when he desists, he perishes. Within the gate of the patch-robed monks, there is no need for deliberation; whether thoughts arise or thoughts cease, it is none other than [the Way].
Liberation: every lifting of the foot and every placing of the foot is the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). At the tip of the staff, heaven and earth are vast and open;
within the alms-bag, sun and moon reflect each other’s light. Those who go forth are like sons fleeing from their fathers; those who return are like long-traveling guests coming home.

Fully transcending the *dharmakāya*, *saṃbhogakāya*, and *nirmāṇakāya*, they cut off the path of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvara. Leveling the high and conforming to the low, they shake the collar and lift the main rope, looking left and right.
Ah! Like dragons ascending and mists gathering, they form a screen before and a throng behind;
like tigers roaring and winds arising, it follows the rhyme of my elder brother Zhongmou as a gift to the Venerable Huan.
It is not that we are similar, but rather that we are not different. North and south meet together; above and below penetrate one another. Suddenly, a single phrase strikes the mark.

The pivot of opportunity: when the mouth opens, it is no concern of the tongue. A dragon of the Buddha-ocean, a moon of the monastic forest, traversing the Five Peaks and Three Xiangs, spanning the Seven Min and Two Zhe—riding upon sound and covering over form, he flaunts his elegance;
yet while he stirs up the dust and scatters the soil, how could there remain any lingering fragrance?

Biting through the arrowhead, breaking through the barrier; cutting through the nail, severing the iron. Examine it from beginning to end—how is it? He has pulled out the donkey-peg that has been tied there for many years.
[The Master] sent Attendant Yuan back to Jiangxin.
To seek the current from its source; when the leaves fall, one knows autumn has come. The lacquer bucket is not yet satisfied; riding an ox while searching for the ox.

To trace the current back to its source; washing one's feet and then boarding the boat. The Peng bird of the vast ocean with its ninety thousand *li*; the crane of Liaodong with its three thousand years. For this old monk, there is no basis for reliance upon the corners of his mouth.
Let me ask those who understand: is it so? If so, the mountains encircle the Nine-Dipper City; if not, the river embraces Longxiang Temple.

Shake your mendicant’s staff and travel to all quarters; you must decide for yourself. Whether it be my burden or yours, let us both cease our talk. Steel tempered a hundred times may become as supple as a finger;
how does that compare to a single flake of snow upon a red furnace?
Sending off Attendant Yu to visit Master Sheng:
the roots and tips of the *xiancai* greens harbor the vitality of life. Carrying away the broken-legged cauldron, he travels afar without traversing any path;
at ease, who knows he possesses such abundance? Call and response are the same from ancient times to the present; with a single push of the hand, it must be overturned.
On Mount Mì, amidst the vast oceans of lands within a single pore, you can restore our school with a mere smile.

Your superior endowment and robust capacity are like a vessel passed down through water; though Śākyamuni Buddha did not receive a prediction from Dīpaṃkara, we shall meet again where all traces have vanished.
How could the myriad dharmas ever serve as companions?

I present to Master Ming the phrase for turning back atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff: A golden-maned lion is naturally beyond compare; with a single gulp, the Western River is dried to its very bottom.
Master Ma shrank his head, and Pang Gong was struck with awe; suddenly, the waves surge across level ground, drenching and rotting the nostrils—what can be done?
At that moment, the heavens were clear and the void laughed; ten thousand phenomena danced. Beneath the sandalwood leaves, the fragrance wafted far and wide.

Having cast aside Dongshan’s three blows of the staff, his chilling heroic wind—who could dare approach it? Whether traveling north or south, none knew its way; on Xiao Island, the waters have receded and the traces of the sands swell.
I see the auspicious clouds parting as he returns east to Jixian; the sun rises over the sea to the east.
From the heavens to the south and from the earth to the north, the light is radiant and clear. The six dragons fly side by side as the Yellow Path aligns;
even the secluded crags and deep valleys are filled with the spring breeze. At Shaolin, the one flower has blossomed into five petals; the land of India and China have both faded away.
Negotiation. Where there is no negotiation, suddenly all is harmonized; whether saint or ordinary person, all are filled with joy.

That which the entire Tripitaka cannot express, is revealed through the equal sharing of half a seat as perfect illumination. Of the thirty-six thousand acres of Lake Tai, who would not know that the moon is in the heart of the waves?
Who would not know? In a sandalwood grove, sandalwood trees surround one another.
Following the rhyme of Master Songyue: Sending off Secretary Xu of Yuwang— The hand that wields the adze receives the wood to be shaped.
Two wonders meet, their eyes both azure; With an iron whip, the dragon of Letan is roused.
The pearl of the black dragon scatters from the chamber of Ciming. A clap of thunder flies up to heaven; The Three Barriers are grandly opened.
He said nothing. To pluck the tiger’s whiskers is a matter within one’s own domain. Not only was Ji Bei able to act with such wild abandon;
his every cough and spittle fell like pearls and jade as they drifted on the wind. He simply took heaven as his dwelling. The waves of Caoxi surged high, lapping at the heavens;
Tian Rui’s fragrant legacy expanded the orthodox succession.
To Master Zecang on his Ten-Thousand-Year Birthday:
What does the "Teaching for an Era" clarify? Ten men, five pairs—deaf and mute. There is a true monk within Mount Laṅkā;
he can speak without moving his tongue. The first phrase is not in the East; it is the morning sunlight upon the land of Fusang.
Dawn breaks. The final word does not lie in the West; the jade tower strikes the twilight bell. The *campaka* flowers spray their fragrance as the sacrificial grass turns verdant;
ten thousand realms are suddenly empty and still. The great leviathan grinds the coral groves to pieces; the white moon and clear wind are all too disarrayed.

He saw off the Head Seat Hao as he returned east to the Manlu Hall, where he personally received the essential instructions. He swept away the three turning words of Xiuju; neither the Great Canon nor the Minor Canon remained.
He casually cut off Nanquan’s station; driving the plow and seizing the food—how dignified! Striking east and striking west, he opened [the way].

Blind and deaf, yet with every step one transcends beyond the kalpas of emptiness; in the end, one never departs from the midst of the ordinary. When inspiration strikes, one sings the tune of returning home;
its melody enters the "Yangchun" mode—whom can it be entrusted to continue? With the autumn wind blowing right through the Nine Heavens, a single sail hangs aloft;
the distant waters truly become the green of a duck’s head.
Next, my Dharma brother Zhongmou sent this verse on the rhyme of Chan Master Chezang:

"The Three Vehicles are beyond the teachings; the transmission of the Dharma and the vestment were entrusted. How great is the sagely plan! Who can truly resemble it? It is like trying to fit a round peg into a square hole."
All say this is suspicious. To let the spirit roam in transcendent realms and attain wondrous realization without a teacher—lightning is not swift enough, and a spark from flint is still too slow.

To shatter one's body and crush one's bones, dispersing marrow and skin; to distinguish the melody by the movement of the strings—this is the realm of Boya and Ziqi. Such are the virtues of *śīla*, *samādhi*, and *prajñā*.

That greed, hatred, and delusion cause one to be confused about what has been awakened to, and to awaken to what was previously confused. When the myriad functions have ceased, there is the non-action of the single essence.
With my eye of wisdom, I observe your arrangements; though my words may be harsh to your ears, my heart does not deceive you. I shall sweep away the four propositions.
Sweeping away all hundredfold errors, letting go with hands cast off from the precipice—this is the moment of arriving home. Drinking water quenches thirst; eating rice relieves hunger.

If one simply understands this much, what need is there to ask about anything else? I prostrate to the Compassionate Honored One, the Great Physician of the Three Realms, who speaks both directly and indirectly.
The principle is as it is, and the phenomenon is as it is. I composed this verse:
"A eunuch plants a beard;
he sends the guest Yongzhi the pine tree in front of the courtyard. Zhaozhou did not say these words; they strike the old Qingliang and miss Jue Tiezui.

A bystander’s smile is truly startling: Mount Taihua splits asunder and the Yellow River collapses. In the snap of a finger, eighty-four thousand years pass; beneath the sun, there is no need for a solitary lamp.
In the end, though the path is the same, the tracks differ. When a guest arrives, offer tea; cherish this moment of rest.
The bright pearl of Hepu shoots toward the Dipper and Ox constellations; the venomous snake of the South Mountain has a nose like a turtle.
Sending off the Abbot Yong: Banyan leaves fill the courtyard as orioles sing in confusion. The entire Great Canon opens like a golden lancet. Upon the peak of Mount Sumeru, sun and moon blaze forth;

Within the ocean of three thousand lands, there is no dust or mire. Whether moving against or with, whether horizontal or vertical—all are samādhi. One cannot squeeze them into a ball, nor can one strike them down.
It is not shattered. For seven days, Sudhana vainly pursued it; for a hundred kalpas, Mañjuśrī has never met with it. At the heart of the Yangtze River, the night tide falls;

the gnarled, withered willow rests against the dragon’s horn. As concentration returns, the iron chimes of the golden hall ring out; with eyes fixed on the distance, one watches a solitary wild goose cross the vast void.

As I see off Attendant Jin to Mount Lu, I observe that on both the southern and northern slopes of the mountain, the fragrant breeze of white lotuses fills the air daily. Clear snow blankets the sky as cascading waterfalls spray forth;
the waters of the Nine Rivers appear as a deep lapis lazuli blue. The practitioner’s breast swallows these nine rivers, his very bone and spirit rising straight to meet the mountain itself.

Rising and falling, I tread upon the path where Master Huiyuan once walked; morning bells and evening drums strike one another in resonance. A jade torrent leaps like a dragon, flashing rock-lightning;
gazing long, my two eyes grow dizzy with the sight. Frost-covered monkeys howl until silence at the highest peak; turning my head, I see but a solitary cloud, the heavens and sea stretching far away.
Lu Zicai of Huating transcribed three sets of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. Shan-zhu Yugang composed a verse in praise of them.
Ten individuals, including Bao-lin Bie-feng Zhong-kuan and Lord Pan, all composed verses in response.
Yugang requested that I follow his rhyme scheme.
Nine peaks amidst the clouds stand like upright brushes, piercing the void yet forming nothing. Radiantly, the brilliant patterns of celestial verses unfold;

they originally emerge from within the Vairocana-treasury. This treasury of Vairocana transcends both annihilation and permanence: the bright sun flies with clear frost. The Wondrous High Mountain rises steep and towering;
the hundred cities assist its growth—how vast and expansive! Yet the stains of the mind have not been removed.
One must wash; how can one realize the True Principle without washing? When principle is severed and emotion forgotten, even "True" does not exist.

The white ox and the cat share the same essence; both the school (Zong) and the teaching (Shuo) are penetrating. The eye atop the head has three pupils suspended; it is the inexhaustible contemplation of the Dharma-realm in its many layers.
Vivid and unclouded are emptiness, the provisional, and the middle. Butter, curd, and clarified butter are most supreme. Treasure.
The forest trees are exceptionally lush and elegant; on this day, we meet again at the distant peaks. Grasping hands, a single smile—surely we shall find harmony.
Taking Zen as our delight and the Dharma as our joy, are Lu and Pan not also sons of the Azure Isle? Before the Hall of Abiding in Goodness, they expound the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*;
from the root of their tongues, the four great rivers surge forth in waves.
I send this to the scholar Tianping Zhan to pay homage to Mount Yan on behalf of his teacher, Fozhi, for the inscription of his memorial stele:

A single grain of millet was brought by a golden rooster; From the rock, twin pieces of jade burst forth. From this point, the school’s tradition was propagated throughout Jiangxi, Turning the pivot of heaven and the axis of earth.
The entire mechanism remained hidden from view—only the father knew it; When the wild sheep hang their horns, where can they be sought?
A trace remains. After his entry into *nirvāṇa*, there were marks of a great man; his radiance pierced through the boundless void.

With a wrist possessing the strength of a thousand *qūn*—the Imperial Academy Scholar Quizhang—the tip of his brush brought forth the adamantine eye. If one were to use the sun and moon themselves as a celestial stele, what limit would there be to opening the way for humans and devas?
Summer after summer, autumn after autumn, he hoisted his sails and sailed westward as the wind whistled; the mountains stretched on and on.
The waters flow on endlessly; the springtime radiance is entirely within the land of plum blossoms.
I bid farewell to the Head Seat Rou (whose style name is Kechung and who inscribed his quarters as "The Chamber of Floating Flowers") with these four lines:
Transcending all that is beyond conceptualization, he preaches with blazing intensity within the Tuṣita Palace; the eighty thousand afflictions are swept away into emptiness.
A bright moon hangs beneath the coral tree; within the practitioner’s breast lie hills and valleys. Within the practitioner’s breast lie heaven and earth.
The Patriarchal meaning is luminous at the tips of the hundred grasses; the full tide rolls surging amidst the foam-flowers.
After seven years of separation, we meet once more. Azure eyes pierce the sun like polished bronze. Sweeping clean the pine hall, he conceals the yellow scrolls. The misty waves of Lake Dongting.
Shaking the clear sky. Zhaozhou’s tea, Yunmen’s cake—when meeting face-to-face, you must grasp it with total intensity. Turning back, you topple the石门 (Shimen) barrier;
there is no hindrance to reaching the summit of the 琴台 (Qintai) peak yourself.
The attendant Yi was being sent to Heshan;
as for the master’s name, Yi did not know it. Yi then asked: "A single phrase cuts off the stream; all capacities naturally collapse. Upon the tips of the hundred grasses—"
I recommend this old monk; let us take another blow of the sixty-year-old broomstick. When the patriarchs and ancestors could not settle it, the calamity reached their descendants.
Like a hawk seizing a pigeon—only then can one engage in true discourse. The Wondrous Peak soars steeply, its azure form beyond the heavens;
the small stream flows with a clear, chime-like sound. Receive these eighty-four thousand verses; when you return, bring them forth and let me hear them.
Sending off Head Seat Xuan to Taiyuan and Yanyue (by Miaoyan):

A man of the Way came from Jinling; his spirit and resolve swallowed the Buddhas and patriarchs. He burned incense while sitting through the long night, and in his comings and goings, he discoursed on the present and the past.
A sword hangs from between his brows, encompassing both life and death; in his hands and face lies the mechanism for bestowing and taking away.

He turns his robe inside out and dances the *zhèzhī*; like lightning and sparks from flint, he sweeps across all things. How lofty are Mount Tai and Mount Yan! Setting sail, he crosses the tide of the Qiantang River.
The spring breeze surges through the eight directions; upon the rock, it is precisely the right time to carve a gourd-bowl.
Sengzi Shouzuo has returned from paying homage at the Fuxing Pagoda to Jiaxin;
if you wish to recognize the marks of a great man who dwells in cessation, the stench of excrement pervades the heavens and is difficult to approach.

If you claim that lotuses bloom in the twelfth month, it is truly like a tortoise’s hair growing several zhang long. The Fengtai Terrace stands towering through spring and autumn; the Three Mountains stand overturned and tall.
The river flows on; atop the lapis lazuli palace, there is no one to recognize me. How vast and distant are the southern reaches of Xiang and the northern shores of Tan!

A hundred negations and four lines are all swept away at once. The moonlight over the central stream connects to the island of Penglai. Master Xie remains right there upon his fishing boat, while the yellow dust of the world buries the roads of Chang’an.
Seeing Attendant Sheng depart to travel through Jiangxi:
Day after day the sun rises in the east; day after day the sun sets in the west. A single point on Mount Jun, autumn over Lake Dongting;

a thousand peaks of Mount Heng leaning against the vast void. Master Yuan’s breast swallows the Nine Rivers; he holds aloft the Primordial Age to gaze upon the great cosmos. With his own hand, he pulls—

Cascading waters wash my straw sandals; in visionary sight, honor and disgrace are like withered stumps. The flowers of the White Lotus Pond from days of yore now appear and vanish upon the Golden Terrace amidst rosy clouds.
A single song of vast resonance resounds through a thousand years; the celestial wind blows wildly, tossing my *kāṣāya*.

The Dharma of the late Head Seat Kang of Lingyin: There is a phrase that points directly upward. One may deliberate on it at will, yet find no place to grasp it; suddenly, it bursts forth from the very lips.
The myriad phenomena stand with brows raised high; whether walking east or west, heaven and earth are vast. Turning left or turning right, it is like a luminous pearl.
Running on the platter: the golden mallet brandishes the void as sun and moon fall; the precious sword emerges from its scabbard as waves and tides surge.

A golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net leaps once more over the billows; a stone horse turns back on its path as steeds vie to face one another. Grasping hands before the great kalpa of *vibhāṣā*, bright casting meets dark harmony—observe the striking and the chanting.
The song of Mount Dong is a boat sailing downstream; the wondrous is not itself wondrous, the profound is not itself profound. Seize it!
Sealing off the mouths of the monks; piercing the mark with absolute victory, surpassing even Nārāyaṇa. Proceeding thus atop the First Peak, the eight-armed Nātha cannot detain him.
Having scrutinized and penetrated all quarters, he returns once more; there is a distinct pure breeze that stirs the entire universe.
In the same rhyme, I send off Master Zhang of Yangshan:
"Not so, not so! Thus, thus! The Way is clearly distinguished; it is thirty *li* further than before. The golden crow pecks through the lapis lazuli shell;
the Śūnyatā-deva suddenly gives rise to malice. Right before one's eyes, he topples Mount Cakravāṇa; the darkness of kalpas is dispelled.

The crossroads are suddenly illuminated and vast; the discourse exhausts the mountain clouds and the sea moon. Sweeping across the Yangtze and Xiang rivers, as well as Fujian and Zhejiang, everyone vies to boast that the crimson steed can chase the wind.
Who would have believed that a mantis could block the tracks? Having shattered the views of annihilation and permanence, one speaks of true emptiness.
When the two extremes do not stand, how can a middle be left? Taking south for north and west for east, with a thunderous shout and a stinging blow, one drives forth the thunder and wind.

In response to the rhyme, I present this verse for the attendant Xi, who has attained realization. You have spoken well. This matter knows neither young nor old; if one does not clarify it for oneself, whom else would one seek to deceive?

As soon as one speaks of "benefiting others," one has already fallen into the weeds. To grasp the tiger’s tail and crouch upon its head—do not boast of overturning mountains and toppling valleys. Lift it up!
In the future, there shall be no way to let this pass lightly. One who encounters it is an enemy with whom one cannot share the same sky.

To the robe of patience and the chamber of compassion—here, all must be settled with a single stroke. Turning over suddenly upon the level fields and shallow grass, before the Buddha’s hand can be extended, the donkey’s hoof has already emerged.
Within the field of perfect enlightenment and the seat of Mount Sumeru, how many are able to hold fast heaven and earth? Only...
The attendant should understand the practice of Zen; only then will he believe that the patriarchs’ household affairs are vast.
As for sending off the Librarian Jing back to Yongjia:
one path is direct, while the other two are circuitous. Whether it be the Great Canon or the Small Canon, they are but water-moons and empty flowers. Yongjia vainly boasts of his "one-night stay."

Awakening! Circling the bed, he shook his staff with a rattling sound. The Old Teacher of Shaoyang turned it upside down with a single word; face-to-face, how could one avoid scattering dust and sand?
To take the narrow for the broad is to deceive the Hu and mock the Han; to compare the long with the short is to throw one's hair-knot into the yamen.
Laying it all out with full sincerity, there is yet another way of life: pulling the six giant turtles, the three islands turn; the straight hook’s purpose is certainly not for fish or shrimp.
Sōshi Zōshu departs northward to visit his teacher; from Nan-san and Hokusan he comes down from Ryūshō Peak.
His eyes shine with piercing brilliance, emptying the entire universe; he overturns the ocean-like world-system of Huazang.

His every movement does not fall within the realm of words or thought. Like lightning turning and stars flying, observe his martial prowess; in the field of Dharma-battle, his very liver [is revealed].
Bold and exposed; with a roar and a cry, he falls into the tiger’s trap. Reversing the halberd and casting off the armor—countless as the sands of the Ganges.
The ancient iron bowl transmitted by the Western Patriarch—who says that after so many years it lacks a handle? To break it into pieces and strike it in fragments is not worth mentioning;
across ten thousand miles, one must sweep it away. This Master is a guest upon the Golden Terrace; crane-like countenance and cloud-like bearing, truly a fine style. The Five Ranks.
The ranks of sovereign and minister stand in their respective positions of orthodoxy and partiality; the three mysteries (*sanxuan*) transcend and clarify both essence and function.

In the past, I first struck the drum of lethal poison; now, trailing my staff, I seek the path beneath the crags. Spreading my wings, I drive forth upon the winds of the North Sea; shaking out my feathers, I laugh as I point toward the mists of the South Mountain.
To employ, abandon, act, or hide—each has its own time. This meaning is not granted to ordinary people to know. Let the green mountains reflect one’s white hair;
the crimson steed naturally follows the dragon in flight. Have you not seen the old man of Nanyang? In days of yore, his responses in the imperial court were once perfunctory.
The "large-eared" one was startled as the flowers beneath his eyes were overturned; Zilin lost the treasure within his robes. Now and then, who can vie with this?
How many? The shadow-grass does not reveal the *sindūra*. Mother and child suddenly share the same moment of pecking and hatching; the golden sun bursts forth from the crystal shell.
Following the rhyme of Elder Songyue, I send this verse to the Venerable Qing.
The Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall into numerical categories. To go and return, one must necessarily travel the great road; iron walls and silver mountains are squeezed open.

In the four directions and eight corners, there is no turning back or obstruction. Without a single hair’s breadth of concealment, the whole body is revealed. This is the dragon of Chan and the tiger of Vinaya.
Pleasure within suffering, and suffering within pleasure. Pure Chan, pure Chan, listen to my words: that which precedes heaven is not the ancestor of the mind.
[This was] sent by the present Librarian.
This is a present-case koan; it does not involve contrived arrangements. To see it upon first sight is already to be separated from it by the ends of the earth.

The Tathāgatas of the three periods open their eyes only to dream; the entire Great Canon of Teachings is nothing but scattering dust and throwing sand. Xuefeng went to Touzi three times and ascended Dongshan nine times;
even at the Inn on Mount Ao, he could not avoid setting them out from the beginning. Thus, Xinghua traveled on foot through the south.

Not one person has ever been able to strike upon the truth of the Dharma. When they finally reach the staff of the Great Awakened One, they deeply understand the intent behind Linji’s receiving blows from Huangbo;
at such a moment, it would be best to dig deep and bury them. *Du du!* What kind of time is this now?
Early winter is bitterly cold, and the great rivers are frozen solid. If you can go, then go; when it is time to rest, then rest. This matter—
What need is there to wait for others to speak?
Next, Yangshan’s response to the rhyme of Liangtang, presented as a gift to the Librarian Qi:
"The entire Tripitaka is but worn-out scrap paper. Before seeking to benefit others, one must first benefit oneself; only when what is beneath the eyes is clearly seen does one ascend."
The pivot: the mouth naturally has no idle words. Dongshan’s sour dumplings were hardly many; only after chewing them through does one know their delicious flavor.
Whether wise, one is naturally worthy of respect; whether foolish, how could one be so easily disparaged?

When Luzu saw people, he simply faced the wall; when Jushi saw people, he only raised a finger. There are many gates for provisional arrangements according to circumstances, but in the ultimate sense, it returns to—
The source has no separate intent; in a single instant, one turns over upon the tip of a hair. Across all ten billion hairs, it is exactly thus.
Who else could cover heaven and earth? To fully accept this in one's entire being rests entirely with you.
Seeing off National Preceptor Lang of Guoqing as he returns to Taiping with the Great and Small Tripitakas. The wind is high and the moon is bright; the whole is raised, and the half is raised.
At Yandang and Tiantai, within the Luohan Temple, one year passes with three novices being ordained. From where did Old Man Zhenjing receive this news? He overturns it all!
To speak of one thing is to speak of all. How can a clear-eyed monk discern this? This very function is distinct from that function;
in the realm of Great Peace, all doubt and suspicion are utterly severed. Thus it is, thus it is. How magnificent! How magnificent!
One cannot help but laugh at that horse-kid of old, who let out a thunderous roar with a single shout of awe-inspiring power.
Seeing off Daozang, the Abbot of the Canon, as he returns to Mount Jiang;
having exited the gate of Lingyan, he immediately enters the chamber of Mount Jiang. He shatters the mani-jewel, and heaven and earth turn as black as lacquer.
Master Bao split open the twelve faces; Zhiwen Sengyao raised his brush of ink and color. At midnight he released the black rooster; touching it, the clay ox bellowed.
Beneath the Hall of the True Lineage, the weeds reach the heavens; the ancestral style of the Three Buddhas has leaked through all at once. *Tu!*
Following the rhyme of my Dharma brother Dongshan, I send this in farewell to the Abbot Yunchang:
Beyond the Three Vehicles of the Teaching, nothing can surpass it; Having grasped its essence, one returns as a *śramaṇa*. How could the various quarters lack those who sever the binding ropes?

Yet, what can be done against these six steeds that chase the wind? I have heard it said that empty fame hangs in the government offices; Many there are whose foreheads are marked and whose gills are scorched.

Suffering is slight. If you are willing to believe that within deep mountains and remote valleys there is another lofty standard continuing the ancestors, then consider my eldest brother, the Elder of the Eastern Mountain (Dongshan).
With a single strike at the profound gate, ten thousand layers are shattered; entering the mud and the water, he has composed wondrous verses.
For now, let me open your azure eyes for you.
Formerly, Jiangxin Wuyan composed a verse to send to Chan Master Chang as he departed for Lingyan; Zhongmou Wuji harmonized it with his own.
Since I had already retired from my duties, I followed the rhyme to present this in honor of the Dharma:
The Dharma is fundamentally perfected; In every dust mote, they mutually interpenetrate. One should know that within daily life, There is never a departure from the Land of Silent Radiance.
The heron’s pond and the Vulture Peak cast off dust and sand; when has there ever been a word spoken that reaches home? The Three Elders, with bitter mouths, exerted themselves to uphold it;
the secret intent is clear and bright—it has always belonged to you. How pitiful is Old Master Wáng! He did not strike this broken drum. Cease arguing over principle and phenomenon;
it stands far beyond the reach of words and thought. Why should the dragon seek a perch? Why need the phoenix find a branch? Out upon the sea!
Wandering freely in all directions, both Miaode and Kongsheng lacked true awakening.
To the Abbot Chang, who possesses the treasury of the true nature within the mind: in daily life there is no error; he cuts off the myriad stimuli before they arise—where can one seek his traces?
One cannot pass through the golden circle; one must swallow and spit out the thorny *liji* fruit.
When the iron wall and silver mountains come crashing against one’s face, this is the good news of the true person.
In the same rhyme, I present this to Attendant Fan of Mount Yang:

The Perfect Circle cast by Dayang has been thrown forth; Maitreya has opened wide the multi-storied pavilion. Transcending the mysterious barrier above, all are wondrous moves made before the trigger.
The ancient tale of a thousand years is being enacted once more; Myriad miles away, the divine light flashes and flickers. The bird’s nest blows up—*! 108*—*! 108*—*! 108*.
A tuft of cloth: how, in the end, can one truly comprehend it? Throughout all quarters there are great luminous pearls, yet they are sold away as if they were mere peas.
Furthermore, my Dharma brother Songyue has sent a verse on the rhyme of Elder Gaō’s “pitch-black brightness, bright and clear”:
"The sixteen-foot golden body is but a single blade of grass; divine heads and demonic faces are applied in vain."

Presented. Holy understanding and mundane sentiments must be thoroughly swept away. Below, it is bottomless; above, it has no peak. At the tip of a single hair, heaven and abyss are suddenly distinguished.
A broken jar cannot perform the function of a jar. Like lightning, it does not endure long; like a plantain tree, it lacks solidity.

Ten-thousand-li autumn light stretches to the coastal peaks; the frost clears the great wilds as returning geese cry out. Recite aloud the three hundred poems of Hanshan—what need is there to pick them up?
The flowers bloom with a subtle smile. I contemplate the ancient Buddha, Master Songyue; his aged spirit often swallows the long rainbows of heaven.

One knows not that the source of Chan drowns the vast ocean, yet one perceives how his literary array drives forth thunder and wind. Universally responding to all capacities without weariness, his celestial auspiciousness spreads fragrance and turns ever more radiant.
He shatters the pearl from beneath the jaw of the Black Dragon King; a single grain of it is truly enough to make the vast sea seem but a speck.
In the same rhyme, I send off the attendant Lingyin Fang, who was called three times by the National Teacher;
he stayed one night at Caoxi. If you understand, white clouds stretch ten thousand miles; if you do not understand, a single nail drives into the wood.
China and India have long been beyond each other’s reach; what connection could there be between the numbers four, seven, two, and three?

To discard one layer is to encounter another layer: the lake’s light glistens, the mountains are misty and vast. Not by discarding one layer to meet another: the *haitang* tree bears rain-stained vermilion blossoms.
An old monk with white hair awakens from his dream; at the corner of the eaves, the wind whistles with a *ding-dong* sound. —Deshan.
The staff and the shout of Linji—iron added to the back of a diamond head. Rolling out from amidst a heap of refuse, he makes even Tao Jingjie of Chaisang fall over with laughter.
I bid farewell to the Abbot Fei as he returns to Cuiyan:

a dharma-son of the Way, a steed of the heavenly horse. He tramples upon the empty universe, having thoroughly scrutinized and mastered the host within the guest, and now acts as the host within the guest.
With feet of faith, one leaps across the Flower Treasury Ocean; in daily life, at every turn, there is nothing to be attained. When the eyebrows have fallen out completely, they grow back again;
the Green Rock is both strange and yet lovable. Strange beyond measure, yet love cannot be fully exhausted.
From three thousand miles away, one vainly harbors deep affection; looking face-to-face, there is truly nothing to say. Who knows this wordless passion? It is utterly worn out.
Faded yellow chrysanthemums bloom by the eastern fence; millet steams in earthenware basins as the autumn days grow dim. A clear frost covers the ground and yellow leaves fly.

This is the song of the zither without strings for the Abbot Zang of Guoqing and Shaolin: one sound, one breath, three thousand notes. Those from all quarters who wish to join in the harmony—will they not?
Complete. To shift the register and change the melody is merely empty clamor. Dongshan’s later "downward-flowing boat" has its sublime resonance transcending the mystery within mysteries.
Upon whose side do the rhythmic beats fall today? That true connoisseur remains unmet—how pitiable. A gentle breeze blows upon one's robes under a sun-drenched sky;
a vast inspiration rises abruptly, linking the Three Terraces. Snow flies from Stone Bridge, spraying across the long river. Fenggan—one—
Laughing at the eccentricities of Hanshan and Shishi,
I bid farewell to Chan Master Lizang:
since the characters do not form a name, and even the eight strokes are not right, cut off mind, intellect, and consciousness, and manifest the principle of True Suchness.
The main peak of Fengtai Mountain stands overturned; in the midsummer heat, frost and hail fall from the sky. Without the sinews of insight in one’s eyes, it is not easy to peer into this;
with the path at one’s heels, one reaches the vast emptiness. Water seeks moisture and fire seeks dryness; if you wish to investigate the ancestral wind, you must sweep away the weeds.
Performing the *zhazhi* dance atop a hundred-foot pole—those "two, three, four, and seven" are all struck dumb with awe.
Next, regarding the verse by my Dharma brother, Master Zhile Liaotang, for the Venerable Shizhi:
Above, there is no transmission; below, there is no bestowal. All currents are cut off, not a single drop remaining. One listens to the void with a ladle.

Successive errors have been inherited and successive delusions have been passed down. Who among the wise would be so enticed by external things as to close their eyes and create night, or open their eyes and create day?

When a disease has entered the vital points beyond the gallbladder and diaphragm, even a divine physician cannot save one. To revive after death is like a bell waiting for a strike. Why does the spring not drink when it is stolen?
Why does the bait not sniff when it is offered with pride? Why do things plot for novelty, and why do people seek out the old?
In this endeavor, seek the dark pearl from the formless; be careful not to exhaust your intelligence on the clamor of petty disputes.
In this way, you may perhaps align your mind with the Primordial Source before Heaven; it is truly unnecessary to debate the distant lineage of one's ancestors.
In the rhyme of my elder brother Zhongmou, I send off Attendant Xun:
That which is practiced is not yet Chan; that which is studied is not yet the Way. True practice and genuine realization—there is neither good nor bad therein.
The Patriarch of Mount Dongshan sought a person and once entered the weeds; at midday the golden cock crows—neither late nor early.
He took my hand and announced it on the long corridor, which was truly enough to comfort my pure heart. Three hundred years of lofty wind—clapping my hands, I offer a smile in response.

You people who chase after sounds and pursue forms—where will you seek the head and brain? You practitioners of the Way, sons of archers and smiths: you should naturally inherit the legacy of your ancestors.
As for the songs of the "White Snow" throughout your lives, do not trouble yourselves to speak them to the mountain barbarians.
To send off Attendant Yin toward that ultimate point: it does not involve verbal explanation. To realize it is to realize it immediately; to deliberate upon it is to incur fault.

If you are a person of the fundamental share, why worry about matters of the fundamental share? You should know that both Buddhas and Patriarchs have all gone forth from this very place. Pick up Mount Sumeru!
Weighed at two *liang*. The old man of the Eastern Mountain is truly ferocious; using the method of black beans, he exchanges people's eyes.
Old Sōngyuan, deaf as he is, does not even see this: every single thread and grain of dust cannot be exhausted. As soon as one moves, one is led away by his ghosts and spirits.
To discourse on the wondrous and talk of the profound is most pitiable; they gallop wantonly behind horses and before donkeys. One must quickly cut them off!
A five-colored rope. Leaping upward, he sits and cuts off the crowns of a thousand sages. A-he-he! Do you understand? Heaven and earth from ancient times to now;
mountains and rivers from ancient times to now. Day is bright and night is dark; the sun is warm and the breeze is harmonious. It is well to return with a high song;
cleaving through a thousand peaks, one enters the misty thickets.

In the transmission of the Pure Compassion (Jingci) Abbot Mingzang, the Chan school possesses both essence and function. Later, with wisdom uprooting what was previously settled, the five peaks fall in majesty at the blow of the staff;
beneath the shout, the thousand rivers dry up in surging turmoil. Now, having set aside both staff and shout, what harm is there in giving them fully? Or not?
Completely stripped bare. Wearing horns and holding up his head, he comes this way. How many can find life within death? The Dharma friend from Yangzhou is truly eccentric;
even the entire Great Canon cannot restrain him. He lifts open the Mirror of the Source to illuminate all lands and worlds;
like a bright jade moon, it radiates pure luster. Last night he stayed with me for one night; when the conversation reached the wordless state, his heart was naturally satisfied. He shifts the pivot—
The boatman returns; who can take up the broken string and mend it with *luanjiao* glue?
To the Master Guangzang:
The Buddha-dharma is omnipresent; when has one ever sought even a grain of mustard seed of it? Not even a single grain of mustard seed can be found.
Attained! It is manifest and clear throughout all places. High heavens and vast earth; the sun, moon, and stars are bright and luminous.
The wildcat and the white ox both recite "Mahā. Miao-de and Kong-sheng are stiff, coarse, and chaotic. There is illumination and there is function; there is punishment and there is reward.
Seven blows for thirteen—how many people know the pain? In days to come, when the true command is exercised upon the solitary peak.
One must surely lift up this Vairocana-treasury and send it back to the distant abode of the Abbot Zang, to return to the White Crane and the Snowy Heart;
the Way is boundless, and practitioners cannot easily fathom its frontiers. Without moving one's heels, one suddenly treads upon it—who would say it is near?
Beside the eyebrows, though near it is distant; though distant, it is near. Reaching where there is nowhere to reach—what measure can contain it?

Spring has already passed, yet the days are long; as summer arrives, one feels the southern breeze even cooler. The clouds across the eight directions have withdrawn, the lingering rain has cleared, and the sky stretches ten thousand miles, a vast azure.

The Way-man left Qiantang yesterday; this autumn, he says again he is returning to his native village. A- (Note: The final character "阿" appears to be a fragment or an incomplete syllable, likely part of a name or a phonetic marker.)
The Master’s Zen mind is as pure and bright as snow; truly it vies with the pines and the moon for luminous radiance. To come and go is not to come and go;
to be a treasury is not to be a treasury. Aside from the venerable teacher Nanquan, who else could sing this one pure song?
I present this to Master Muzang, who has come to meet me by shattering the mirror. A single orb of brilliant sun shines across the void; the Tathāgatas of the three periods do not show their heads.
From where could five thousand scrolls be sought? Neither provisional nor real, neither partial nor complete—this is why it is called that which is outside the teachings.
The single transmission: at Shaolin, the direct pointing has long since become a winding path; only when the blind donkey is extinguished does one transcend.
O practitioners of the Way, the three eyes on the crown of your heads are upright; watch for the command as the grass bows and the wind blows. How pitiable and how laughable is Old Gautama:
yesterday he was settled, today he is unsettled.

In sending off the Abbot Hao to my Master’s place of seclusion, I do not take his way as a teacher, nor his virtue as a teacher, nor his principle of speaking when it is time to speak and remaining silent when it is time to be silent as a teacher;
nor do I take his "living capture of Zhou Jingang" or his "arresting of the White-robbery Thief" as a teacher— only that he has nothing to teach.
And as for following such a teacher—what would that ultimately amount to? Have you not seen what the Patriarch Baizhang once said:
"With a single large coin, one buys a sesame cake; having eaten it into one's belly, one is immediately no longer hungry.
Furthermore, who cares about the Southern Heavens, the Northern Wutai, or the myriad Bodhisattvas in Mount Qingliang? It is enough to attract this old man of Changting.
Clapping hands and laughing heartily. *Du!* (A shout).
Sending Attendant Qing to Jingci:

The great thousandfold world-system is entirely the Tathāgatagarbha; the Mirror of the School is loftily suspended, emptying the myriad phenomena. With a single leap, the crimson-tailed fish pierces the dragon gate.
The gate. The level lake rises with waves a thousand fathoms high; the old monk hastily rolls up the corner of his *kāṣāya*. "Watch you, for snow and hail fly through the blue sky!
A chick born this very morning is a phoenix; it makes the thousand-year-old crane atop the pine tree laugh until it falls over.
Following the rhyme to see off a monk returning to Shu:

his gait is like that of a donkey’s hoof and a horse’s trot. It stirs up a thousand doubts and ten thousand suspicions. If you wish to recognize your original face, look well at the autumn moon casting its radiance.
How many clever fellows have missed the mark? To come back and place eyebrows upon the eyes—to put on clothes only when one is already fit for them.
To ward off the cold: how can a painted cake ever satisfy hunger? Having smashed through the Jiamen Pass, one turns their head and finds the sun already behind the pines to the west.
This is a verse in the style of "Snow at the Window" by Yiwang, presented as a single sentence to the Record-keeper Yin:
A dragon is no dragon; set all that aside. To be called "majestically powerful"—it is evident that this does not fall within the realm of words and thought. Solely.
Neither one nor two, neither dual nor single—the old barbarian has struck out his front teeth. A wondrous lute without strings—who can appreciate its sound?
Return to me that which lies to the left of Mount Dongshan. Most outstanding yet utterly ordinary; how could a mere hair’s breadth suffice to discuss long and short?

When pressed against the Three Barriers, they shatter at the touch of the hand. The Sea-Seal is profoundly still, containing the autumn light. It transcends the Three Sages and surpasses the Ten Philosophers. Atop [the head]...

At each gate there is a hole piercing to the heavens; though his belly is full of literary compositions, not a single character exists. A bandit’s face looks like a man’s, yet every man looks like a bandit.
To the Archivist Gong of Jingci Temple, who has returned for further study under the former Abbot of Jiangshan:
"The first character of the True Lineage is recognized by no one. When the author meets him, Gong bows in silence. His fourfold eloquence flows like a hanging river all at once.
Qian. Eighty thousand Dharma gates are empty and profoundly still. The lake and sky have received their fill of rain, and a cool air floats upon them.
Verdant waves ripple as the wind whistles through the reeds. Where speech and silence cannot reach, the oriole calls out several times by the willow bank.
Raising my eyebrows, my eyes are like the moon; why should I, an old man, trouble myself with further words? Returning east, I shall meet the Elder of Zhongshan; he has had his own life.
I shall speak for you according to your capacity.
Following the original rhyme, I send this verse to the attendant Qià:
To receive resonance and inherit the void is truly to undergo the waves. Will you, a man of great character, truly consent to this? Then, please let go from the very beginning.
Stop! Otherwise, you shall run hither and thither. This year has passed, yet another begins. To whom does the Patriarch’s intent truly belong to transmit?
Three times he calls, three times he responds, yet no trace remains. It may not necessarily fall before the Empty King.
Old Bhikṣu Nantang: though he has a mouth, he speaks no Zen. Even if you were to grasp it, it would still not involve words. *Du!* Such is the presentation.
Singing this to cleanse the field of the mind: one must believe that within the alchemical vessel there is another heaven.

This gift to Cao from Boting—Zhaozhou’s discourse on Chan is truly of a transcendent style. When someone asked about the Westward Transmission, he pointed to the courtyard cypress; sitting thus, he caused his school’s gate to flourish with purity.
The wind! Not only does its essence and function transcend clarity, but it stands out even more exceptionally at Yangqi. The chestnut thorn and the golden circle are tossed about in chaotic embrace;
the mule with its prancing hooves leaps and gallops with joy. It tramples the heavens and earth to pieces, leaving no trace behind.
For how many years have these two elders remained inactive? The assembly on Vulture Peak remains as it was. Tugging up his head, the dhūta monk smiles at Huayan; the peaks are clustered and steep.
A blue lotus blooms upon the wall; spring fills Jiangnan for yet another three months. Willow catkins fill the sky like falling snow.
For you, I pour forth my heart at this very moment. In the past you did not come; now you do not depart.

When Chan Master Gaō was sent to Baizhang for his second visit and was struck with a shout for being "hot," Huangbo heard of it and was so startled that he stuck out his tongue. The True Lineage has vanished toward the side of the blind donkey;
even a monk with a mouth finds it difficult to explain. Ciming changed his robes and returned to Fenyang; eating in the wind and sleeping by the water—what [can be said]?
Majestic! A solitary standard rising above the mundane for three hundred years—its lofty principle once again brushes against the azure heavens. To disregard peril and ruin—how utterly perverse!
With a tiger’s head, he has severed the horn of the azure dragon; treading upon the Yuanyang Lake, he dries it up to its very bottom.
Across ten thousand li of autumn sky, a single falcon soars.
Master Yunshuo, within the Great Canon there is no dharma to be spoken. Practitioners, be careful not to create complications; the direct pointing of Shaolin has already become circuitous.
How could I possibly add further words? A thousand flowers and ten thousand plants are now vying for spring; emerging above the heavens, now—
Who is this person? Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, they turn their body in a single phrase; with one kick, the great earth is cleared of even the finest speck of dust.

Vertically and horizontally encompassing all, you must see for yourself: silent and desolate, yet the light blazes forth. Like refined gold made as supple as a finger-ring, it must enter the red furnace once more to be forged.
I see Master Huizang off on his return to Shangjiang. At the same time, I invite Qinglan and Yuntong of Nengren to return to Zongyuyi;
let them take the precepts as their body and wisdom as their life. Let them emerge and enter through the Dharma-gate without deficiency or excess—opening their mouths, they swallow it all at once.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time chew up empty space and spit out bones; the tiger’s jaw and braided whiskers have not yet made it as a master.
Only the rabbit’s head wearing horns is truly extraordinary. I have a single phrase for you: beneath the Hall of White Clouds, waves cling to the sky.
Yuan Tong does not open a pharmacy for life-restoring herbs; the stone of the dhūta practitioner is entwined by moss.
The Abbot Xizang returned from Dayang to Ningqin;
leaving his parents to rely upon his teacher, he was still young. To leave his teacher to care for his parents—how could that be deemed aged?

Not failing either parent or teacher, his filial piety truly exemplifies the Way of the Ancient Sovereign. White clouds fly solitary as the heavens and sea turn azure; by the banks, willows and river-plum receive their spring.
Spring has arrived early. I too have kin whom I must return to see; the child in his variegated robes will cry and laugh until one falls over.

Once one has left the household life, there is ultimately no principle for remaining in the secular world. How long can such laughter last before it turns to vexation? Sorrow and joy are fundamentally without root or stem;

the entanglements of affection are but a burden of suffering in the breast. One must surely lift up the great round mirror and sweep away both the defilement of attachment and the dust of emotion all at once. Right now...
Neither of the past nor of the future, the wisdom of awakening radiates a brilliant light. To repay the teacher, the teacher says it is so;
to repay one's parents, the parents say it is good. When all worldly affairs have ceased and one has returned home, this undivided single essence is the Jewel of the Sangha.
This is the verse sent by the late Master Baoning to Venerable Xuan: "Last night, the void collapsed entirely;
In the blazing heavens, hail was found amidst the fire. Seeking a kindred spirit beyond the limit of Avidyā, At Caoxi, he encountered Yisuo Jue.
Generally speaking, these words do not fall to the edge; The broken chopsticks stir the azure sky."
The Dragon Abyss: smashing the black pearl is but a trivial matter; sitting and watching the waves on level ground stick to the sky—throughout all antiquity and to this day, there is only this.
If you wish to observe what the predecessors employed first, where will you seek the Three Sages when you lift your eyes? A single step casually transcends the Ten Stages.
This school, this school, must be realized by oneself; once realized, one does not borrow the power of another. In the same cauldron.
Eating together and sleeping in the same bed, yet by the end, liver and gall become separate realms. Nan Tang’s song of "Resting" is the response;
one can roam freely within the treasury of Vairocana. Myriad dharmas cannot serve as companions; the solitary moon naturally knows how to follow the three boats.
Sent by Master Liang of Xuedou:
Clouds atop Mount Miaogao, The moon within the Mirror-Pool of Brocade; Its clear reflection falls upon the world, Its solitary radiance fills the vast void.
For forty-nine years he has not spoken; the old monkey’s cry cuts short the dawn in the central crag. From amidst the grass, a sleeping hare slips out;
startled, the two spirits set forth upon the Bird Path.
Seeing off Chan Master Wanshou Zhen on his journey to Mount Tai and Mount Yan.
Mount Yan is high and cold; even in the fifth and sixth months, ice flows down its rushing torrents.

Since you already hold the staff—the very form of the mountain—in your grasp, you may explore its depths as a resource for your travels and observations. Perilous peaks compete to stand like jeweled banners, while the narrow paths wind like sheep’s tracks.
The intestines are coiled; I know not what Dharma the Arhat is preaching. I see only the rain of flowers falling vast and wide.
How does this compare to turning the pivot of Vairocana’s treasury? A single ray of divine light swallows the ten thousand phenomena. It overturns the seas and mountains beyond compare;
how could one scratch an itch through a boot with one's fist?
Your conduct is such that you could have left earlier; Bao Ning has sent a verse requesting a response.
To engage the tongues of patch-robed monks is like scraping hair from a tortoise’s shell or shaving iron from the point of a needle.

When one encounters the ignorance of self and others, what need is there to seek the joy of Dharma or the delight of Chan? In the three winters, withered trees bloom with flowers throughout the forest; in the nine summers, the scorching heavens stretch on and on.
Earth and snow. The master returns me to the old Xuan Sha, who could say, "Lingyun had never yet reached the ultimate.
Where things are磊磊落落 (leilei luoluo—lofty and expansive), there is great prolixity; where they are忉忉怛怛 (daodaodatata—frantic and distressed), not even a single pull will suffice.

When the myriad functions have ceased and the thousand sages are no longer carried, there is emptiness within, emptiness without, and emptiness both within and without. Like a snake forced to transform into a dragon, one attains realization at the appointed time.
Ah! For one month, two months, three months, and four months, the Dharma-joy was transmitted;

before the time of the Patriarch Wei-yin, there was no bestowing or receiving. Śākyamuni’s coming into the world was in vain after the Lamp-Lighter; his picking up the flower on Vulture Peak was but a needless leakage.

The pivot. At Shaolin, they obtained the marrow and vied to display their ugliness; at Huangmei, at midnight, they struck the very bottom and erred. Old Lu held them back, yet it was not inherently evil;
alas, the people of the world rush about in pursuit, receiving echoes and inheriting emptiness without realizing it. O practitioners, rejoice that you have long since forgotten one another;
coming and going, there is no hindrance—both hands are empty. To transcend the past and surpass the present is no small matter; seizing the food and driving away [the delusion].
Plowing and gnawing at pigs and dogs. Have you not seen? When Linji took his leave of Huangbo in those days, he picked up the meditation board and burned it.
The True Lineage was extinguished among blind donkeys; an iron snake in the weeds with horns upon its head.

In the same rhyme, I present this verse to the attendant Sī, who crosses waters and pierces clouds to visit his teachers and friends: In the morning he discusses Tiantai; by evening he studies Xianshou. As for the matter of one’s own fundamental being, how should it truly be?
When pressed, few people know that it exists. If you have not yet mastered the art of inquiry, listen to my words: Who is it right now? Who is it?
Open your mouth! You are a great man among the monks; why follow in the footsteps of others? On the summit of Dongshan, stride with wide steps;
before the Jade Terrace Peak, extend both hands. Pushing aside the myriad phenomena, one sees the whole body; cutting off all conceptual machinations, one reveals the true roar.
Those of small capacity dare not recklessly speculate; only Buddhas and Patriarchs are fit to discuss transmission and reception. The golden duck...
The fragrant incense has faded from the brocade curtains; the gates of earth and heaven have both been dislocated from their sockets.
To the Southern School:
the secret seal of the Southern School has been transmitted for a long time; the Ten Sages and Three Worthies know nothing of it. It drags the void over and turns it upside down.
Look! Layer upon layer of brocade thread pierces the Ox and Dipper constellations. When the staff descends, the true mechanism is revealed; even Deshan and Linji would be moved to pity.

Only by breaking out of the nest and shattering the trap can one truly grasp it; then, like wind blowing and thunder crashing, all will be as it should. I am a guest of the universe with nothing to do;
having tested those with copper heads and iron jaws, I have cast them all into the great lake. With a single pillow, I sleep high.
Sleeping in truth is the supreme strategy.
Using the rhyme of Benjue Chushi, I present this to the venerable masters Yiyunwu, Yangqi, and Shichuang.
Their magnanimity is as vast as a great hall; their conduct further enhances the legacy of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

The radiance of his conduct and concealment spreads widely, bestowing blessings upon humans and devas. He assisted Hongzhi and supported Ciming; all were those to whom he was personally entrusted at Vulture Peak.
The snapping of a string is most skillfully mended by the *luangjiao* glue. Play for me once more the melody of Yunmen. On lofty mountains and flowing waters, few are those who understand the music.
How quickly do they harmonize with the "White Snow" and "Yangchun"? Throughout his life, this old man of Chu has graced the Five Phoenix Pavilion; he is truly without shame before the Great [Master].
Compassionate Thousand Hands and Eyes. Three years have passed since I left Lingyan; returning now, I rejoice to see carved eaves rising from the level plains.

These pillars and foundations serve as peerless resources; how could these rafters and beams be ordinary wood? Master and attendants can maintain a mind of non-duality; past and present share the same single mechanism.
It is like the wind following the tiger and clouds following the dragon; it resembles the earth upholding the mountains and stones containing jade.
The great master surely knows that there is no discarded timber; what merchant of skill has ever hoarded anything?
Gathering the great chiliocosm to make it a single grain of millet—its substance is sufficient and its utility is sufficient. Its utility being sufficient, Luo-hu was not born; who could record him?

A Gift to the Wayfarer of Non-Action Returning to the Peaks The Wayfarer of the Peaks is named "Non-Action. He gazes with haughty indifference upon the realm beyond things, transcending the subtle and the obscure.

At times he manifests his body throughout the dust-motes and lands of the universe, vying directly with the Buddhas and Patriarchs in their swift exertion. Which of the Buddhas and Patriarchs comes first? Who am I that follows behind? To act while not acting—this is the ultimate.
Jiǎdòu: At night he ascends Tuṣita; by day he is in Jambudvīpa. When questioned, people of the time rarely know of his existence.

How many with eyes of doubt have peered through the wall? Stolidly and listlessly they maintain empty stillness. To the end, they do not understand the phrase for turning around. What benefit is there in practicing in such a manner?
If you wish to recognize the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), listen to my words: A solitary moon coldly bathes the moons in a thousand rivers. Wave upon wave.
Sudden manifestation is the ordinary; meeting everywhere, it is fundamentally not different. My mind and the moon are equally empty and at ease;
they illuminate heaven and earth in a continuous cycle. When both light and object are forgotten, the illumination is naturally still. A single cry of a crane comes from amidst the clouds.
Next, following the rhyme of "Stone Buddha Yuan'an," I see off the Venerable Ju to Longhe.
The Stone Buddha of Xinchang has long been renowned. Within the tip of a single hair, infinite oceans of lands exist; Beyond the nine heavens, his entire body appears;
From the crest of ten-thousand-fathom peaks, he extends a single hand. Sentient beings are mired in inversion and difficult to transform; Time and again they travel eastward, yet turn back.
He fled westward; even the Buddha could do nothing from the outset, so how could I possibly open my mouth?

The Daoist holds a golden mallet within his sleeve, sufficient to shatter the heads of the demonic armies. If this wondrous function and numinous mechanism manifest before one, there is no hindrance to making a true roar at every encounter.
Have you not seen how the Elder of Longtan blew out the lamp, its light piercing the Seven and Eight Stars?
Doubt. You, Master Zi, have personally inherited from the Stone Buddha; do you not know whether the Stone Buddha ever spoke? Yet you seek a true kinsman beyond words.
Where in the eye can beauty or ugliness be found? The Woman of Darkness and the Goddess of Merit—no wise host accepts either.
Nan Tang’s grandmotherly Zen like this—perhaps he could grasp nine out of ten, but not necessarily seven.
As the carriage-bearer attendant returned home to visit his Dharma brother Baofu Yichan, who dwells thus:
"This very mind is Buddha"—the stray cat climbs upside down upon the Bodhi tree. As he departs thus:
"Neither mind nor Buddha"—the cast-iron scale-weight is eaten through by worms; pine flowers for food, lotus for clothing. Upon the precipitous cliffs and sheer walls—what?
Majestic and lofty! Holding fast to the secure barrier lacks the quality of liberation; letting go of the path is ultimately most appropriate.
When the Abbot stepped forward and extended his hand, he stirred the golden-haired lion’s roar. If you ask what the matter of Lingyan is like:
black, black, bright—three, eight, nine.
In the style of Zhongmou, I present this verse as a gift to the Venerable Zhi:
One exhale, one inhale— The heels do not touch the ground; The nostrils hang down like great gourds. When the whole body enters the weeds, Both eyebrows are lost.
Before the sound, it is not sound; A vast iron net is spread across the heavens. After the form, it is not form; [The net] covers the earth.
The ripples of wind spread throughout the world; sometimes there is a roar of defiance, sometimes a lingering glance and hesitation.

In their lofty coming and going they transcend the mundane; in their brilliance they stand out like a needle’s point from its case. On the battlefield of a hundred battles, their spirit is vast and surging;
with a single throw of Mount Taihua, the void is rendered immense. When masters meet, there is yielding and seizing; above the thousand sages, there is no tongs or hammer. —Jue Tian.
The sun has suddenly fallen; who can now brandish the halberd of Lu Yang? Before the Hall of the Horse Ancestor, the words of the second encounter ring out:
upon the solitary peak of Miaofeng, the clear frost flies. One shout truly deafens both ears; within the Great Tang, there is no Zen master.
Sending Master Chen back to his hometown:

"Those who enter through the gate do not possess the family treasure. If one seeks the whole body upon the tips of the hundred grasses, what is the point of picking up one thing and putting down another?
To emerge from here and vanish there is merely following habitual patterns. A monk’s staff, six or seven feet long, beats the wind and strikes the rain.

The rain startles gods and men. The spiritual mechanism of hand and face transcends thought and calculation; the true eye at the crown of the head knows no partiality. This very thing gives birth to parents;
it overwhelms Buddhas and patriarchs, surpassing all ordinary ranks. Treading upon the Stone Bridge, it is split in two;
with a single shout, the clouds of a thousand peaks are dispersed.

Next, following the rhyme of Xianyan Zhongmou, I present this verse as a gift to the Venerable Yao, who has investigated his own nature and clarified the fundamental source, thereby establishing his own course: "What need is there to seek you out from such great distances? Before leaving Mount Ou, our paths had already diverged;
Treading upon the clouds of Wu, we have become even more separated. Have you not seen how the moon does not wait for the wind to be cool? Nor... (the text continues).
Behold! The sun shines with brilliance without waiting for fire. One must know that the living and the Buddha share a single source; one should trust that Caoxi has no "orthodox lineage.
To exhaust the profound mysteries is to skillfully explore the subtle; the crow is not inherently black, nor is the crane white. Ignorance and afflictions are True Suchness (Tathatā);

even the tiger’s den and the demon’s palace are all peaceful dwellings. Those of noble character and talent will ultimately transcend the ordinary; at ninety thousand *li*, they shall ride the whirlwind of transformation.
Spreading its wings: the ocean of *saṃsāra* across dust-mote kalpas is contained within a single instant; ten billion worlds are cramped within a single hair.
Striking east and hitting west, calling an uncle "elder brother"—how startling! A golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net meets with a black spot on its forehead.
A Verse by Master Xue’an Jin: The Chan practitioner seeks the phrase within the eye;
the eye within the phrase. Blinking one’s eyebrows, one still does not see it. Sometimes he brandishes the Vajra King;
Sometimes he alone plays with the Unadorned Seal. Whom can the secret instructions of the immortals be transmitted to? Beyond the kalpas lie the sun and moon within the alchemical cauldron.
Central Heaven. On the peak of Mount Taibai, the snow is a furnace of flames; with a snout like a turtle’s, he seizes and swallows the long serpent.
To Jangshan Yuan, the Venerable Who Returns to Shu:
A man of the Way who has seen three Buddhas come; at the place where the bucket-rim was stripped away, his heart-mind opened. Turning back toward Chengdu—ten thousand [li].
The mountain village lies by the gorge where the spring floods roar and clash. Have you not seen how the old man Deshan first left Sichuan?

Before even engaging in battle, his full edge was already blunted and defeated. How much more so when he blew out the lamp during the night assembly; from that moment on, he sang no more of the "Song of Returning Home. Grasping his staff, he was as fierce as a dragon;
reviling Buddhas and scolding Patriarchs, he wielded thunder and wind like whips. Now, in the monastic groves, there is no such elder.
I have composed this verse to send to Yuan Xingkong.

As for the attendant Min, he is reticent in speech yet diligent in practice; having traveled to various regions to seek out patriarchal masters, he now asks: "Who within the realm today is fit to be my teacher?"

This person travels far and wide, fond of seeking and visiting. Do you not see? In ancient times at Jiahe, there was the Elder Yunmen. With a single stroke of his hand or face, he drove forth thunder and wind.
When Gujian met him before the pivot of the mechanism, he suffered a heavy blow. Lightning and sparks flashed in a sudden blur. Dongshan’s head was split; Foguo was blinded.
Suddenly manifesting separate bodies throughout the dust and lands, the Golden Cock flaps its wings and lets out a single cry—then one understands.
In the presence of others, bestow the "Eight of Meng.
Within this Dharma-gate shown to superior persons, the fundamental principle lies in seeing one's nature. To see one thing is to see all things, like gazing into a great round mirror.

The lush and the slender can both be discerned; from beginning to end, all is naturally clear and luminous. When deluded, the sage is but an ordinary person; after awakening, the ordinary person becomes a sage.
Transcending both delusion and awakening, sages and ordinary people are alike as echoes and reflections. Vast and open, penetratingly free of doubt—the work of study and practice is complete.
In the same rhyme, I present this tribute to the Venerable Master Shan upon his reading of the entire Tripitaka:
over five thousand scrolls, in which every land is fully revealed and every atom suddenly manifests. He endures being struck down by the Vajra Deity;
Śākyamuni Buddha does not sit within the Palace of the Sovereign of Emptiness. High comes the call and low is the response; valley echoes and spring sounds harmonize in secret accord.
The light is cast; the divine spirit has a demonic countenance. Since you have already taken up the cangue and confessed your transgressions, I shall settle the case according to the evidence.
To grasp the meaning before the pivot—what need is there to seek out a *śrāmaṇera*? To clarify the essence beyond the categories—it is already too late for expedients.
Unless one belongs to the true lineage, seeing it once is seeing it at once. *Du-du-du!* Do you understand yet? You must cut through nails and sever iron; do not hesitate to bite into it.
Sticking to the teeth—no contrivance involved. Responding universally to all stimuli, it is a ready-made enjoyment. Without the slightest deviation, held up in both hands:
within the ears, the four great oceans can be contained; with not a thread of silk hanging, within the eyes, the sands of the Ganges may be placed.
Unveiling the Makara Ocean, leaning back against Vaiśālī—there is such a man of immeasurable capacity in heaven and on earth.

Riding upon sound and covering over form—truly it is wondrous beyond addition. When one realizes this, it encompasses everything before one’s eyes; when one does not realize it, one establishes a separate livelihood.
When hot, seek coolness; when cold, turn toward the fire. When hungry, eat; when weary, drink tea.
In response to the rhyme, I show this to the monk Daoshe:

This school of mine does not establish written words; the seven times four and the two times three were like water being passed from one vessel to another. If you wish to attain intimacy, [you must realize this].

To cast off medicinal taboos requires neither study nor practice; it is not reached through effort. The "Single Finger" of Cundi and the "Thousand Arms" of the Great Being—know these to be deluded perceptions;
do not mistake them for neutral ignorance. If you seek absolute perfection, you must smash them to pieces. This is the head that reaches toward heaven.

These feet tread upon the earth. Between father and son there is the debt of parental kindness; between ruler and subject there is the principle of righteousness. Discerning colors and distinguishing fragrances, they possess eyes and noses.

When it is appropriate to advance, they advance; when it is appropriate to retreat, they retreat. They can employ things, rather than being employed by things. Thus, both the mundane and the sacred are forgotten.

Benefiting both self and others—this I entrust to you, O Sangha and practitioners of the Way. Firmly maintain your original resolve; keep this in mind at all times. Thus shall you perfectly realize awakened wisdom.
You originally have nothing to seek, and I likewise have nothing to show. It manifests before you in vast openness, beyond words and beyond thought. You should skillfully protect and uphold this.
Do not treat yourself with levity.
The monk Sangchu arrived in the city of He for two nights and three days, yet could find no trace of Nantang; only then did he realize that Sudhana had to visit Deśanā.
Clouds: For seven days it was likewise thus. Cloud of Virtue did not leave the summit of Wondrous Peak; how could this mountain monk ever depart from within the Southern Hall?
Midway, a hundred thoughts suddenly ceased; white birds and misty smoke were all old acquaintances.
With a handshake and a smile, we returned together; finding a simple couch, we lay down to sleep. Tomorrow morning, wishing to sing the tune of returning home, upon waking first—
