I am asked for a verse to accompany his departure. I observe that you originally did not come; why now do you speak of going?
Abandoning both "not coming" and "not going," the pure breeze of the old country is but half a sail. This mountain monk has no substantial dharma to give to others;
you must look well at the opportune moment. What more need be said of the old fellow Xuefeng who went up the mountain nine times, or Dongshan who ascended it three times?
Touzi, if one examines this closely, it is precisely the livelihood of ghosts within the mountain caves beneath Black Mountain.
Even if one were to overturn the entire establishment of the Ao Shan Inn, how would that differ from leaving Zhengzhou and heading toward Cao Gate? It is far, far removed. *Du, du, du!*
Stop! Stop! Stop! Turn toward the other side of Fusang; there lies another radiance that covers heaven and earth.
To the attendant Jing of Mount Jingshan:
take one more step from the top of a hundred-foot pole. With this single step, you transcend the sands of the Ganges. Suddenly overturning the level fields and shallow grasses.
Body. How many can distinguish the paths of mud and water? After the rain, the mud and water are abundant in the wild fields.
In the river it is full; the river fills the riverbed. The old farmer rises at dawn to weed the young seedlings. Exhausted from their labor, they rise together and sing aloud.

The blazing sun fiercely scorches the azure sky, yet there is joy that a breeze has arisen on the willow banks. The Way-man does not shrink from the depth of the mud and water; he labors diligently to clear the way.

His body perspired with cold sweat; upon entering the gate and seeing him for the first time, he forgot the distinction between host and guest. Their shared path and principles were so earnest that their feelings became even more intimate.

They spoke exhaustively of ten years of affairs on the mountain peaks—like dreams, like illusions, like drifting clouds. Sitting until the water was dried up and the mud had vanished, snow-covered carts often lined the ice pillars.
As the incense of the golden duck-burner faded, his mind was naturally at ease. He possessed a noble reputation that continued the legacy of his ancestors.
Presented to Chan Master Jian of Jingci:

The Great Canon of Teachings and the Essential Meaning of Yongming. Mountain colors and lake reflections shine upon the window and desk; The essential meaning of Yongming fills the entire Great Canon.
Sanskrit and Chinese words cannot be lifted up; Azure seas and red dust fly close to the sun. From the womb of an ox, fragrance is born.
The elephant cub tramples the universe to pieces, leaving no trace; how could the thousand eyes of Great Compassion perceive it? How extraordinary is the practitioner of Tiantai!
Before a word is spoken, he has already grasped the whole—both are luminously vast. The nine-feathered phoenix of the Cinnabar Mountain, and the auspicious qilin with its single horn.
I show that the Chief Librarian Jingyan of Lingyin is the Great Dharma Treasury.
It does not involve names or words; it is the daily life of the patch-robed monks and the fundamental source of all Buddhas—not only for those of wisdom.
Behold directly the single assembly on Vulture Peak, solemn and as if never having dispersed. Right now, I, this old monk, am with you in the Hall of Universal Radiance;

we bow to the Honored One Śākyamuni. He has blocked the vital ford, allowing passage neither to the mundane nor the sagely. All proclamations have been swept away, utterly transcending the senses and their objects.
*Tut!* Be careful! Shouldering the iron staff across your shoulder, do not let it smash the broken sand-pot.
Sent to the Venerable Songyue, within the realm of True Purity there is not a single dharma.
Ultimately, one must use a raft to cross the river; atop the tip of the banner-pole, he suddenly turns his body around—who cares if the path on Stonehead is slippery?
The vast and boundless mind of a thousand rivers in a single month; the pine wind plays its music of non-existence.
Tuning the zither: the eight directions are hushed and the night air is solemn. If Old Pang does not speak, who can know his music?
If you wish to penetrate the mystery, you must weed through the grass; only when the bottom of the bucket falls out is it truly finished. The golden hammer in the sleeve stirs its shadow;
at every door is the road to Chang’an.
I bid farewell to the Abbot Shou as he returns east to Fusang.
A man from the East has arrived, soaring ninety thousand li on the celestial wind. He sought pearls but did not enter the palace of the Dragon King;
for ten years he has wandered throughout the Middle Kingdom. What did he encounter amidst this Middle Kingdom? The white sun flies westward, and the waters flow on.
Flowing eastward, at first one sees the willow flowers fly like snow; yet again, one is startled that the white snow is like flying花絮 (willow catkins).

The Great Hua [Mountain] is rent asunder and the Yellow River runs dry. How negligent and superficial is one’s own fundamental matter! Having overturned the five thousand scrolls of the Great Canon, not a single phrase has ever been brought to its conclusion.
Suddenly, upon meeting the Elder Nantang, all myriad kinds and a thousand variations are swept away in a single stroke. For kalpas on end...

Ignorance is extinguished in this very moment; the public case of the former master is resolved instantly. Beneath a bright window, a single mat is spread; atop a hundred-foot pole, one leaps and strides at will.
Externalists and celestial demons alike cast down their spears; the Dragon Spring and Great Arrows swords have just emerged from their scabbards.
Returning to the peak of Laṅkā in the morning, sailing three days by following the wind as before. When relatives and friends ask about the matter of the fundamental inquiry, tell them:
"In the morning, I washed my face with hot water; I took off my clothes and socks and went to sleep. After all, how is it? *Dot!* (A shout).
The secret instructions of the immortals are not transmitted even between father and son.

This original copy was sent as a parting gift from Dongting Lake to the masters of the Eastern and Western Dongtings: "Seventy-two points of floating azure shells; a cool breeze blows upon my robes as the sunlight grows thin."
White waves reach far to meet the darkening heavens; Master Lu lies high in repose as the years grow old.
Through ancient times and now, who has shared this Way? Upon the Hánkōng Pavilion, his two eyes open wide; with one long cry of laughter, he falls joyfully prostrate.

The wild sheep hanging from its horns leave no trace; why must you, my friend, seek it so painfully? The emerald clouds do not stir, the stone screen stands still; by the bank, the *liao* grasses and marsh flowers bloom.
Amidst the autumn colors, he plays. How could such a grand journey be for the sake of indulging in rare wonders? He looks up to the former patriarchs as a mirror and a guide.
Calling out across the river, they understand how to know their home; they are fit to provide a handle for empty space.
A Ballad of the Terrace and the Wild Geese, Sent Off for Attendant Jing:
The Terrace Mountain is green, the Wild Goose Mountain is green. Thousands and tens of thousands of peaks stand tall and dense against the high, dark heavens.

Across the void, stone bridges vie with snow-capped waterfalls; Flying currents splash foam, often scattering like stars in the Milky Way. Its hidden wonders and nurtured elegance cannot be fully described.
Seated here, he caused five hundred and sixteen śrāvaka monks to perish. Alas, my karmic conditions for birth were beneath this very place;

my two feet have not yet had the leisure to ascend these rugged heights. From where has the Superior One come, wishing at once to release his hidden sentiments? Clinging to creepers and climbing the steps, he reaches the summit;
looking down, he sees that among the myriad phenomena, none can escape his gaze. May I vow that my study of the Way shall be like this—probing the depths of the caverns of principle.
Opening the mysterious portal, he has swallowed up the ocean of the Buddhas and overturned the ancestral courtyard, causing Han and Shi to clap their hands in joy and Juna to submit with reverence.
It is my hope that this will suspend the precious moon of the celestial mind and brighten the true lamp beyond the kalpas.
If it were otherwise, why would one need to disdain the swallow and sparrow while boasting of the cloud-soaring Peng, sharing the same likes and dislikes as the mundane world?
A Ballad of Mount Lu, Sent Off Senior Seat Di:
Mount Lu stretches across the mouth of the Nine Rivers. The Five Elders stand towering, as if about to roar. The morning breeze blows through the incense smoke of the Incense Burner Peak;
jade dragons spit snow, flying through the clear day. Master Huiyuan once planted white lotuses here; what manner of people were among his community?
Transcendent! The mountain spirits restrain the carriage of the worldly scholar; this sacred site is entirely entrusted to the immortals of the West.
Tao Qian’s knitted brows were truly in vain; the Prince of Yelang sighed over his ambitions, all for nothing. They speak in vain of elixirs that permeate the fragrance through a flask;

in the end, they cannot change the bones of an ordinary man. My life was originally that of a monk within these mountains; since we parted, a thousand years have passed in the blink of an eye. On this day...
Because you spoke of the past, I suddenly perceive the brilliant colors swirling in the azure sky. That azure sky can be grasped and bound—this pure body with its broad and long tongue.
With a single laugh, it overturns the nine-fold mountain screen. The Mahāyāna Dharma is beyond words and speech.
The Verse of Venerable Beidu at Xiangyun Hermitage, Requested for Harmony by Head Seat Haoling Miao:
The Ten Practices, the Ten Dwellings, and the Ten Transferences. The Elder Beidu is ever the true reality (*dharmatā*). Non-retrogressive (*avaivartika*), equal to, and wondrously awakened.
His lifespan and radiance are immeasurable; The realm and essential nature of every Buddha are identical. Acting in accordance with what he preaches, he is himself...
Not by force. The Iron Ox of Shuangxi eats a single blow; casually he swallows the Elephant of Jiazhou. A hundred thousand Tathāgatas all join in joy;
the kalaviṅka bird fills the void with gifts. Ascending high to gaze afar, the intent is naturally unique;
auspicious clouds form emerald knots atop the jade grove.
Henglang, my Dharma brother, has invited me to respond using the previous rhyme;
thus I answer him: Three thousand li apart, we face one another from afar. Among brothers, who could say there is no mutual intent? At the tip of a hair, the jeweled king-realm surges forth;

Within the breast, there remains the capacity to swallow the ocean’s breadth. When the work is finished, one should proceed with composure; If the power of the Way is not yet complete, how can one rest at ease?
It is well that you have come; the Beidu of former years has returned today. With a glance that cuts across the stream, he is truly a fragrant elephant.

A porcelain jar filled with black rock honey, its exquisite words sealed within, is sent from afar as a gift. In my declining years, I ought only to respond to this gracious invitation, engaging in spirited conversation and clapping hands atop the Cloud Nest.
Song of the Reed Basket (with Preface):

The Venerable Beidu appeared in the Song Dynasty. His spiritual wonders were manifold; he constantly traveled carrying a reed basket upon his shoulder. Upon arriving at Guangling, he went to attend a vegetarian feast hosted by the Li family.

He placed the basket in the middle of their courtyard and said, "The Four Heavenly Kings bestow blessings upon your household. When the Li family attempted to move the basket, [it remained immovable].
Several people were unable to lift it. A young boy peered into the basket and saw four small children, each several inches long.

When the meal was finished, he took them away. Later, he went to the invitation of Liu Yubo, the Governor of Yuan. Yubo ordered the basket to be brought for inspection; dozens of men could not even lift it.
When Yubo approached it, there was only a tattered robe and a wooden bowl inside. Xuanzi then went to the Lanruo Monastery in Jixi, where he paid his respects to the Venerable.

This is the dwelling place of [the Master]. Master Chong of Xian’an resided on the mountain and wished to establish a private chamber, naming it "Luchui" (Reed Basket), but he passed away before his wish was fulfilled.
He entrusted his disciple, the Venerable Zhiming Yi, to carry out the task. It was completed more than a year later by his grandson, Master Miao.
Seeking another title, I again harmonize with the verse of Venerable Xiangyun An and provide a brief preface, requesting that it be engraved as follows:
"Carrying this reed basket, he comes and goes; He truly seems to lack the marks of a Great Man. Behold him, sitting firmly, cutting off all sounds."

Peak! Shedding all mundane sentiments and transcending the measure of the sages, the Four Heavenly Kings crouch like tigers amidst the peaks. When the path of resonance and response intermingles, how could one be merely "wooden" or stubborn?
Turning over the seas and mountains to verify the traces of practice, treading upon heaven and earth until no shadow or form remains.

Carrying down a pure breeze, wood is made into cups; from above, alms-bowls of rice are vied for by others to offer. Zhi Ming built this dwelling and I have composed this song; I write it large upon the reeds.
The name *Miaochengzhou* (Wondrous Ferryboat) was inscribed upon it. The following is the song for the Wondrous Ferryboat, together with its preface.
The Wondrous Ferryboat was formerly the floating residence of Ciang-shan, the former Censor-in-Chief. The Secretary of the Palace Library, Lord Lian Liang, inscribed its nameplate.
Jinshan immediately ceased [his work] and composed a eulogy for it; Caoxi Yue’eng wrote a preface for it, which may be called complete in its excellence.
Yet, he still felt it was insufficient and came to solicit my words. Unable to refuse, I said to him: "True nature is my boat; wisdom is my water;
the six perfections and myriad practices are my sails, masts, oars, and rudders. I ride upon these to roam through the three realms."

In the ocean of the realms, whether flowing or halting, one finds contentment solely within the mind. The winds of right and wrong cannot cause alarm; the eddies of honor and disgrace cannot cause drowning.
Within, there are no rare treasures to arouse the hearts of thieves; without, there are no sounds or colors to stir the judgments of onlookers.
While others are cramped and constrained, I alone am vast and expansive; while others are sorrowful and distressed, I alone am serene.
Yi recited the verses on "Carrying the Moon over Huating" and took delight in the charm of the misty waves at Ezu.
Dwelling neither in this nor that, and clinging to neither the middle of the stream, he nonetheless encountered the scarlet-tailed fish; is this not most wondrous?

Why, then, must one sweep the Weak Water to the east, skim the Flowing Sands to the west, release oneself into the Fiery Sea to the south, or reach the dark abysses of the north? To do so in vain is no small matter.
Yi’s wandering is vast and boundless; he drifts with no fixed destination.
To conclude this, he composes a song: "The universe is vast and boundless—let me set my boat adrift. All transformations ceaselessly flow—may I ride upon them to wander.
I return to my mind and restore my nature; In expansive, unobstructed penetration, what more shall I seek? Casting down the hook and gathering in the line, at Huashan..."
At the ferry of Chuanzi, he brandished his oars and danced with his paddles at the head of the cliffs by E-zhu. Alas for my life in this degenerate age;
I do not behold the sages of former times. I unfurl my sails and turn the tiller to pursue them with all my might, yet my emotions remain weary and far-reaching.
Is it that there is no pure breeze or bright moon to enhance my aesthetic delight? It is simply that the toil of the mundane world and my deluded thoughts have not yet ceased.
It is not that the remnants of mountains and waters are what is lovable, for he has no desire for the rank of duke or marquis.

There is a Great Being (Bodhisattva) who transcends his lineage and stands apart from the common eye; it is only fitting that he should brave the cold and the heat to engage in spirited exchanges of verse.

He is surely about to moisten his mind and bathe his virtue in the Pool of Coolness, gathering lotuses from the fragrant islets. Though the vulgar world may be submerged in darkness and ruin, [he remains unmoved].
I know this; perhaps I may thus avoid rinsing my mouth with stones and using flowing water as a pillow. As the Yangtze and Han rivers stretch boundlessly, let them not restrict my coming and going.
Yet, through the lofty integrity of those who endure the cold of winter, there may still be some consolation for this desolate autumn.
Cessation upon Cessation Pavilion: A Gift to Master Zhang Mójùn.
Master Mójùn named his pavilion "Cessation upon Cessation" (*zhǐzhǐ*). To cease where one ought to cease—this is not yet [true cessation]. One must know that true cessation is fundamentally not so.
When there is no place to cease, only then does one penetrate the principle. This is why the *Shū* (Commentary) clarifies its primordial source, while the *Ní* (Mud) becomes defiled by dust.
Arising from toil, the old official of Lacquer Garden—how could he understand the Way? The void gives birth to white clouds; in vain do you take pride in yourself.

If you can turn things over, you are a Tathāgata; naturally, you leap out from within the pickle jar. The six windows are vast and silent as the autumn moon shines; mountains stretch long and the sea is wide, while heaven is shrouded in mystery.
Fishermen’s songs drift on and off across the reed-flowered marshes. Cease, cease! At this point, one shall forget all worldly emotions.
At Bāngshàn Gǔyuè, he established a dwelling named Xìn'ān (Cave of Faith). When the attendant Zhǎolián came to request a verse, [the Master] said:

"How magnificent is Xìn'ān, who is able to have faith in himself! The sages of antiquity and the worthies of today share one and the same seal. How could this solitary peak, winding and towering, be equaled?"
At leisure: within the blow of the staff and the shout, there is the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). At the eastern edge of the City of Enlightenment, faith does not reach;

wandering throughout the South, there is nowhere to stand. Within the sound of a finger-snap, one finds the path home. The multilayered Dharmadhātu has been entered all at once. When not a single thought arises, there are no floating bubbles.
Vastly empty, the three periods of time are悠 (yōu—vast and indeterminate). Before a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, an iron net is spread; in the ninefold abyss...
Casting the golden hook from the depths. Have you not seen? Your family’s founding patriarch, the Venerable Zhenjing—his transcendent spirit surpassed the long rainbow.
Throughout his life, he skillfully wielded the great drum and banner; with might he cast aside frivolous disputations to restore the True School.

You composed the "Xin'an" [poem], and I have written this verse; its lofty and dignified style remains vividly present. Xiedun has swallowed up Baizhufeng, yet it still releases the waters of the Qinhuai River.
Entering the sea to the east, Zhutang presented this "Half-Room Cottage" to the Abbot Qi while he was writing among the bamboos.
In my dreams, everything was the music of the Heavenly Court; upon waking, I sat in meditation in profound stillness.
It moves; one sees only emerald jade lining the eaves. The wind whistles and the rain whispers; moonlight and celestial radiance wash over the mind and eyes.
The spirit is pure, the bones are pure; all eighty-four thousand pores are permeated with spiritual resonance. Do you not see?
The iron staff of the Dongpo Recluse—sometimes it can produce sound by striking the void. It makes no distinction between lay dwellings and monasteries.
Everywhere one goes, true rewards are realized. Yet, one does not see that ancient master Xiangyan of yore;
with a casual blow, he forgot all that he knew. His vast wealth and glory were utterly bare and naked; it is truly lamentable that there was no place even to plant a single awl.

The Zen of the Tathāgata and the intent of the Patriarchs are like a lightning-fast arrowhead or water cascading down a steep roof. At the top of a hundred-foot pole, one walks with arms dangling free—settle yourself firmly!
Your elder brother’s three-foot beak:
he presents a mustard seed to the Dharma Master and Daoist Lingzang.

Within a single room, there is a single mustard seed; within that mustard seed, there is no place where the great and small *cakra-valaya* mountains are not present, nor are the billions of Mount Sumerus within it.

Lu. Encompassing the boundless seas of fragrant water, as it is in one chamber, so it is in a hundred; though there be a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions, all are perfectly interfused.
The jewel-adorned lands upon the tip of a hair are but its play; like water entering water, space merging with space. You observe the phenomena of the Samādhi of Vision:
Buddhas and sentient beings are fundamentally not two. When the sentiments of sage and ordinary being are exhausted, their essence is suchness (*tathatā*). This is what is called...
It is truly inconceivable: the sparse curtains are rolled high, the mind and its objects are at ease; the round rush mat and curved armrest are as stable as a mountain.
Radiant breezes and clear moons revolve around one another. Who would say this place is not the realm of men?

*Zhu Xuezhai Zeng Shou Shouzuo Daoren* (Presented to the Venerable Head Seat Daoren at Zhu Xuezhai) The Master does not cook dragons; the Master does not roast phoenixes. The Master sits upright in his deep hermitage, boiling balls of snow to provide a Dharma offering.
Upon drinking once, a pure breeze arises from every pore; upon drinking twice, the flesh and bones become crystalline and clear. [From] East Land...

In Western India, he took up the phrase; the jade bell, its resonance yet unfulfilled, still rings with golden strokes. With three-stacked firewood, spring fills the room; who would dare lightly touch the crimson qilin?
In the night that follows, one dreams of ascending the Tuṣita Palace; upon awakening, one stretches out both feet upon the bed.
In the ancient city lies the Bōan Jōshutsu Temple. The Dharma Master named his pavilion "Jōshutsu" (Quiet Retreat). With the single mind unmoving, the myriad functions are at rest;
throughout the three periods of time, it is as tranquil as still water. Before the pavilion, tall bamboos reach toward the heavens in lush green; beneath the bamboos, a clear pond reflects the light.
Cold Jade: The wondrous discourse on Prajñā is fundamentally wordless; what need is there for five thousand scrolls in a precious casket? A favorable breeze blows and breaks the Puṇḍarīka flower;

the provisional and the ultimate are simultaneously and fully revealed. Even stillness does not stand—where could a direction exist? If you have not yet entered this carriage, you must have a sudden flash of realization.
The veteran Chan master Dàshù Xiān built a studio overlooking a great tree; beneath that tree he dwelt in meditation, truly finding the essential flavor.

He directly named his Chan studio after the "Great Tree," and from a thousand li away, one has sought me to transcribe these Chan verses. I ask you: in what year was this tree planted? Its green clouds sweep the ground, its azure...
Lofty and steep, the vast heavens do not allow the sun and moon to descend; Beside the seat, one is startled only by the coming wind and rain.

A single path of cool shade extends together with Ji North; It empties away the mind, intellect, and consciousness of this weary life. The pain of sixty thistle branches remains unrelieved; Reflecting again, from where could another sudden blow be obtained?

Listening to the dream atop a hundred-foot tower, he stretches out his feet; with one pillow, the yellow millet for the midday meal is cooked. In the fifth month of the river city, plum blossoms fall;
the whole world truly becomes a covered banana tree and a deer in a dream. This one melody, that one melody—the rare sound of the celestial drum ceases and returns.
Continued: Closing one eye and opening the other, he rises and further turns his body over. The three periods are vast and empty; the ten thousand realms are at rest.
The six faculties, door by door, are all stilled and returned to their source. What foundation for sleep could there be in the Great Origin?
Yongjia’s vain lodging at Caoxi yields its elegance to the old Muzhou. The spiritual powers of these two sons are truly extraordinary. As soon as the face-bath is finished—
A hand-towel is brought; a bowl of strong tea, as thick as congee.
The Daoist of Huancuilou dwells high upon Huancuilou; from every bamboo window, mountain light floats. White clouds fly at dawn after the overnight rain.
The sky clears; sweet dew pours through the night into the azure jade bowls. The tall forests ride the wind as the surging waves roar. In the midst of summer, it suddenly feels like a clear autumn.

The golden sutras resound clearly from the ocean of the Flower Treasury; the koans are fully understood at the head of the meditation cushion. The youth who traveled south to seek the Dharma withdraws his thoughts and enters;
in a single snap of the fingers, how vast and distant are a thousand kalpas! Returning east, my enthusiasm for the Ruoye River remains unspent; yet, it may still serve its purpose.
I wandered about for a while.

At Listening-to-Pines Hall, when the wind comes, the resonance of the pines is clear; when the wind goes, the resonance ceases. The hall and the pines attain this resonance, such that even in the sixth month, a cool frost is born.
Heavy shadows cover the jade mats; from time to time, the sounds of the *shao* and *gou* music resonate. Since there is no Hanshan in this world, who can appreciate these notes?
I wish to call forth my vermilion strings to harmonize with this primordial sound. Suddenly, I hear the spring from the deep ravine; it flows serenely, resonating with my own heart.
The Wayman of the "Empty-Empty" Room has a single chamber as bare as a hanging gong; he inscribed it with "Empty-Empty," which fits well enough.

Suddenly, thirty-two thousand lion thrones burst forth, yet they are entirely contained within the tip of a hair without the slightest remainder. To call this "existence" is for the Buddha’s face to be produced quite casually.
A hundred uglinesses are called emptiness. The light of the net of imperial jewels is layered upon layer; it is empty yet not empty, existent yet not existent.
The Elephant King turns in circles, the Lion roars; the General of White Battle does not employ weapons, and the Emperor of Great Peace lets his two sleeves hang down.
Yemuyi—whom can it be known with? Beyond the crystal curtain, celestial flowers fly. A pair of white oxen tread upon the cymbals;
a three-faced cat dances the *zhazhi*.

Composed at Guiyun Pavilion: I built this pavilion to wait for returning clouds; when the clouds return, the pavilion stands as it was. The man of the Way is fundamentally without mind, serenely resonating with the clouds.

Along the paths grow noble trees; following the stream, emerald screens are arrayed. When people are at leisure, the scene becomes even more tranquil; the clouds are white and the mountains are naturally green.
Gazing at the mountains while seated upon the pavilion, I part the clouds to bathe in the clear, cool air.

Verdant clouds hang above the long pines and lush bamboo that frame the windows; wondrous peaks, carved like jade, scrape the azure heavens. Verdant clouds separate the days, as the southern breeze fans the heat away.

Cool. The ancient texts of India and the records of Lu fill the bedchamber; the practitioner dwells in seclusion, forgetting ten thousand anxieties. His knowledge and insight radiate as the fragrance of his pores.
When guests come to inquire of the Dharma, he calls for hot water to brew tea. For a moment, the sound of the carriage wheels echoes through the winding sheep’s-gut paths.
Pogam’s Gift to Attendant Hwa Pogam, Pogam, you ask me for a song.
How can one like you, Pogam, not follow the ways of antiquity? The world prizes extravagance and excess;
To cherish integrity and embrace simplicity—would that not be deemed eccentric? Pogam, Pogam, listen to my words: You are a man of the era of Fuxi and Huangdi, clad in hempen garments.
The Heavenly One: having ears, he does not hear the sounds of silk strings and flutes; having eyes, how could he know the nobility of carriages and official robes?
Low enough to burrow through, high enough to nest in—where is there no mugwort for a head-covering? With a vessel of mud for a cup, one is naturally satisfied;

with a clod of earth for a drum and a basket of grass for a mallet, what need is there for instruction? At the end of the year, suddenly falsehoods arise; the Seven Apertures split apart as Chaos was pierced. Sometimes...
Drawing the sword, he cuts through the wheel of wind; startled, the clay ox rises to fight, its horns broken. Sing this song, and let no one laugh at you;
who among the great void or small void can truly know it? At the end of all things, nothing can be relied upon; early in the day, the hundred birds come to carry away the flowers.
Zhitang presents this to Attendant Yun.
Zhitang, Zhitang, you requested a song from me; though I was asked three times without ceasing, how can I simply remain still?
It would be better to stop right now, so as not to stir up wind and waves on level ground. Zhitang, Zhitang, listen to my words: when a river is already swelling, how could one...
Having attained it, the waters flow backward through the Three Gorges and lose themselves in the Nine Abysses. Its surging torrents and its tranquil depths are all this same water.

Whether moving or still, who is the creator? Whether coiled or uncoiling, it remains vast and luminous. In the vast emptiness of the empty chamber, white light arises; the expansive spiritual mechanism penetrates into numinous awakening.
Since the characteristic of movement is fundamentally non-existent, how could there be stillness? It is like twisting straw rope to bind a mountain ghost—useless effort. Copper sand...
The bowl is filled to the brim with oil; this very one cuts off heaven and earth. Even the mark of stillness does not exist—how could there be movement?
A hundred flowers compete in the dream of the spring breeze. At this moment, the house-swallow of Mount Dongshan opens its wings: "Luo-lo, she calls out; Luo-lo, she sends her off."
I sing this song as the clear night draws to a close; all sounds are hushed and my spirit is at ease. Who is it that parts the clouds and lets forth a long, piercing cry?
A single note bursts forth among the thousand forests.

The Head Seat Chengtian Yi’s style name was Mugu (Wood Old Man). Songyue Weng further called him Gangzhong (Middle of Firmness) and sought my correction. I said, “Gangzhong is his courtesy name; Mugu is his style name. For him, I composed this song:

木翁木翁 木之為物 其性本剛 不假磨礪 自然成器 剛中剛中 剛之為德 其體至中 不假矯揉 自然合道 Mugu, Mugu! As for the nature of wood, Its essence is fundamentally firm. Without needing polishing, It naturally becomes a vessel. Gangzhong, Gangzhong! As for the virtue of firmness, Its substance is the ultimate center. Without needing artificiality, It naturally accords with the Way.
Why does this old man act so woodenly? His mouth cannot speak, yet his intent is most extraordinary. With a single stroke he cuts off the sentiments of both ordinary and sage;
splitting rocks and crumbling cliffs, he reveals his true wind-bone. When the moon over the pines sees him, it calls him "Gangzhong" (Stiff Center);

when the various quarters see him, they call him "Moweng" (Wooden Old Man). One is his name, the other his title; in his lofty detachment, he is surely the leader among all eminent men. Have you not seen? Mow...
The Bhikṣuṇī manifests a thousand, ten thousand, and a hundred million transformations; her many glorious reputations shake metal and stone. The two origins are neither different nor the same;
in the ultimate sense, she truly becomes a "white-handed thief."
A Single Tree Presented to Attendant Linji: The tree stands alone;
it covers heaven and earth without exception. Its Jambu-river gold radiates more brightly than the sun and moon;
Without day or night, fragrant winds blow. In the midst of the vast heat of the three summer months, it sprinkles ice and snow; Every pore of the body is cooled and refreshed.
Chè: The scorching heat of the five turbidities stifles people to death; in my desolation, I have no other recourse but to speak for them.
A solitary peak is presented to Attendant Āṅ:
Myriad mountains and peaks stretch across a jade table; a single point of blue-green shell emerges from mid-heaven. The white clouds do not produce the sound of rain.
Qian. Only the warbling birds call out to one another. Who can sit and cut off the very summit? Eyes empty across the four seas, there is neither spring nor autumn.
The azure void and the red dust are utterly severed from one another. Do not let the leaf of the vegetable garden lightly follow the current.

It presses down upon the axis of Kun and stabilizes the Southern Pole. The Five Peaks must be made level, yet they cannot be leveled. One must immediately topple the entangling vine-stake, lest it cause Heaven—
Huajie placed it in his bosom.
Wusheng presented it to the Abbot Duzang.
Where does the Way-man Wusheng come from? He entreats me with longing for a song of non-birth. Since birth is fundamentally non-existent, how could there be a song?
There is. One who denies fire as being the son of water and stirs up clear waves—do you not see? When the ocean of awakening is limpid and perfect, a single bubble arises;

the four modes of birth and the nine realms of existence strike against one another. If you know that the essence of the bubble is originally empty, only then do you realize the true teaching of non-arising.
When truth does not exist, falsehood is also empty; the billion peaks of Mount Sumeru are toppled, and the ten directions are instantly extinguished beneath. Three.
The Buddhas of the world leave no tracks; all is silent and vast, clear and bright. Turning the pivot of the profound mystery—how magnificent!
Closing one's eyes in a dream to leap across the Yellow River; opening both eyes wide upon the long bed.

A fish in the Eastern Sea struck by a single blow, casually leaping out through a thousandfold net. The lame tortoise and the blind turtle know nothing of it; even Śakra and the Asuras lose heart in terror.
Angry yet not angry, joyful yet not joyful—laughing to death the seven virtuous women of the charnel ground. A hundred kinds of offerings fail to satisfy their desires;
they stubbornly demand a rootless tree. A-he-he! Do you understand? Upon the sprout-less branch, the spring breeze abounds.
A bewildered fellow clutching the head of a dead snake; a live hawk released by the immortal Śāṇakavāsin. Singing the song of non-arising, he plays the Shaolin melody;
plucking the stringless lute, its sound is naturally sufficient. A clay ox roars, shattering the mist of the emerald pool; lotuses are planted upon the rock, their stalks as pure as jade.
A White Ox Presented to the Master of Mount Chang:
The white of this white ox is as white as snow; its temperament is utterly distinct from that of ordinary oxen. With a single plow, it has tilled the empty fields of the kalpas;
its four hooves are well-accustomed to traversing steep precipices. Lan’an and Xiangyan were praised as skilled herders—how could they have failed to distinguish between the plains and the peaks?

In the deep valley, the nostrils reach toward the heavens and cannot be pierced; though the horns are long, they cannot avoid bumping against things to the east and west. Having grazed for a long time, one eventually forgets them;

with water sufficient and grass sufficient, the mountain stream breeze is cool. Within the burning house, he deliberates on how to entice his children; at the four crossroads, the canopies and carriages are how brilliantly resplendent!
Recorded Sayings of Master Liaoyuan, Volume Six.
Recorded Sayings of Master Liaoyuan, Volume Seven:
Verses and Hymns.
Compiled by the student-monks Ruxian, Yuangao, Huirang, and others.
The Celestial Seal is revealed to the attendant Jue Tian:

the sky is cloudless and the ocean waves are stilled. The myriad phenomena of the universe are all marked by this single seal; the conceptual measures of both sages and ordinary beings cannot fathom it.

It shines forth, shattering the gateway of the face; one should have confidence in this oneself. The mechanism of the Iron Ox has always been thus. To accept it upon hearing the words is not merely superficial;
its influence throughout Wu and Yue remains to this day. Who understands that being born together is to die together?
Sealing mud, sealing water, and sealing space alike—two, three, four, seven, all have hidden their traces. To meet the dark with the bright is nothing but child’s play. It sweeps past the tiger.
The cave and the palace of Māra; the seal of space, the seal of mud, and the seal of water. When guest is fully guest and host is fully host, the escape from Caoxi is not yet remarkable;
only when Luopo is captured can one truly rejoice. The seal of the chamber, the seal of water, and the seal of mud:
the jade dog barks at night, the golden rooster crows. The purple sash is brilliant, revealing sun and moon; the golden insignia is indistinct, coiling like a rainbow.
The Patriarch has no transmission and I have no bestowal; coming and going, my empty hands are sufficient.
Should you meet someone who asks for a talisman to protect the body, I would simply strike them across the jaw and shut their mouth.
The attendant Xezilu extinguished the Linji lineage;
the Yellow River’s nine bends dared not flow east. Dongshan cast out the secret signal:
an iron snake and a painted phoenix coil through the clear sky. How laughable and how tragic—this dross of the land! Look directly at the pivot of the moment.
Underfoot. Striking away the eyebrows, ten thousand matters cease. It draws laughter from onlookers until their voices fail. If the ancestral wind is like this, how can it not perish?
This mind should be told to a blind donkey. When told to the blind donkey, the donkey does not listen; a shout bursts forth, casting down the moon upon a thousand crags.
To the East, I offer white silk as a gift to Attendant Sheng:
the golden cock flaps its wings as the sun rises over Fusang. The myriad nations are bright and clear as heaven and earth open. Did not the transmission from Shaoshi Mountain come with intention?
Alas, those of later generations who wish to see it find no gate. Five leaves and a thousand lamps illuminate China; within the clarity of this single color—what [is there to seek]?
Brilliantly radiant! Once again, one must penetrate the profound barrier from above. The heavy darkness of kalpas is utterly dispersed; the azure sea is limpid, illuminating the empty chamber.
No phenomenon can escape its shadow and substance. One cannot help but laugh at the old Zhaozhou of yore: before his eyes, everything was nothing but Jinzhou lacquer.
Siyuan presents this to Attendant Chuan:
What is there to say about the successive transmission from patriarch to patriarch? For as long as earth and heaven endure, it shall never be severed.

Yet, without cause, it was extinguished within the jaws of a blind donkey, adding nails and wedges to the lineage of descendants. Who is it that extracts this wedge when it seeks to emerge? This is the secret manual of the immortals, transcending—

Transcending the subtle: the mountains are green and yellow, the sun and moon grow old; before the house and behind the house, the seasonal flowers are sparse. It is transmitted, it is distant—between you and me;
thinking yet not thinking, how many times do we perceive the subtle turning point?

To Dongyun, presented to Attendant Hai: The mind-ground of a Way-person is like clouds and the sea; Moving with the wind through the void, it is entirely without hindrance. At dawn, a single expanse stretches across the eastern sun;
Ten thousand *li* of dense shadows cover the heavens beyond. In the east, it is the east—how could one fix upon a direction? Rolling up or spreading out, appearing or disappearing, all are thus.
It is perfectly so. Nailed down and suspended. Nanyang points directly to the essential framework of the school. With eyes, what monk would not see it?
Failing to realize this mind, one is dazzled by external circumstances; chasing after objects, one loses the true intent and is led astray.
The nature of consciousness is turbulent, changing by the thousands every day. I wish for everyone to be like this cloud: neither rejoicing in praise nor resenting abuse. When moved...
Free from worldly striving, tranquil and without abiding; light as a breeze, serene, and transcending the dust of sensory objects. Clouds, oh clouds, how wondrous you are!
If people were truly like clouds, they would have few afflictions. When the time comes, they would fulfill their purpose as sweet rain, washing away the heat and dust to nourish all that is withered.
"Beyond things, he demonstrates the Way;

yet the attendant says the Way is not beyond things, nor is that which is beyond things the Way. To speak of its essentials: who can reach its profound depths? Nanquan brushed his sleeves and walked away;
Mazu saw it exactly as it is. When the wooden leaves have fallen and the four mountains turn yellow, the golden rooster beats its wings a thousand times.
The River Dawns.

Zongyuan showed the world that before the heavens and earth were divided, who could be called the Patriarch? Echoes are received and emptiness is inherited from antiquity to the present. Both sides—India and China—are thus.
Look! The sun over Fusang stands at its zenith at midday. Before the time of Wei-yin and after the time of Wei-yin—every step falls upon the descendants.
It is no cause for wonder that the colt tramples it to death; it is only when the blind donkey extinguishes it that one can feel pity.
The sun may grow cold and the moon may grow hot; how can this matter be explained to others? The heart’s concern is truly like the cold plum blossom, which holds all the spring within itself.
The light radiates and flows forth everywhere.
In the Hall of Silence, Master Bian is presented with the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa*:
"One silence opens the gateway throughout the ancient and the modern; in every atom and every world-system, the Flower-Scattering Goddess understands how to follow along."
Wrong! He splits open the void and repairs it with a twist; when the clouds over the eight directions have vanished, the clear day is at leisure.
With the sparse curtain half-rolled back, the autumn mountains arrive. The Way-man has a mouth, yet hangs it on the wall; sitting, he listens as the myriad phenomena present the profound pivot.
Iron horses neigh in the wind, wooden cocks crow; wild waters flow on naturally, and Hua laughs to himself. The blue-eyed barbarian monk nods his head in secret. Wondrous Virtue is empty.
I have never understood this before.
*Xuechuang’s Song for the Abbot Ying*, presented at Shuangfeng.
*Xuechuang’s Song for Baohua*. Two mouths, not a single tongue—what can one do with these two elders?
Cast aside both the prolix and the direct; push open the pine-window and invite the bright moon.
A heron flies into the reeds; a single expanse of pure light faces the vast void. Do not ask how deep Shaolin is; do not ask how towering the Snow Mountains are.
When the yams emerge from the fire and their fragrance wafts forth, what else could one know beyond a full meal? The snowy window sees me.
Having spoken these words, he nodded his head, raised his brow, and said, "Yes, yes. Not a single character was written upon the full sheet of paper that arrived.
When you meet people on the road ahead, do not speak of this by mistake. Presented by Daming to Attendant Tao.
The Great Encompassment has no exterior; it is identical to the Small. Discerning the finest details of autumn hair, the illumination is never forgotten.

Being great yet without greatness, luminous yet without luminosity, one need not hesitate to tread upon the aperture that pierces through to heaven. Once this celestial aperture is opened, the nine realms are vast and clear, free from even a speck of dust.
Reflecting back on Longtan’s act of extinguishing the paper candle, the shimmering light of the Milky Way shines brilliantly, its radiance manifest both near and far.

The commentaries are incinerated and the sub-commentaries consumed by fire; what can be said of a gnat trying to understand the light of a firefly? Seated atop a solitary peak, the True Command is put into action;

the blind staff and the blinding lash are truly but a trivial matter. The radiance of the Way-man is neither small nor great; it illuminates the past and soars through the present, forever ending the night.
When the nine suns have been shot down until not one remains, he grasps the thorny plum and swallows it whole.
"No-self presents my treasury-master to me;
since I myself am no-self, who is for whom? Grasping the iron flute, I blow it freely in all directions. With one song of Yunmen, I strike out the five-colored marrow of the phoenix.
With the five ranks of Dongshan, I shatter the bright moon pearl of the black dragon. As for those who go forward..."
The cat catches the mouse; yet that which comes back is like looking down a well at a donkey. It is already glowing red. Strike once more:
sparks fly within the land of the Great Tang, and Silla burns away the Yellow Gate’s beard.

The Ocean of Nature bestows upon the Record-keeper Ming the realization that the ocean of awakening is clear and perfect, its nature pure and pristine. Deeply still, its cold radiance soaks into the reflections in space. When a single wave stirs, ten thousand waves follow;

thus there arise the six realms of ordinary beings alongside the four classes of sages. I observe that movement and stillness are fundamentally without action; it is only because delusion is able to give rise to them.
Delusory awakening—awakening to the fact that delusion is fundamentally empty, one penetrates the original reality. A single path of void luminosity shines forth spontaneously and expansively.
Do you not see? At Vulture Peak, the artifice of holding up the flower was exhausted; at Shaoshi, the single transmission once again forged the seal. At Sanjiao, the "iron ox" device was set in vain.
Linru’s total presentation is still but a prelude; at Nantang in the fifth month, the pines blow a cool breeze. As cups of tea overflow, the fragrance permeates every pore.
When guests come to ask for instruction, do not open your mouths; there is only the staff and the shout—nothing to deliberate upon.

Xiuyan’s Gift to Chief Seat Ting: A thousand crags rise majestically beyond all things; Looking down upon heaven and earth, how small they appear! Flowers scatter, yet find no path to reach the heavens;
Only the green mountains are permitted to encircle them. The green mountains do not hinder the flying white clouds; How could the vermilion cliffs follow the spring?
The wind grows old. I intended to ask how matters are within the mountain crags; at dawn’s arrival in spring, I hear the crows crying.
From within folly, I present this to the Chief Librarian Zhe:
before the time of Wei-yin, there was no orthodox phrase. From where could one establish these idle names? Within folly is wisdom; within wisdom is folly.

The fool: the meaning lies beyond the words, and the words lie beyond the meaning. At Mahākāśyapa’s closing of his room, opening the mouth was difficult; at Vimalakīrti’s single silence, the mind was naturally at ease. Both Qi Guo and Li Zhu failed;
Wangxiang attained it spontaneously, like one who is dull and stubborn. How much better is this dullness and stubbornness! When weariness comes, one awakens and collapses with one's clothes on;

the snoring is like thunder, and though called, there is no response. Only when the eyes are opened— *Note: This passage is a poetic commentary on the famous encounter between Vimalakīrti and Mañjuśrī, contrasting the silence of Mahākāśyapa with the eloquence of Vimalakīrti, and ultimately praising the state of non-conceptual realization.*
When the great dawn of heaven arrives, one points to the east and west while speaking of the south and north; hungry, one buys a sesame cake to eat.
Ultimately, what is this matter of folly? One must wait until the future to ask Maitreya.

Leyuan’s Gift to Chan Head Seat Chang: The pleasures of this world are but form and sound; In this single hermitage, so cold and desolate, who would harbor lingering attachment? A thousand peaks and ten thousand crags tower in wintry green;
The man of the Way attains them, and both his eyes grow clear. When the eyes are joyful, the mind is likewise joyful; With mind empty and eyes empty, there is joy.
What attachment? Non-attachment is as joyful as empty space, which is itself empty. Within emptiness, flowers bloom and fall; flowers bloom and fall through spring and autumn.
The myriad affairs of the world are empty and vast. A single hermitage, cool and simple, remains just so. Where can one seek the joy that is beyond joy?
This is the delight of Zen, this is the bliss of the Dharma. The mouth cannot speak it, but the heart speaks for itself. The wooden man strokes—
The palms sing the "Yangchun" melody; the stone maiden holds her flute and harmonizes with the flowing stream. Beat after beat, high and then low:
the jade hare grinds the elixir, the golden cock crows. Drawing forth the wine of Qingyuan and the Bai family, the clear tax-master becomes drunk as spring mud.
The Moon-Mirror is presented to Monk Man:
A great round mirror flies forth from the azure sea; it swallows and eclipses heaven and earth without a trace remaining. Though the Holy Mountain pointed it out, it was not yet the whole truth;
only when Dongping shattered it did it become truly worthy of its name. When both light and mirror have perished, what thing is this? The Śūnyatā-deva is revealed.
Wind and Bone. When Chiyou fled in retreat, Xuanyuan was startled; through all time, who would dare to treat this lightly?
Xiangyan presents these words to Head Seat Zhi:
"The sandalwood fragrance fills the crags and valleys; the orchid’s bloom and the calamus’s beauty share the same rich scent. Ten thousand trees and a thousand forests vie to offer their tribute."
In response: When the sense of smell is silent and the mind is naturally satisfied, the practitioner sits within my cave; from every pore of his body, fragrant winds blow forth.
The eighty-four thousand oceans of bodily attributes interpenetrate one another in perfect harmony.

When a single hair-tip is raised, all hairs gather there; each emits fragrant light, lush and moist like emerald clouds. Without ever leaving the pores of Samantabhadra, who could say that this is not the Mind?
There is no path for hearing to enter.
Meng’an bestowed a robe upon an attendant before even the hut was built;
he first dreamed it, and then the dream occurred. Dreaming of entering Huaxu to select beams and rafters, once the hut was completed, both dream and awakening were equally vast and indistinct.
Indeed. Throughout the eight directions and the ten voids, all is vast and empty. Whether raising the fist or pointing a finger, whether deceiving gods or shouting at ghosts—it is all in vain.
When the golden cock crows atop the jade balustrade, the mountains are mountains and the waters are waters.

Chun-ting shows the longevity of the Abbot; eight thousand springs, eight thousand autumns. In a single instant, ten thousand ages—how utterly vast! The green screens hold the breeze as the night air grows solemn;

the crimson curtains roll back from the rain as the morning countenance is fresh. How could the teachings of Ji-bei have been obtained through artificial fabrication? Mu-zhou’s words were merely intended to bring about mutual realization.
Complete. Since Huangbo’s staff-head has already revealed the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, what further use is there for the three punches that struck Daoyu so painfully in the ribs?
It is simply a case of the mulberry branch being hit by an arrow or the willow trunk exuding sap. What need is there to speak of carrying water and seeking fire under the moon and amidst the smoke?
With a single flip of the body, one casts it across the five heavens; when skin and flesh are stripped away, the reality is seen.
Jambudvīpa still lies on the southern edge of the sea.
My ancient sound is a gift for the Abbot Zengshao;
it is not the melody of this present age. Once Master Ma plucked it, and a pure breeze filled the forest slopes.
With no strings, it is difficult to raise the hand; when hearing ceases, the mind is naturally satisfied. In the meditation window after the spring rain, the distant mountains remain lush and green.
Zhongshan presents this to Attendant Ying: "Towering and rugged, it supports the void; blue-green and dark, how solitary and precarious! Neither leaning nor biased, it reveals the One."
The pivot. Aside from this stubborn rock, no one knows it. The famished man of Shouyang was skilled at gathering mugwort;
how could he have known that heavenly flowers were flying by the side of the cliff where Śūnyatā was born? Alas! For a thousand or ten thousand years, to whom shall it return?
The Great Void, the Great Void—no gate, no bolt to lock it. Strike it and it rings out with a *pò-pò* sound. The myriad phenomena of the universe listen intently;
the stone man and the wooden man both respond in unison. The golden crow rises in the east, the hare falls in the west; the celestial wind blows the flowers down.
Fragrant rain. The practitioner sits in meditation, silent and unmoving. With a smile, he watches Mount Sumeru dance in unison. My true body merges with the great void;
utterly spotless and pure, it is free from all confusion and clutter. Within the flash of lightning, I swiftly turn my body; amidst the sparks of stone, I stride and leap at will.
Failing to clarify this principle is merely empty prattle; relying on substantial talk makes it difficult to uphold. Directly toward—
Within emptiness, reality is found; only then does one know that outside of reality, there is fundamentally no emptiness. Emptiness and reality—now they have returned to their ancient state.
What need is there to count appearances or non-appearances? Speak this for the wise and intelligent to know: break it apart and then gather it back together once more.

The empty crags, the empty crags are wonderful; how wonderful are the empty crags! Having dwelt here for many years, there is no affliction. The meditation cushions and Zen boards are entirely forgotten;

with my bamboo staff and straw sandals, I follow the shifting of circumstances. Sometimes I sit—what need is there to choose? What does it matter about the Shaolin barbarian Bodhidharma? In a single thought, all is complete.
Transcending vast eons past, one is unaware as the sun’s orb passes overhead. At times I stand; the colors of the water and the light of the mountains merge in tranquility.
At dawn, a clear breeze strikes my face; passing clouds bring a fine rain that wets my robes. At times I walk; a single slice of sunset stretches across the heavens beyond.
Trusting my own will, I am unaware of the distance to the mountains; as I climb, I may even contend with monkeys and tigers. There is...

At that time, lying down, I let a single moment pass with my head resting on the winding stream. Unable to bear the passionate *huáng lìliú* [cuckoo], several times it startled all my good dreams to pieces.
"How empty the crags! How empty the crags! Flowers fall across the ground, yet no one sweeps them away. When people are empty, phenomena are empty; phenomena being empty, they too are empty.
How can this be explained to the worldly crowd?

The Snowy Mountains encompass the earth, with snow three feet deep filling the heavens. A thousand peaks and ten thousand mountains are all one color. Samantabhadra has lost his fragrant elephant king;
he tramples through empty space but cannot find him. Six-flowered snowflakes fly into a silver bowl; the jade groves and crystal trees radiate light.
Linglong: Amidst layered cliffs and deep valleys, fragrant herbs flourish. A white ox lies peacefully, forgetting east and west. At midnight, Gautama leaped over the city wall;

shaking his head, he did not look back at the station of the Golden Wheel. Having cast off his imperial robes to trade for a skin garment, he turned his back on the human world, no longer knowing where he was.
The Wayman Tending the Ox tends the ox as if tending a stone; Without the application of whip or rope, effort is ultimately saved. Suddenly, the entire world is revealed in its vast clarity;
Tranquil and empty, it returns to silent stillness. Sometimes there is a single melody drifting east and west across the stream; On the long embankment, green grass mingles with mist.
Vast and boundless; among the myriad affairs of the human world, not a single thing enters my ears. Sitting upon the ground, I listen to the yellow oriole’s song.
The ocean of emptiness and the ocean of awakening are infinitely vast and silent; the white sun rises in the east and the moon sets in the west. The azure dragon sleeps soundly, never to awaken.
He knows. The divine pearl beneath his chin illuminates the vast void. With a single stroke of his hand, it shatters into a hundred fragments; leaping up, he is already upon the back of Mount Sumeru.
Unstained by the clear waves, his intent is naturally extraordinary. To others, there is naturally one who loves such a person of realization.
I myself tend my water buffalo. From birth, I have tended it alone. Since the whip and rope are already in my hands, I need not worry about it bumping into things to the east or west.
On the plateau above, the spring grasses are green; below the plateau, the spring waters are lush. Following what is appropriate without seeking much, I am satisfied with having enough to eat.
Thus for thirty years he was nurtured until he was thoroughly matured. Though there were the crops of others, he showed no desire for them.
His coat color had gradually transformed, and his head and horns remained perfectly intact. Since he did not oppose the will of men, nor did he trespass upon the fields of others.
The three months of spring have ended the farming labors; along the single embankment, willows shroud in mist. What need is there for man or ox? May we thus live out our natural lifespans.

Within the ocean of awakening, empty bubbles are clear and perfect; when a single bubble arises, its arising and ceasing have no source, leaving all naturally void and vast. In this expansive clarity, the ten directions are fully revealed.

Emptiness: the four modes of birth and the nine realms of existence are uprooted together with their roots. Emptiness is not itself empty; it is free from "mine-ness. Within the vast expanse, one enters the humble courtyard.
At dawn, the golden rooster brushes the branches of the Fusang tree; at night, the jade hare grinds the coral trees.

The emptiness within a bubble is a bubble within emptiness; stirred by conditions, they rise and fall. This rising and falling has no inherent nature from the beginning. The six giant turtles—[one...]
Draughted by the golden hook, I opened this chamber and inscribed it myself. Inscribing with the emptiness of a bubble—how could this deceive?
The sparse curtains are half-rolled, the incense smoke curls in blue spirals; the three periods of time are vast and silent, leaving only the reflections in the mirror.
A Gift to Lu Pingyuan, Also Shown to My Nephew Qin and Other Sons:
For one year, a foul wind has blown across the world; for three years, my traces have been like a whirling tumbleweed. Master Lu Pingyuan’s path of humanity and our bond of affection are deep;
he invited me to build a dwelling within his estate. Qin was able to oversee the construction, managing the transport of grain and labor. Diligent and steadfast, he forgot his own weariness.
In autumn and winter, the pickle jar is not full and the millet does not fill the granary; with smoking staffs and rain-cloaks, how weary they wander!
Have you not seen how Xiong Feng’s daily activities were the same as the common folk, yet at Daopei, acorns and chestnuts became a grove of Chan monks?
And have you not seen the old man of Yangqi, who traded his fields for his rice, suddenly upholding the Linji school? I am now old and weary of all things; my eyes grow dim and my head...
I am white-haired and both ears are deaf; I do not lament like a commoner over the end of my path. I do not seek to have my reputation spread among princes and dukes;

I only wish that the Imperial transformation may permeate all, that the Buddha-way may flourish, that seasons may be harmonious and harvests bountiful, that boats and carriages may pass freely, and that all things—flying, hiding, moving, or stationary—may find a peaceful end.
Let every hill and every mountain be a celestial palace.
The World-Honored One sending the Abbot Shouzang was merely entrusting him with the golden robe; why did Kāśyapa need to reach the flagpole?

How joyful it is that at Fengtai there is no giving or receiving, sparing Kaifu from the embarrassment of being deceived. For the young phoenix, the scenery before its eyes is unique; for the mosquito, the realm is within its own brow.
The realm is vast; with a single blow, empty space is reduced to dust. Yet he returns to level ground to roll forth waves.

To send off Attendant Ying back to Zhangjiao—this Chan practitioner has been by my side for three years. Grasping the one move prior to the trigger, there is no need for many words upon arriving home.

Speech: With palms joined, one knows only to listen as it is proclaimed. A pillar is shattered by a swift thunderclap and a startling, scorching roar; a long sword leaning against the heavens emits a cold radiance.
Suddenly, the mountains collapse and the brooks overflow; only then does one believe that the dragon hides in shallow waters.
The phrase "the Abbot Huìzàng holds [you] up beyond the extraordinary" is not difficult to grasp as an extraordinary holding-up.
Before one’s eyes, Mount Ayodhyā (Iron Ring Mountain) is toppled; the nostrils of the Patriarchs have long been pierced.
What hardness is there in the skulls of the non-Buddhists? Sentient and insentient are both delusions; phenomena are not phenomena, for they are of themselves...
Chengxian: "Upon a single hair-tip, there are three thousand worlds; with whom do you know how to interact?

Furthermore, the Librarian Jizhao is silent and still, his single thought unborn as he penetrates the ten voids. As soon as one distinguishes between stillness and agitation, they are vastly different. Within the room of Vimalakīrti, the golden light...
Manifest: Before the Hall of Good Dharma, jeweled nets unfurl. As soon as you lift your foot, you must transcend all limits. Once you have reached home, why bother asking about the journey?
Right now, the six faculties have attained rest and renewal; the meditation board and the grass mat are entirely as they should be.
The Great Master Zhinpa’s palanquin was sent back to Putuo;

the *pingga* bird flies out from the eastern sea-gate. As the sun shines upon Fusang, the myriad lands turn crimson. His Dharma-body remains as it is seen this very day; the sound of the tide is still the same as of old.
With no four walls to limit the heavens, how magnificent is his mind! Though three *kalpas* of *asaṃkhyeya* aeons have passed, his karma is exhausted.
Self-empty. The true path of the youth’s southern pilgrimage remains; with staff in hand, he finds the spring breeze wherever he goes.

As he sends Master Kong up to Mount Jinshan, they sit together in virtue atop the wondrous peak. The mountain is naturally lofty and cold, the water flows of its own accord; throughout the three periods of time, no external objects arise.

Silence: ten thousand functions vanish together, the single mind rests. A boat lies across the wild crossing; the tide’s sound fills the night. The constellations shift as the autumn moon ascends the Milky Way.
The shadow of the golden staff flickers, shaking heaven and earth; Hidden scales surge upward, struck by the hook that catches the giant tortoise.
Answering Weiyou’s bamboo gift, I transmit the *Record of the Transmission of the Lamp*:
How easily can the true lamp beyond kalpas be transmitted? It should only be extinguished within the mouth of a blind donkey. Try exploring the profound depths from the Seven Buddhas;
It is fit to distinguish the orthodox and the biased for all schools. Who would have been startled by the exposure of the patterns? In this shared wind, one realizes the Way for oneself.
The sentiment is complete. Shoushan had eyes but could not recognize characters; he kept them by a bright window to accompany his twilight years.
Following the rhyme of my dharma-brother Songyue, I send this to Jing, the *karmadāna*, as he returns home to visit Longxiang:
In terms of meritorious achievement, you hold several moves ahead of me. You alone know that true joy lies in having no seeking. Among the old masters of Jiangxi, who is not [a fellow traveler]?
The horse. The surviving clansmen of the village are surnamed Liu. When raising this topic, it is rarely heard; when meeting a tiger on the road, do not speak of the ox by the window.
Only Xinghua should be able to prolong the encounter with the enemy; he is not like those children rolling a silk ball.
Seeing off Master Jingzang as he travels to Zhejiang:
I forget words, and you too must forget words. Shattering the Three Mysteries into two sides, opening one’s mouth is enough to swallow Buddhas and Patriarchs;
turning the body about is truly capable of benefiting humans and devas. Outside the mechanisms of the Three Vehicles’ teachings, at the tips of the hundred grasses—
The essence and its function are complete. Raise up the eyes of the monk on pilgrimage; north and south of the great river, his inspiration flows freely.
Sending off Attendant Ren to Mount Jing:

He does not go to Yangzhou to listen to the falling plum blossoms, but thinks only of washing his eyes to behold the total presentation. Atop the mountain, the vermilion-tailed fish seizes the clouds.
Depart! Yellow dust at the bottom of the well mists the bright day. When noble understanding is not yet eliminated, one remains stuck in the shell;
when ordinary sentiment is exhausted, one naturally forgets the trap. Cast aside all five flavors from every quarter; flowers fill the thousand crags, and water fills the streams.
In the same rhyme as "The Wordless Beyond the World" by Jiangxin:

The world beyond the world is not easily exhausted. Within sameness there is difference; within difference there is sameness. The myriad functions do not fall into the realms of sense-objects, sense-bases, or consciousness.
In a single thought-moment, one suddenly transcends emptiness, the provisional, and the middle. Even a stubborn rock may at times nod its head; In the great void, there is no trace to be found.
Description: Opening wide the doors and windows, he has returned; though we meet, it is as if still on a distant peak.
This is the mountain-dwelling verse of Venerable Lingcheng, requested by Treasure Master Bao to be translated into Western [language]:
"The Westward Transmission has no intention to speak with others; when the plum blossoms open, the year changes of its own accord. These three matters of the tattered robe are truly worthy of praise.
His body has a single head of white hair reaching his shoulders; he gathers fallen leaves to fuel the tea cauldron, and sits leaning against a *pūtuka* cushion facing a waterfall.
Both the mundane and the supramundane are but dreams; who can debate what lies after death or before birth?
Following the rhyme of Elder Songyue, I send this off for the Venerable Librarian of Chengtian Monastery as he pays homage to the Patriarchs:
What remains unfinished before one’s eyes must be brought to completion; once the ground of the mind is clarified, what further is there to seek?
Last night the Bāshé swallowed the fragrant elephant; this morning at Shaanfu, the iron ox is bathed. A person under Mazu—how truly remarkable! Thus spoke Toudi of Tongcheng.
Glistening and smooth. At this very moment, no one raises this talk; having gazed upon the green mountains until one’s own hair turns white.
To the Chan practitioner Yin, I present the *Lotus Sūtra*:

the seven parables and three turnings are all gathered within a single silence. No one can reach its deepest, most remote recesses; the provisional skillful means may be directed toward the realm before sound.
The True Aspect—how could it be sought upon paper? Bodhisattvas surge upward as the golden earth splits; devas and dragons pay homage as precious flowers float.
The fire-housed dwelling is suddenly opened to reveal the treasury of radiance; hand in hand, we ride together upon the ox of the open ground.
The subtle truth of East and West is not transmitted;
the ready-made case is also manifestly clear. Was Muzhou merely carrying a wooden board? How could Huangbo be made to carry it on his lower shoulder?
On the road to Nanpu, the orioles and flowers fill the spring; on West Mountain, the mist and rain are emerald green.
Reaching the heavens. Debts from all quarters have been fully repaid. A single melody of pine wind at one’s ears.
Sent to the Venerable Wan as he departs for Siming; also addressed to Cuisan, Dapao, and Daobian.
The clouds of Wu have passed, yet his resolve remains unextinguished. He now longs to enter the sea to behold Penglai. Upon the diamond rock, the kalaviṅka bird...
Behold! Before the Jade Bench Peak, the stupa opens. To inquire of the Dharma and the mind—how magnificent! Seek the Master and seek your companions; do not linger.
Entrust this to you to tell the old man of Cuiyan: let him keep his eyebrows planted beneath his chin.
Seeing off Master Lin as he travels to Mount Ming and Mount Tiantai to visit his parents:
Turning over the veil before the birth of father and mother, The journey of visiting teachers is complete;

Myriad dharmas do not depart from the seal of the mind-ground— Fine mountains are all right here at the edge of one’s own house. The Qín River has waters that reach the Three Isles; In Fangguǎng there is no cloud to obscure the view.
Five days. The autumn fills the heavens and earth; the seasonal winds are favorable. Roll up your robes and return, catching the eastbound ships of Zhejiang.
Following the rhyme of Master Songyue, I see off Chief Seat Zhu of Yuwang as he returns to Min.
Within the ancient mountains of Moshan there dwells this gentleman; with his brandished halberd, he can cause the Buddha-sun to shine once more. His breast and mind are naturally empty now.
Ancient! Why labor over comparing lengths and dimensions? What a marvelous Dharma-gate for planting true seeds! It can serve as a bridge across the evil realms.
Though the price of the rush-sandals is high, no one buys them; he takes up his rattan staff once more and returns to his native land.
In the same rhyme, I send off Chan Master Shu to pay homage at the stupa of Hongzhi, the Great White Elder and Patriarch of the Dongxia school:
A single pivot does not fall into the midst of the orthodox or the biased; The sheep’s-gut path and bird-track open the mysterious way.
Under the white sun and blue sky, the black wind beats; Transcending past and present, it can clearly be seen— The forging and smelting of both ordinary and sage beings is its very essence.
There is no merit. After nirvana, there are the marks of a great man. The mountain is cold, the clouds are chill, and the moon fills the sky.
The iron drum returns to its root;

the foundation of the stupa was originally non-existent—where could it return? Turning back one's head, all human affairs are seen as unreal. On all eight sides it is brilliant and transparent, without a seam.

A fissure. The ten voids are vast and expansive, yet inherently solitary and precarious. Where the flowers of emptiness adhere, the True Dharma is proclaimed. The iron drum conceals its transformative mechanism according to the times.
Before being buried in death, one is interred while alive; laughing, one watches the setting sun on the horizon of heaven grow faint.

In response to the excellent verses sent by the First Seat, Tuncheng, composed last year: The rolling pearls are vast and wondrously turning; Chewing through ice and frost, he swallows the character "He" (和).
In dreams, wind and rain accompany the shared sleep upon the bed. Who could entrust the path to one who moves with such freedom? Beak and shell strike simultaneously—of itself.
It may be transmitted. Phoenix dances, dragon soars—observe the guest and the host. With its head emerging beyond the heavens, how could there be no karmic affinity?
Seeing off a monk to visit Xuexi:
In the eighth and ninth months, the west wind is cool. A single sail hoisted high, it passes beyond Qiantang. At the edge of the eye, one intends to pay homage to Xuexi.

Snow. The practice of the nose has already become the fragrance of Mount Xiang; where teacher and disciple meet, all traces and forms vanish. When knowledge and views are exhausted, the path of temporal opportunity perishes.
Do not follow Danyuan in drawing circles, causing Mazu to expend his efforts in calculation.
In the rhyme of "Clouds Deep," I thank Zhongzhu Konghai for his invitation:

An old man with white hair and a weathered face, entrusted to the Yuwu Peak, expounds the profound mysteries atop the Jiliu summit. With a single blow of the staff, sun and moon swallow the thousand worlds;
with a single shout, wind and thunder shake the nine heavens. Let the torchlight rest in idle daylight; why must a mere blade of grass strike the great bell?
The great bell. My old friends are all Liu Wenshu. His feet press upon the dragon’s waist, leaving no room for others.
Sent to Guo Wuzhu, Huiyun, Muyan, Wanshou, and Daming: as the years have slipped by, I am now a seventy-year-old elder.
With whom can I clasp hands and speak of the ancestral school? Throughout my life, there have been but two or three true friends.

For those like us, the distance is separated by tens of thousands of layers of clouds and mountains. Since we struck the drum of retreat for our own peace and happiness, we have mostly not heard the temple bell since falling asleep.
In the cold of winter, only the tall pine trees remain; they do not change their ancient appearance because of the frost and ice.
To the two attendants, Gaomo and Zongni:
An old man in disarray by the east of the Xilei Pavilion speaks with his heart; his words also propagate the school. The golden needle and double lock—the celestial mechanism is secret;
the precious seal slightly opens, yet the brocade seams remain layered. With wise illumination, contemplate deeply the three blows of the staff; like Rāhula, strike once more.
The bell sounds; how can one compete with the wind-crazed son of Puhua? He has transmitted the countenance of the old man Panshan.

Sent to Min Chun-gu, before the Hall of the Osmanthus at Kyeong-dong, he serves his father. He smiles as he watches the Yangtze and Han rivers naturally flow toward the sea. The withered flowers are swept away by the thousand winds.
A single fragment; the fragrance of incense wafts as rain falls in layers. Within the dream of Tuṣita Heaven, iron drums are pushed; amidst the shadows of the celestial city, golden bells are cast.
That the tally-sticks fill the stone chamber is but a trivial matter; yet outside the door, how can the shoes of those seeking entry be accommodated?

Dedicated to Master Yǎnfú Dàyòng of the Kingdom of Southern India, the Elder in Crimson Robes: Speech and silence both forgotten, the True Source is revealed; The Middle Way meaning of Tiantai is upheld.

Transformative practice extends through the thirteen layers of the Flower Treasury World (*Avataṃsaka*). Fragrant clouds drift and coil within the jeweled nets; Flower rain falls in profusion, scattering and covering all.
The Lecture Bell: Seeing that your head has turned white over these years, it is as if one views the mountain’s form after a snowfall.
Sent to Juezong, Shengmin, Zhongfu, and Qimie:
Your lofty spirit resembles that of Master Muzhou; you can both revive our school and extinguish it. You manifest the "Dragon’s Eye" of Jibei.
Correct. Enveloping Shaoyang, the iron net is heavy. With snowy peaks, he himself bears the Maitreya statue; in the frosty sky, who strikes the Zhai-bell?
Both city and mountain forest are wondrous beyond compare; a single lake of autumn water reflects the countenance of heaven.
Next, Dongshan Wujie sent attendant Mei to Lingyan;

following the rhyme, I rejoice that this later-born one possesses a transcendent resolve. It happens that Yanhou has just dispersed his assembly, leaving behind Dongshan’s words for the parting guest.
These are superior to the failure to send a letter from Nanyue. He brought forth the dish to present it first to me; I received it back, holding it with both hands.
Entrusted to you. With tail wagging and head shaking, go forth like this. What harm is there in letting what is hidden become manifest?

I present this "Broken Sandalwood Basin" to the Chief Seat Shi of Zhongzhu from Zhongfeng. Great penetration meets the opportune moment, opening wide the crown of the head; sweeping away the Three Mysteries to support and aid [the teaching].
To the north, he overturns the hundred dharmas and gives rise to the school of Ci'en. How can one describe his dream-climb to Tuṣita? What discourse could be made upon the empty sky he expounds?
As the year draws to a close, those carrying provisions come to join me; they expand beyond the mundane world to establish heaven and earth.
Long have we harbored hopes for the assembly at Longhua;

may blessings and fortune reach Wenxi and his brothers. They have vanished from sight, arriving at the Southern Hall. Is this not a case where the mountains grow ever higher and the waters flow ever deeper?

Since they have turned toward paths of many perils and hardships, I have letters but no means to inquire after their well-being. Who can exert the power to turn back heaven and grant them life on this day?
The nation is at peace; let the rivers run clear while my head turns white. Yet we must still join hands to discuss the fundamental principles of our school.
