Next, Xuedou Hua echoes the rhyme of Guo to present this verse to Chief Seat Ming:
When stepping out the gate under the moonlight at Zhongfeng, There was only silent, lingering awareness within. Leaving the kiln behind, he laughed at those who consider themselves clever.
Han: "I have ruined my family to bring back such a fine child. The Mahāyāna Dharma discourse is wondrous; the Tuṣita Heaven dream was slow to awaken.
From now on he shall roam freely across the seas; let him strike the crown of his head once more at the heavy barrier.
Attendant Songguang returns to Guanghua; the Master himself has come from Wansong.
He departs again wearing a double-layered paper robe. The heart-seal of the Direct Pointing School remains;
the gate of expedient means is opened wide. What need is there for straw sandals and bamboo staffs? Green waters and blue mountains are utterly beyond [conceptualization].
A speck of dust. Last night the spring breeze reached the southern foot of the hill; trouble you to inquire after the plum blossoms at the crest of the ridge.
Seeing off Chan Master Guan as he returns to Sanzu:
The White Crane Peak is high, its emerald green piercing the heavens. The single stream of the Qian River flows with clear, rippling waves. There is a path in the ancestral gate where people travel.
A little. The ocean of wisdom is windless and its mirror is naturally perfect. On the mountain valley, the horns and head of the stone ox are revealed;
the golden countenance has the skin of a leper dog’s foot worn through. Having turned one’s body beyond the precipice of the pivot, one collects the old price for the rush sandals.
In praise of the Cloud Abbot’s silent recitation of the Lotus Sūtra:
Reciting the Puṇḍarīka since childhood, twenty autumns have passed since then. No trace of the original characters remains before his eyes;
From between his brows, he naturally emits the white tuft of light. Within the blazing fire-house lies a treasury of spiritual powers; He understands the towering clouds and mountains.
The stage is cleared. From the root of the tongue, the words flow forth like water cascading from a high roof; each sound resonates with the clanging of iron bells.

As he sends off the Chan Master Xuan of Tiantai for Jiangxi, this journey shall carry him all the way to the Great River of the West. There is no need to beg others for guidance; Huangbo has already administered three painful blows.

A blow! When the great fools gather, they share but a single stalk of leek; there is mystery and subtlety, yet it is not the true limit. There is neither right nor partiality—this is but half the teaching.
Having traversed Mount Kuang-lu, he beholds Mount Heng; on Dongting Lake, the frost makes the waters white and the sky low.
The *Huateng Tianxin Tongxuan Dazhang* arrived. He produced two poems in the same rhyme as my "Shi-zhong" (Ten Poems on Forbearance), which seemed to contain his inner sentiments.
One was intended as a gift for his journey to the East; the other was sent to Nengren Yongzhang and Tianzhang Yongzhen.
Snow weighs down the tips of the plum branches, yet it has not yet melted. How deeply I admire the paper robe, superior to the hempen cloak.

Wind arises at the valley mouth as a thousand rivers roar; the moon reaches the heart of heaven, a single mirror held high. Swallowing and incinerating the ten voids, his eyes shine bright and clear; reversing the flow of the Three Gorges, his eloquence surges like a torrent.
Virtue-clouds do not descend from the summit of Wondrous Peak; how much toil has the youth endured on his southern quest?
The celestial mirror opens wide as the lingering mists vanish; at the Orchid Pavilion on a spring day, we try on our light spring robes. A thousand-jin strength rests upon the tip of the brush;
the Five-Phoenix Tower is completed with masterful skill. How tangled are the creeping weeds, difficult to map; the surging floods block the road, flowing vast and wild.
Seeking the Cave of Yu to the east is not without inspiration, yet these two feet of mine have lately been unable to endure the toil.
In the same rhyme, I respond to Yuan Tong’s invitation, who remained at Tianzhang Monastery:
The story of the "dead cat's head" has long been lost to transmission; From a thousand miles away, this sealed letter comforts my old age.
Every phrase is entirely the lion’s roar; Every sound shatters the wild fox Chan. Flowers bloom on iron trees, yet spring leaves no trace; Flames erupt from the icy river, yet the snow remains.
The entire river is filled. There is another pivot that illuminates the ancestral enterprise; do not worry about there being no path to penetrate the profound.
Responding in the same rhyme as the previous verse to Tianzhang Yongzheng:

"When name and reality correspond, how could it be a mere rumor? Its elegance is worthy of succeeding the era of Yonghe. Without departing from a single thought, one contemplates the dust of the world."

The kalpa ends and one is liberated from the three calamities to reach the fourth dhyāna. The winding streams and flowing cups welcome new guests; the lush forests and tall bamboos remain the old clouds and rivers.

As the *xuan* and *chi* flutes play in alternation, they silence all other sounds; the melodies of the *huqia* flute turn toward the profound, echoing with every beat (at this time, Shi Yue-zhi and Tian-min both sought refuge from the turmoil here).

Beyond the golden brocade robes, what else remains to be transmitted? In the distant ten thousand years of the Dharma-ending age, one must chew thoroughly the iron-sour dumplings of Mount Dongshan and swallow raw the chestnut burrs of the Patriarch Huai.
As the myriad stars bow to the North, the heavens manifest their signs; as the ten thousand streams flow toward the sea, the rivers find their source.
Cast down the monastery’s banner-pole before the gate, and let the crane be white and the crow be black—whatever they may be.
In the preceding rhyme, I sent this to Nengren Yongzhang, Baolin, and Biefeng, who dwell on the mountain and have obtained the true transmission of the axe-handle.
One more year has passed since crossing the Qiantang River to the east. Placing a blade of grass, he casually established a Buddhist monastery;

responding to circumstances whether favorable or adverse, he enters all levels of dhyāna. He carves out a new sun and moon, opening the celestial mirror; yet the wind and thunder remain as they were before.
At Heshui, this old man does not blow the unperforated flute; he returns to him a single word complete with the Three Mysteries.
Within the Xianshou school, he excels in the orthodox transmission. On his waist-cloth, he recalls the *Putong* era.

All know that Qianzi was able to propagate the teachings, but who recognized that Guifeng had early on awakened to Chan? A single stroke of lightning passes faster than a split arrow; a thousand verses flow forth like surging waves.
The Long River flows on; in its brilliance, one treads upon the aperture that pierces through to heaven. In every dharma, how could there ever be a falling away from the wondrous mystery?

At Qiguang Monastery’s Qiyun Pavilion, the yellow tubers have no intention of producing purple clay. Dwelling high, they naturally occupy the white clouds’ retreat. The five peaks cut out against half the sky.

Above, twin streams turn back; below, a solitary islet looms low. When the dragon takes human form, he departs to hear the Dharma; when the monkey follows the moon’s descent, it cries out amidst the frost.
Turning one's body, there is another path leading to the profound mystery: the Southern Dipper shifts east, the Northern Dipper moves west.

Presented to Chan Master Shou, Head Seat of Tianning Temple, who originally entered the inner chamber under the guidance of the Double Emei Peak. His tenure as a seat-holder at Nanhu was likewise leisurely.

Having eradicated the "one hundred negations" and the "four propositions" from their very roots, the ten thousand households and a thousand gates are all thrown wide open. Like a brocade-scaled fish leaping through the snowy waves of the blue sea, he pours forth the white wine of Qingyuan.
The spring ale. Forging an iron boat is but a trivial matter; the true wind of the vast eon calls it back.
Embracing Heaven, I seal this single school of the Dragon Flower Friends;
my brothers at Home are of this one lineage alone. Sharing a bed under the night rain can never be repeated. Planting the Vajra Banner, I strike the stone.
The drum: using black beans to open the seal of heaven. Watch him let out a great lion’s roar; what room is there for my own traces of a wild goat?
At the Dragon Flower Assembly, he shall find a peerless companion; upon the stone, he speaks much of the Elder Nantang.
In the same rhyme, I reply to Chief Seat Zhì:
The western wind scatters celestial fragrance through the courtyard; Facing one another, words are forgotten, yet the meaning grows ever deeper.

Do not let your reputation and brilliance be lightly flaunted; It is better to securely conceal your traces. Reflect deeply on the Great Teaching by frequently unrolling its scrolls; Look up to the former sages with unwavering reverence.
Gazing across the vast ocean, seven years have passed since the ancestral temple was consumed by flames; yet the banners of the three frontiers still flutter in the wind.
Wanshou Yuyin, rightful grandson of Xuantian Rui, has opened the Dharma in Zhongwu; I have had no leisure to offer my congratulations.
I have previously taken the trouble to send inquiries, accompanied by a gift of medicinal broth.
On my way, I visited his grandson, Renshou Tianze, and read two poems in response to Bai Ma Yueming—one to express gratitude for his humble seclusion and one to present to Tianze.
It is my hope that when Yan Shenggang sees them, he will join us in a shared smile.

An old man heads toward the desolate wilds to learn how to plant rice; he need not worry about what will become of the ancestral temple. In the Three Wu regions, the flourishing transformation meets the Zen month;
throughout the nation, the patriarchal wind finds its home in Niaoke. All words beyond the written script are medicinal stones; within the breast, there is no room for the clash of arms.
Everyone knows that my uncle has neither Zen nor the Way; yet the principle of forging iron into a boat—how could it be otherwise?

In different fields, we repeatedly observe the ears of grain merging; unaware, we enter the realm of non-being through laughter and conversation. When the Way of host and guest is in harmony, how could traces remain?

When the sentiments of ordinary and sage are forgotten, one naturally sheds the nest. The dragon-king’s command stirs the nine abysses like thunder; the sun turns back three stations from the spear of Lu Yang.
The flying spray of the waterfall becomes a cascading river of eloquence, startling the Nāgas of the Dragon Pool into submission.
Five Verses on the Buddha’s Birth, Enlightenment, Nirvana, and the Sandalwood Image of Avalokiteśvara, by the Elder Songyue. A Zen practitioner requested these verses for chanting.

Buddhas and Buddhas are born together in this very realm; sentient beings and Buddhas are fundamentally not distant from one another. It is only because they cannot employ the fragrant bath themselves that [they remain as such].
Washing away, he instead takes him and pours foul water over him. Siddhārtha presents his wares from the very start; Yungmen’s fine staff brings forth the sprouts of the mind.
A manly deed that startles heaven and shakes the earth—do not boast of storing a "Little Bride" in a golden palace.
Since you first set out from the capital through the spring cities, six years have passed before your resolve for the deep mountains was finally fulfilled.

Your neck is adorned with the round light of the moon in the silver river; your entire body is as cold as dew upon jade-ice. You have simultaneously realized the samādhis as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; you have ascended the single path of the True Vehicle across the ocean of lands.
The Dharma masters and monks of the final age know nothing of this; they wear borrowed robes and seek food, wandering about in vain.
How great is the unsurpassed gate of *nirvāṇa*! Originally non-existent, how could there be anything that persists?
The Dharma-eye was personally transmitted by Kāśyapa; the ancestral wind did not fall from Śākyamuni. Reaching the profound and exhausting the subtle, the teachings have flowed on;
continuing the flame and linking the fragrance rests with the legitimate descendant. Shattering empty space to seek traces—clearly, for every blow there is a mark.
Udayana remains only within the realm of worldly sentiment; how could the True Buddha ever depart and not return? His marks and signs are solemn and majestic like the full moon;
yet this carving and polishing has merely wasted sandalwood. No effort was required to raise his hand, yet as soon as one engages in conceptual thought, the vision is no longer expansive.
From antiquity to the present, it is all one and the same day: there he sits, resplendent upon his single throne of purple-golden mountain.

A wondrous body adorned with a hundred jewels serves as refuge and shelter for ten thousand *yojanas*. Hearing, contemplation, and cultivation constitute the *samādhi*; compassion and wisdom form the thousand-spoked wheel.
Preaching the Dharma, he naturally transcends emptiness, things, and self; scattered flowers gather like celestial deities at every turn.
This realm of perfect penetration requires no bolt or key; the fragrance of white sandalwood wafts through the springtime on the seashore.
Seeing Master Ke off as he returns to visit his teacher:

With a round skull like an ancient cauldron, he is called a son of the Śākya; such an enlightened master is difficult to encounter. This is the place where a needle can be cast into the water of the alms-bowl; it is the moment when Mount Sumeru rolls through a mustard seed.
Mindless as a mirror image, his brilliance emerges like a needle from its bag. Who would have thought that after his southern pilgrimage, he would once again place his eyes above his brows?
Responding in kind to Professor Zhang Boyi’s verse:
His perilous words startle the gentry; his true spirit sweeps away the miasma of heterodoxy. Before unfolding the wings for his journey southward, he has already cleared the herds of the north.

Seeking the words of the monks, one pursues the Great Way; crossing the waters, one arrives at the deep clouds. From where could the Three Teachings have been established? Exhausting the source, they remain undivided.

To the Secretary Gang I present this: not a single stroke is drawn. Looking at one another, eyes are like eyebrows. It is difficult to make the Master understand; it is permitted only for the Old Barbarian to know.
Where the patterns of expression are fully manifest, when the wheel of the Dharma turns subtly, the ten directions are illuminated as one; even a spark from flint is too slow.

To Chan practitioner Duan: When silently closing the volume of the Lotus Sutra and turning the lotus flower, why concern oneself with the passage of years? If you do not understand the Parable of the Poor Son, it will be difficult to reach the House of the Dharma King.

Dew and rain fall without distinction of high or low; yet roots and stems possess varying degrees of difference. In every instance where the teaching is revealed, the meritorious practices performed are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

In the same rhyme, I send off Attendant Xin, who wishes to become a guest of the Chan school: First, one must give rise to the Great Mind. If one does not roar like a lion, how can one bear the burden of the Elephant King?
At every step one transcends all quarters; at every turn the wondrous sound is revealed. The eyes of the wandering monk are opened wide; neither mountain nor sea can be called high or deep.
In the rhyme of Master Huiji, I present this to Master Ding:
Standing in the heart of the great ocean, Walking atop a thousand peaks. His breast holds no sun or moon; His hands and face possess the scales of authority.
The plum and willow stir with the spring light; the lakes and mountains clear from the lingering snow. A phrase from within the *nāga*’s meditative concentration—utterly dead, yet utterly alive.
In the rhyme of my dharma-brother Songyue, I send off Chan Master Ming on his journey to Mount Wutai:
Treading the paths of Wutai, you truly engage in a vast and boundless wandering. How stern and majestic is that sword-like brow! A floating aura of lethal energy alone lingers there.
Countable without remainder are his sons; none can match this one head. At Caoqi, the wind and moon are fine; emerald pure, they contain the chill of autumn.
Following the rhyme to see off the monk Fǔ:
Day after day, mountain upon mountain, ten thousand peaks again. To clarify the seal of the mind-ground, one must pass through the patriarch’s barrier.

Whom can the resonance of the Way rival? Mundane ties naturally cease their grasping. With both scales and weights held in one’s hand, one must surely laugh at those who peer through a tube for a mere speck of color.
As Xian, the *venerable* (karmadāna), departs for the direct path to Mount Wutai:
Who boasts of the "trap-for-tiger" ruse? Before a word is spoken, he has already been scrutinized and seen through. Hand-in-hand, we shall return together.
The lion appears in the void; the kalaviṅka bird flies beneath his feet. Celestial flowers are truly abundant, falling in chaotic profusion upon my meditation robe.

In the same rhyme, I present this to Attendant Fu of Mount Jiangshan, who does not dwell in a court monastery: Living in leisure near the roadside, I still encounter guests as before. I put on my robes in a topsy-turvy fashion.
How much more so now that you have arrived at Mount Zhong; it is difficult to hide the Northern Dipper. From the eagle’s nest emerges the majestic phoenix;
amidst your conversation, celestial fragrance is released.

As you, Abbot Zangyuan, depart for Jinling, your stillness is inexhaustible. Yet you wish to go further to Jinling: the universe is empty before your two eyes; mountains and rivers age with your single staff.
Unfold the inexhaustible treasury and continue the lamp of the ancestral masters. Do not follow the example of Chan practitioner Xian, who remained silent while longing for the blue peaks.

To instruct Chan practitioner Ang on the essential matter of traveling abroad: there is no need to seek elsewhere; only when you have extinguished all thieving thoughts will you realize that mindfulness is all-pervasive.
Vast and empty across the three realms, loftily he emerges with his head held high. Able to let go completely from the precipice, his liberated body is all the more elegant.

In this same rhyme, I present these verses to the attendant Zhi, who holds the rhinoceros-hide fan: He is truly a jewel upon the mat. Do not sever the seed of the Buddhas; You must become a cause for benefiting living beings.
Gold refined a hundred times is cleared of its dross; a mirror polished again and again is free from dust. He comes with such ease, saying: "This is one body of freedom.
In the same rhyme, I present this to Attendant Ben:
Where the pecking and the hatching meet, It is difficult for mother and chick to know. If they can remain undifferentiated for even a moment, Then their future greatness may truly be expected.

Self-confidence arises entirely from oneself; when dwelling among the multitude, who else can you ask? After the clouds have dispersed across the eight directions, the single moon shines its brilliance perfectly.
In this same rhyme, I send off Attendant Zong to rejoin his studies at Mount Jiang under Master Dafayi:
Do not remain long apart from an enlightened teacher. You must know that the final word is not the same as the initial impulse.
When the whisk was rebuked, when ascending the hall the mats were rolled up; the paper robe could not reach him—whom shall we take by the hand to return together?

In this same rhyme, I send off the Dharma-warden Tan, a man who has waged a battle of the Dharma. With a roar he shattered the golden city; his coming and going weighed as much as a goose feather, while fame and glory were as light as the sea and mountains.
Carrying my pitcher and bowl, I passed through Xili; the season is approaching Qingming. Upon the road from Baiyue to Santai, I wandered on, heedless of the distance.

Following the original rhyme, I lament the loss of the son of Yungan, who found joy in having no dual attachments and maintained himself solely through humility. Opening his door, he faced the wild waters; for guests, he rolled back the sparse curtains.
Ancient temples such as Fengxue and the Chan lineage following this hermit—these koans have been fundamentally self-existent; from now on, who is permitted to pick them up?

Having traveled three thousand *li* on pilgrimage, I dived into the nine abysses to seek the pearl. Grasping the handle of a broom upside down, I sweep away the "wild fox" Chan with a resounding blow.
Having settled the affairs of this life, I now reflect on karmic ties yet unfulfilled. The true path of the Old Barbarian remains; he took up his sandals and crossed to the Western Heaven.
He sends this message in advance for the future; as he departs, he pulls at my robe. Out of pity for my aging self, he has lent his crimson countenance its radiance to my white hair.
There are those who cherish the great lineage of the Way, yet no mandate is granted as time passes. The path at the head of a thousand sages is the same as returning hand-in-hand.
Mayan, in presenting this to Shao Shangren, says:
To understand the customs of this gate, one must rely on diligent effort. With tireless devotion, forgetting both dawn and dusk; with steadfast perseverance, enduring through autumn and winter.

Once cast away in a ditch, it was severed; now it has become a paulownia tree beneath the hearth. With a single blow, he expands his livelihood; for a thousand ages, he continues the lineage of his ancestors.
Duan Qian presents this to Master Ying: all sharp edges have been entirely removed.
He appears as if stunned and yet like one who is simple-minded; myriad phenomena do not reach him, and in that singular truth, he finds his own delight.
Forgetting artifice is like the *wangxiang*; to conceal the profound is the expedient means. Among those who have known the truth since of old, only Master Wang remains.
Next, following the rhyme of "Zhengzong" (The True Lineage) by Jiangshan, I send this to Attendant Qi as his fan breaks—he seeks the ox.
The trigger of a thousand-jun crossbow has been released; who now speaks of the True Lineage? The autumn moon shines forth of its own accord.

The sound of mortars and pestles vibrates through a thousand homes; a single wild goose returns to the clouds and sky. Having failed to return to Xichuan, I changed my attire to inquire about the eastern promontory.
Master Zhuyuan’s Four Mountain Songs: At the request of Attendant Shou, I offer these verses in response.

In my old age, I have no concerns; with my body at ease, all matters are sufficient. Though I have inherited the transmission outside the teachings, I still take up the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra* for reading.

The eastern peak abounds in creamy butter; the western ravine is rich with streamside greens. Having eaten my fill, I bid farewell to the dusty world; what need have I for the deer that carries blossoms in its mouth?
Within the vast expanse of the six directions, every single being is but a guest. One man is the match for ten thousand men; six horses are driven by a taut rope.
Luyang did not need to brandish his halberd for the midday sun to set in the west. Alas, old Zhaozhou! Only at eighty did he begin his pilgrimage.
I possess a stringless zither, which harbors the sounds of antiquity; is it that there is no "Song of Shaolin," or does it simply fail to enter the hearts of people of this age?
The white crane returns after a thousand years; the vermilion phoenix sings for but a single day. Alas, O Jingwei! You do not heed the depth of the vast blue sea.
I possess a flute without holes; though it has a mouth, who can understand how to blow it? One who blows it is not easily found, and one who truly understands how to listen is indeed hard to know.
The empty mountains are silent during the day; the grass seat is lush in spring. A single yellow oriole sings atop a high branch.

He should have paid homage at the ancestral stupa of Yinyang An, rather than receiving Yunju’s "spike behind the head. Yet he came instead to the tiger’s den to exert his full majesty; what moves the heart most is Mei Yang.
The Old Man [Baizhang] distantly entrusted the five-generation robe to Yangqi;
he paid homage at the ancestral stupa of Damei.
The rotten plum has neither color nor fragrance; even when crushed and chewed, it can still deceive Old Pang. He pinned down Mazu’s three inches.
The tongue flows backward into the Eastern Sea and enters the Western River.
In response to the rhyme of the miscellaneous sayings of Chan Master Hejiao:
"The single spirit is unobscured, ancient as it is now; delusive thoughts sink of their own accord amidst every speck of dust. The bright pearl of Hepu is born from within the oyster."

The belly. When the bright moon of the cool autumn reaches the heart of the sky, gain and loss are both forgotten and the meaning of the words is true. At that moment, the Lord of Space is struck down; a thousand doors and ten thousand gates are without locks or keys.
The eight-armed Nātha manifests his half-body.
The guest prefect Songguang returns to Shuangxi;
entering the deep gate, he has already discerned the wind from afar. Is this not a path that opens before the pivot of action?
When the double stream plays with the bright moon tonight, one suspects his very self is within a crystal palace.
Mourning the passing of the monk Xibai, who wished to repay his country:
as the time of death arrived, he prepared his traveling gear. Having finished bathing, he changed his robes and sat in passing away. The tide recedes at the Sea Gate and the new moon rises;
one knows not that his entire being is revealed in majestic dignity.
Today the city of Great Nirvana opens its gates; vast as it encompasses the dharma-realm, it is pure and free from dust. How many skillful means does he employ for the sake of beings?
Nothing is more intimate than this single encounter.
The four elements disperse and the five aggregates become empty; at this moment, one may surely establish the fundamental tenet.
With the mark of the broad and long tongue, he swallows the vast ocean, extending it from amidst a blazing mass of fire.
Seeing off the Chan practitioner De-mao Jian on his pilgrimage to the Ancestors in Xiangnan and Tanbei:
The road stretches long and far; it is not as good as the spring breeze atop the hundred grasses. In the night that follows, one shall gaze upon the waterfalls of Mount Kuanglu:
The great river is like a white silk ribbon, the moon like a curved hook.
The fragrance of the Five Leaves fills the Great Tang; the golden sacred bones are increasingly difficult to conceal. It is precisely now that the iron spades should be frequently raised and lowered;
do not ask about the length of the watchtowers in Hunan.
The ancestral teacher’s sacred remains pervade heaven and earth; a single radiance penetrates both dawn and dusk.
If you do not understand that the mirror is before the trigger, you will find it easy to enter the gate of the superior man.
In the style of Master Zhu Yuan’s "Verses on Miscellaneous Remarks from Leisurely Dwelling":
The youth’s southern quest was a mistaken calculation; Seeking his original companion, he beheld Qingliang. The eyes remain beneath the eyebrows;
Deep in springtime in the courtyard, the grass grows of its own accord.
At that time, Wumeng was in his old mountain cave; he asked, "Why must you be so hurried? According to the command, taking up the essential principles is a matter of extraordinary distinction;
let the swallow on the beam speak of the True Constant.
The worldly path is difficult to traverse, as slippery as moss; dwelling in the mountains is easy, yet it makes one’s heart turn to ash. People of this age are simply unwilling to come;
I, the old man, keep my thatched gate open all day long.
Hanshan and Shide are formidable adversaries; Bailin and Old Pang are not fellow practitioners. Clouds fly high and waters flow low;
the horse's head points north, the ox's head points south.
Skin and marrow shattered, he felt pity for the Patriarch; arrow-points meeting, he laughed at Sanping.
On the mountain path of eight hollows and nine mounds, only the solitary cloud is permitted to manage the farewells and welcomes.
The Vajra Seal is the singular mind-transmission; it does not exist prior to the Great Kalpa of Bhīṣmagarjitasvara. A few brushstrokes depict distant mountains, the ocean, and the sun;
a single stream flows through green willows and mist.
Picking up withered wood to boil snow and cook the moon-balls; the incense smoke is fine upon the round porcelain bowl. Xiangyan and Dayang have but small skills;
Yuanmeng has come straight before the gate of Muzhou.

Showing the assembly sixty thorn branches, yet not a single mark remains; a slap across the cheek is for knowing gratitude. Where tiger’s head and tiger’s tail are gathered together, the Tathāgatas of the three periods all have their lineages extinguished.

Sending off the Monk with a Snow Song: The air of spring has not yet risen high. The sea and sky are vast and wide; one beholds the surging waves of the whales. Turning around, he treads upon the summit of Penetrating Mystery;
an eighty-year-old elder wearing an embroidered robe.
Within the mountain of form there is treasure; seek it not elsewhere. Sitting and cutting off heaven and earth, a hundred thoughts cease.
A flying waterfall opens across a thousand-foot cliff; amidst the massed clouds, one gazes upon the dragon pool.
Master Ma takes a single gulp of the Western River; last night at the third watch, the moon shone through the window. At Lanzo’s crag, the fire of yellow tubers burns;
the spring breeze blows upon the long, entangled vine-stump.
The great river stretches across the foot of Mount Lu; sails are full with the eastern wind as the waters rise. Within the stupa there is neither Buddha nor patriarch;
upon the back of empty space, someone walks.
Now there is no receiving; in the past there was no transmitting. A single phrase completely transcends eons beyond measure. Before even entering the gate, one must first discern the mark.
The great river’s misty waters are a jade-green that reaches the heavens.
In the same rhyme, lamenting for Master Wujian of Huading:
Between the mundane world and the world-transcending, there is no separate dharma; How could nirvana and birth-and-death be different paths? The auspicious dragon has snapped its golden chain;
Ten thousand miles across the vast sky, the moon’s orb stands solitary.
Short hair, shaggy and disheveled, gleams with light through the night; before and behind his body, all is worthy of pity.
No one beholds the King-Crown Samādhi; it is in vain that Pāpīyān laughs a single laugh.
The sea and sky are vast and wide as the evening clouds hang low; Mount Huading’s peak soars high, level with the Big Dipper. The moon shines upon the stone bed and all movement has ceased;
deep in the night, one still hears the wooden cock crow.
Shattering the浑仑 (Hunlun), spitting it out and swallowing it again—whose message can be discussed at such a time? The frost-whale awakens from the dream of saṃsāra;
the boundless ocean of karma is the Buddha’s original root.
Seeing off Abbot Kuai as he returns home to visit his teacher, Master Zhuyuan:
A True Successor of Mount Mao, the Elder of the Evening. He cleaves through a thousand peaks and leans against the tall pines;
when the wild goat hangs from its horns, there is no trace left behind—how easily could a hound chasing a clod of earth encounter him?
When the faculties and their objects are completely shed, the numinous light shines forth; throughout daily life, how could there ever be any concealment?
Having entered Luoteng Peak as the third month ends, a fine breeze blows open the fragrance of a hundred blossoms.
Seeing Jing the Venerable Return to Yue:
Three Times Passing Before the Hall, the Battle of Dharma Concludes. The wind and moon of Lake Jian embrace the lofty terrace; Upon the water’s flowers, no idle dust settles;
May the green mountains now be permitted to escort his reflection back.
A Verse by Master Xiyu Feng Sent to His Junior Disciple, Attendant Haoshou:
The teachings of the Dharma are as deep and vast as the sands of the Ganges; To speak of the wondrous and discourse on the profound, the path becomes increasingly divergent.
When both ordinary and sage are forgotten and all-knowing views are exhausted, The great chiliocosm is entirely the realm of the Dharma King.
How easily one returns home! A hundred cities of misty waters stretch boundlessly to the horizon. Before the feet have even moved, the bamboo sandals are worn through;
the cool moon is high, and the pine shadows slant.
My son, as you depart, you must clearly understand direct pointing: it is right here at the eastern side of the Miaoluo Pagoda.
Picking up the matter of meeting at another peak, the rain of flowers upon the lecture platform is falling thick and misty.
At Vulture Peak, he merely smiled while holding up a flower; the golden-haired lion emerging from its cave brandishes its claws and fangs. With a single crash of thunder, heaven and earth turn black;
sitting and watching, one sees a flash of lightning strike like a golden serpent.
I see you off, Xiangyin Hui, a man of the four dhyānas, to the foot of Mount Baozhu in Jinling.
This is Jinling: where mists and waters stretch far to the Iron Cauldron City. Through how many ages have there been matters of rise and fall?
The mountains and rivers have no mouth to offer their critique for you.
A hundred-foot tiered terrace holds deep ancient meaning; across the river, the misty haze sinks low at dusk. The phoenix does not grow old upon the *wutong* tree;
the weary horse neighs of its own accord in the shade of the willows.

The spring of the garden of awakening flourishes with the blossoms of true wisdom; the moonlit groves and star-studded islets are pure and free from dust. Unmoved by the waves of the world, he rests upon the stone of meditative concentration;
the drifting clouds follow his sovereign body at will.
Passing by Xuedou, he did not return home; his stubborn will remains matched only by his sturdy backbone.
At the ancient terrace where the sun sets, three hundred feet high, the misty trees of the Six Dynasties stand in deep, verdant gloom.

As the Chan practitioner Songju returns home to visit his parents at Ruiyan, the awakening that has been clear and alert across ten thousand miles lies within the lineage of master and disciple. Ninety thousand li are traversed in a single instant;
across the sea and sky, the frosty night moon shines solitary and full.
In the same rhyme, shown to two Chan practitioners of Xingping:
When the occasion arises, the mystery within the phrase bursts forth; To deliberate through speech or silence is altogether premature.
If you can topple the mountain at the gate before you, The Jambū tree stands on the shores of the South Sea.
I intend to repay the two injustices of the human world; your heels are well-suited to receive the black staff. The springtime radiance resides solely upon the plum blossoms;
what need is there to strike again at ice within the fire?
When illness arises within illness, there is no place for it to originate, and medicine has no efficacy. The sounds of autumn fill the four walls as the lamp alone shines.
This Dharma of peace and joy amidst the world of five turbidities—I speak it clearly; let the pillow listen.
Within the breast, not a trace of the original word remains; inside the room, golden light spontaneously arises. The three periods are serene and all objects are stilled;
atop the roof, the wind shakes the iron chimes.
In response to the verse by the Great Master Meiwu of Xiqiu, composed at the First Terrace of Mount Daibai:
A single branch of spring news, beyond the reach of those with limited ability, In what year did it drift down into the world of men?
It has scattered as ice through the long streets even in the sixth month.
Sending off the Guest Master Xiu:
How can one cite the phrase "cultivation is non-cultivation"? To emerge from within the gate, yet remain within the gate;
before the Thousand-Year Rock, he sings a song—a single note—and the celestial fragrance of cassia blossoms falls in profusion.
Seeing Master Jing return to Yunmen, I know that stillness is the true message; yet he must cast his body across the bustling marketplace.
A single white cloud has no place to dwell, following once more the solitary moon as it hangs from the tall pines.
Sending off Attendant Zhong to Visit the Master:
Autumn heights, leaves fall, and the cries of geese grow rare. Beyond the heavens, I rejoice to meet the white phoenix returning. Do not let the patterns on your paper robe be revealed;
The Master employs the perilous cliff mechanism in its entirety.
Harmonious silence, wordless—the song of the twelve periods of the day.
Who knows it? Upon the eyes, one naturally places a pair of brows. The divine pearl needlessly hides with the dark moon.
White clouds fly beside the green mountains.

At midnight, when a person has fallen fast asleep, they cannot be roused by anyone’s call. With the clear breeze and bright moon, autumn fills the four eaves; it is better for me to take the heavens as my tent and the earth as my mat.
At the hour of Chou (1–3 a.m.), the rooster crows; mistaking the Seven Stars for the Eight Dippers, the colt tramples the people of the world to death.
Can Shitou truly roar?
At the hour of Yin (3–5 a.m.), at dawn, the red sun breaks through the massed darkness. How many still dwell in dream within a dream? A single incense stick of purity...
Incense serves as the soul-restoring elixir.
At dawn, when the sun rises in the hour of Mao, this very ordinary mind is the Way. The pupil within the eye is the person before you;
why need one with graying hair study the Huang-Lao teachings?
At the hour of eating, white-haired heads meet under a single canopy; there is no distinction between old and new. The Brahmin who arrived just now speaks with such fine words:
"I am still the man of old, yet I am not the man of old.
At the hour of *yuzhong* (mid-morning), one who knows the sound relies on Hanshanzi; he has pressed down the gate of non-duality at Vaiśālī. *Shang Daren*.
Ah! On the day of the *qiūyǐjǐ* star, at noon, the thirty-three heavens struck their celestial drums; the Gandharva King knew nothing of it all, yet Kāśyapa rose up and began to dance for no reason.

Before noon: Who is there to distinguish between body and touch or front and back? When the myriad affairs have ceased, one returns; when has the One Dharma ever been outside the gate? The hour of *bú* (3–5 p.m.):
A single shout distinguishes the essence and function as they meet the occasion. If you do not know the phrase "the same wind on the Snowy Peaks," how can it compare to the clouds?
The gate penetrates the Dharma-body;

when the sun enters the hour of You (5–7 p.m.), one must still extend a hand within the darkness. All say that seeing and hearing penetrate the sense-bases and objects, yet how could the root of the tongue ever leave the mouth?
Dusk (Wu hour): The myriad phenomena and the vast array of forms are all of one principle; the bright moon clearly illuminates the traveler at night.
One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Midnight (Hai hour):
With the seven holes pierced and the eight apertures penetrated, he dons the armor of firmness. Beneath the mountain of ghosts, he suddenly turns his body and sweeps past the Unconditioned.
The fragrant ocean at the edge of the world.
A-he-he! Do you see it? Whether there is a Buddha or no Buddha, one must pass through it. When hungry, eat; when tired, sleep.
What can the heavens above or the earth below do to me?
In his four modes of deportment, he did not walk with others; as he stepped upon the ground, moss grew beneath his feet. How laughable that Śūnyatā-utpāda has not yet realized this:
his "non-contention" is no different from contention.
Dwelling alone, not dwelling with others; striking coral trees with an iron whip. The bright moon in the mountains is a single household;
where are the white clouds outside the gate?
Sitting alone, not sitting with others; realizing that one need not cultivate causes to realize fruits. Unbinding the three bamboo strips of the belly, one wins—
Swallowing grains of rice with the mouth;
lying down, not sharing a bed with others. While one is wide awake, how can one be so deluded? Waiting for the jade hare to come running, one does not realize the golden crow has already flown past.
In the same rhyme, I send off the four venerable monks Man, Zhen, Cheng, and Kang:
The minds of these Chan disciples are as bright as the full moon; Verses that settle heaven and earth shall be presented together. Three thousand miles away, we have walked hand in hand;
The Yellow River’s nine bends are clear through to the very bottom.
Filling his heart, he pours forth the pearl from the dragon palace; Yangshan, however, says there are no words. It pierces through heaven and earth, startling people to their wits' end;
a banana tree in the snow knows nothing of the heat.
Wishing to become a great tree to provide cool shade, he brushes away the weeds as his resolve for the Way grows long.
Turning his head toward the path beside the Yichun Terrace, the insights within his breast naturally imbue him with fragrance.

How many are the delights of a thousand crags and ten thousand gullies! The golden-scaled fish of the playful sea have emerged from the net. A fragrant breeze fills the courtyard, wafting the scent of *campaka* flowers;
do not let the Elder Vimalakīrti be disappointed.
I see you off, Head Seat Baizhuo, as you pay homage at Mount Emei;
on the back of the Golden Turtle, you must quickly turn yourself around. Gazing west toward Emei, your path of devotion is pure.
If you wish to recognize the true countenance of Samantabhadra, look at the moon with its double halo in the azure sky.
My Dharma brother Zifu Daoyuan has kindly sent me his brush, saying that it might slightly assist in the endeavor of stringing together the flowers [of the patriarchs].
I replied with two verses:
"Severing the true command at Yufquan, fresh and new; Yet you still can hold the brush to send it to an old man. How could this compare to using one's own wrist?"
Power! It points to the eternal spring of Mount Song.
From afar, he dispatches the brush of Xuan to assist in threading the flowers of the scriptures. One must behold the spiritual brilliance as it emits celestial blossoms.
Having grown old, I lack such leisurely mental strength; this matter is now entrusted to the master.
The Master Chijue has provided a response to the verse on mountain dwelling by the Patriarch Baiyun; Master Zhong requests a matching verse.
In leisurely seclusion there is nothing to be judged; A single stick of incense naturally brings its fragrance to one’s nose. When sleep ends, there is tea; when hunger strikes, there is rice.
Walking, I gaze upon the flowing stream; sitting, I watch the clouds.
Returning from my dream, the morning bell tolls atop the pavilion; the setting moon pierces the window as the night air grows clear.
Just as I rejoice that worldly karmic ties have been exhausted, I listen in stillness to the sound of the youth reciting the sutras.
Pure wisdom is suchness, fundamentally wondrous and perfect; it makes no distinction between ordinary and sage, for the essence of all is thus.
Now, when the six faculties have all ceased their activity, this is precisely the time before the Great Kalpa of Vimalacitra.
The single nature is void and still, a hundred thoughts come to rest; I needlessly hang my two eyes upon the azure sky. In this deep village courtyard, there is no dust or soil;
Ten thousand tall pines encircle a stone screen.

After seeing off Abbot Xun to pay respects at the Yong’an Pagoda and sweep away empty heterodoxies to reveal the True Vehicle, there remains but one monk from Tengzhou. Behold the moon within Mount Yong’an;
even now, it is still the lamp for writing this book.
I send word that I shall not go to Zhīyún;
I am naturally aloof from the Loyal and Upright Hermitage. For now, let us simply drift upon the light boat on Yuánhú Lake;
keep your long pole to fish in the Eastern Sea, where with a single cast you may haul up the Three Mountains and the six giant crabs.
I send my thanks to Stone Mountain;
the solitary moon and the wind and moon of the Snowy Mountains are shared equally—how could this be taken lightly? A long sword leaning against the heavens rests between the eyebrows.
Alas, on the day the flower was held up at Vulture Peak, only the *dhūta* ascetic knew how to break into a smile.
The moon of the mind is solitary and full, the resolve for the Way firm; naturally, there must be causes and conditions for Prajñā.
Transcending and rising far above the dust of worldly toil, one does not even perceive that Nantang understood Chan.
Ten thousand miles of azure sky, a single moon of cassia; it illuminates the void, all phenomena pure and free from dust. With wind and dew covering one’s entire body, one knows no cold;
how many are there who have transcended the realm of light?
Continuing the ancestral style rests with one's own person; overturning the thirteen layers of the ocean of the Tripitaka.
You must know that where the Buddhas and Patriarchs bestow their compassion, one transcends the dust of emotions and the paths of speech.
The pale kudzu from Huangyan is especially suited for the heat; it far surpasses that of Qingzhou for making robes. I have instead written this gāthā to inform you from afar:
three times three before, and three times three after.

Presented to the Venerable Master Zongshao Miaosan upon his realization of the True Principle through Zen meditation and the study of the Way: Within the Three Essentials and Three Mysteries, in a single phrase, he takes a step that overturns the crowns of a thousand sages;
the azure sky and the crimson sun move naturally from west to east.
Beholding Mount Song from within the shadows of a thousand peaks, it is precisely amidst the autumn wind and the setting sun. The entire earth, when grasped, is like a grain of millet;
Master Zeng was not deceiving the foolish and stubborn.
The wondrous song does not stir the three-inch tongue; the true mechanism resides solely upon the tip of a single hair.
With the Vajra-eye raised at the crown of the head, the six directions are seen within the palm of one's hand.
Seeing Attendant Yin emerge from Nanhu with a high-collared paper robe on: Empty and spent, all worldly toil; not a single thing remains. Go now to Jinling to seek a true friend;
Ahead lies one with a great red beard and whiskers.
Next, Tianning Konghai sends off Ke the Venerable with a verse:
The golden mallet within his sleeve is released and gathered; All the splendor of wind and light resides in the Yuebo Tower. With both eyes wide open, the vast ocean is empty;
There is no need for further laborious strategizing behind the curtains.
Seeing off Nanhua’s Head Seat, Cao Houxixiang, at Nanhua Temple on the banks of the River. Nārāyaṇa shoots his arrows through solid *lakṣas*; the seat is shared equally by wind and moon.
The Jewel Forest shines upon the *kaṣāya*.
At the Rainy Window, shown to the monk Ju:

Drops fall one by one upon the empty steps; listening amidst the rain, I could not help but let my thoughts reach as far as Jingqing. Sentient beings who lose themselves mostly chase after external objects;
They do not know that true hearing is fundamentally without sound.
Drops fall upon the empty steps as wondrous fingers point the way. By returning the hearing to hear what is heard, one beholds the complete reality.
Those of later generations who have not yet reached the realm of perfect penetration must not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma.
In mourning for my Dharma-brother, the Indian Immortal Jianchang,

who occupied the fifth seat at Zhaoti Temple and exhausted the Great Dharma; whose assembly was thronged by the crowns and canopies of the imperial procession, and whose thunderous voice resounded afar across the land of Fusang—
I have transcribed [his works] to bring home as a treasury of jewels.
Seizing upon echoes and responding to hollow sounds, he called out, "Come, come! Holding the gourd and sprouts, he planted them upon a stone. For over twenty years it was but a true dream;
now the sea wind has carried back the news of his passing.

Nandikeśvara has reached the summit of Laṅkā; this is the most victorious banner of the East. Whether alive or dead, buried or entombed, once it is clearly understood, this time the thicket of entanglements is toppled.
I send my attendant Xing to visit Yunyan;

within Yaoshan’s room, they play with the lion. Yunyan’s skillful means are lofty—he lightly hurls it back from the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, only to stir up wind and waves upon returning to level ground.
Seeing off Master Ming as he travels to Mount Lu:
This entire Great Canon of Teachings is a mere footstep. As for the ultimate reality of the true text, to whom can it be revealed?
Directly upstream on the great river for three thousand li, the towering Mount Kang rises before one’s eyes, its azure peaks piercing the sky.
Sending off Head Seat Shou back to the Tuṣita Palace to recount his dream’s return; atop the tip of the banner-pole, he dances the *Sāṃyāma* dance. Śākyamuni the Old Man knows nothing of it;
the white ox and the tabby cat have their cheeks full of smiles.
I hear that Yue Tang of Beishan has returned to Dongchan, while Yonghuai and Yueyun have both returned their robes to eat the ferns of their native mountains.

Who else like this mountain elder understands the signs of the times? Having nurtured his body and mind like those of a child, he has personally planted pines and bamboos to guard the gates of his meditation hall.
As soon as I spoke of resting from abiding, I recalled my eternal longing; our white-haired brothers have already been buried.
Amidst the corners of the village fields during years of famine, the custom of eating "horse-grain" has naturally suited us.
In the same rhyme, I respond to my four friends—Xingke of Zhongshan, Xiguo, Guhang, and Sifu of Muzhou—who carry their burdens with steadfast resolve.
Having received the lineage of the Elder of Shaoyang, how many of the younger generation have fallen into deception?
All at once they are buried and lost within the ancestral school.
Flowers are plucked and brought forth by the Iron-Demon; the kalpa of emptiness and the kalpa of space endure forever. How could the eyes of dragons or the eyes of hawks ever comprehend this?
The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time share a single gate.
A great burst of cold sweat has broken forth; all the ailments of a lifetime are now gone. The divine physician folds his hands in submission as the sorcerer Wuxian flees;
one need no longer doubt that the *gāohuáng* (the incurable spot between heart and diaphragm) is a gateway to life.

My grandfather had but a single broken sand pot; with it he carried out his livelihood, moving it here and there. He used it to boil medicine, to boil broth, and to boil congee—far superior to riding a horse to the doors of others.
Following the rhyme of my dharma-brother Songyue to see off the two venerable monks Hong and Er:
Skillfully weaving a Suzhou beauty without using a shuttle, A pair of mandarin ducks are cast forth—what can be done about them? The young gentlemen vie with one another to gaze first;
Each and every one wears water-boots upon the waves.
Just as I lamented that few would follow my Way, I suddenly saw a rain-carrying bamboo hat upon the river.
Tell the deity who tends the incense burner to take heed; do not let him overturn the tea kettle.
Jue Shouzuo has delivered the late Master Songyue’s inherited inkstone; I compose this verse to present it to him:
The Dharma community withers and the Dharma destiny declines; The Dharma lamp has been extinguished and the Dharma banner toppled. Humans and devas wail in grief while Pāpīyas laughs;
In the spring breeze, all is once again in disarray.
In the flash of lightning, one must swiftly turn over; the ocean of lands is truly but a single mote of dust. What use is the inkstone left behind to me?
It still must grind away all people of the world.
Yunmen’s staff transforms into a dragon, flying into the ink-well water of Caoxi;
it stirs up wind and thunder that shake heaven and earth, yet the bright moon remains hanging from the tall pines.
The True Man of No Rank is a dry piece of excrement; the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye is a broken sand pot. How can these compare to that child of Caoxi?
Beneath the golden incense burner sits an iron Kunlun. (These are the lines of a verse lamenting one’s own original mind.)
Next, Jingci’s Pingshan composes a poem in the rhyme of Zuqin, the Head Seat:
I long remember Master Lu leaning against his stone screen; Boundless wind and moon filled his pure breast. How can one compare this to Zhijue hanging up the "Mirror of the School"?
He shared half his seat to welcome those born late.
A thousand peaks line the lake like emerald screens; the autumn waters of the lake are clear with the frost. The essential teaching of Yongming is without past or present;
fine ripples, holding the wind, arise in succession.
Following the rhyme of Guifeng Daoyuan, I lament for Chan Master Zhuyuan of Jianfu:
With horns and fur, you possessed the body of a different species; Living fully and dying fully, you manifested complete authenticity. The waters of Chaohu have dried up, and fish and dragons weep;
You have departed to become a person who transforms others in other realms.
Plying an iron boat amidst the waves of the five turbidities, where the peaks of Mount Sumeru are submerged by surging tides reaching the heavens;
with a single blast of the iron flute, the three thousandfold world-system resounds, while a mere snap of the fingers spans eighty thousand years of human life.
Going, there is nowhere to go; thus one goes. This Dharma-gate breaks the pillar that supports the heavens. Coming, there is nowhere from which to come; thus one returns.
Amidst the sea of afflictions, one pours down the rain of Dharma.

Iron caltrops and mallets are hurled right at one's face; the udumbara flower blooms amidst the flames. How pitiable are those who remain stuck in their shells, lost in their attachments, all chasing after the sound before the word and the meaning after the phrase.
To fully manifest the spirit of the school takes but a single punch. It sweeps away the tangled vines of "exposure" Chan.
At the head of Lake Chao in the south, during the fifth and sixth months, ice fills the long streets and snow covers the heavens.
The Golden Immortal with his iron countenance does not allow a single speck of dust to stand; he sweeps it all away with renewed vigor. Beyond the city walls of Nirvana, the vital energy unfolds:
the spring breeze does not reside upon the flower branches.

Entering the Buddha’s realm poses no hindrance to entering the realm of Māra; knowing that the other is oneself and oneself is the other, one weighs lightness and heaviness upon the pivot of the scale—yet from the start, the measure has never varied by even a grain.

Both doctrine and practice are mastered through the Gate of Non-duality; a single shout for the occasion rolls like a wrathful thunderclap. The golden circle and the thorny plum are but household accoutrements;
they test all monks as thoroughly as an iron falcon.
The waters of the Chaohu Lake settle the fundamental principles; this elicits a fit of laughter from Pāpīyas. When the three periods of time are severed, mental activity ceases;
one’s entire being is the mouth—how could there be any further discursive calculation?

With sincere intent, I sing this song of liberation from emptiness: where there was deficiency, there is now abundance; where there was little, there is much. Ten thousand miles of azure sky, the clouds have all dispersed;
a single wheel of frosty moon shines upon the pines and vines.
Sent to Daochun of Jiuyuan, also addressed to Qingyuan of Shifo:

Shifo lifts his eyes and gazes upon Jiuyuan; The bond of brotherhood is naturally well understood. I know from afar that when the conversation reaches the point where it is most difficult, It brushes past the "three before" and the "three after."
In spring rains, the mountain zhen-ferns grow lush; one knows not that the mundane world holds peril.
When shall I borrow the stone for peaceful meditation, to gaze together as the solitary cloud drifts at its own will?

When it was heard that Mingyan Mumuan had appeared in the world, the robe reached Songyuan and was no longer transmitted. For his entire life, he did nothing but clench empty fists; now both hands are fully bestowed.
The secret meaning is clearly present right where you are.
Seeing off Chief Abbot Zhong beneath the lamp in late spring, we conversed until the third and fourth watches. Waiting for the crowing of the cock, we parted;
as the great river flows eastward, my feelings are beyond measure.

Entrusting himself to the scenery of mountains and peaks, he is without shame; in his study, there is no one who feels shame. He takes what is non-existent as existent, spontaneously harmonizing all things.
Who would have known that the matter of "the same breeze blowing over a thousand miles" does not reside within Xuan Sha’s blank sheet of paper?
The sound of the stream within the house, the mountains outside the house— With the single mind unmoving, myriad functions are at rest.
Knowing only how to sit steadily upon the meditation cushion, One is unaware that a lofty wind fills the world.
Lamenting that the Great Sun of Samādhi and Prajñā is sinking in the west, there is nothing to be done; yet he rouses himself and brandishes the spear of Lu Yang.
Those who previously entered emptiness wielding their spears now vie to gather the *śarīra* after the fire has passed.
The variegated phoenix soars through the void at the height of its glory; the golden sun blazes away the five Mount Sumerus.
Casting his entire body into the fire to bathe, there is no need to inquire after marrow or skin in future generations.
"I have grown old and no longer dream of the Duke of Zhou. You clearly recognize my decline; how could it be within a dream? The lofty wind of Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa stands supreme through all time;
the ink-well has no bottom, for fire burns through the void.
Good and evil have always followed two paths; what is the use of closing one’s eyes to act as if it were night? Master Zheng’s literary power is capable of lifting a tripod;

he has come to write this living stele for the Chan Master. (According to the inscription composed by Zheng Mingde, it briefly states: "In the spring of the sixteenth year of the Zhizheng era, the Master appeared in the world to reside at Dinghui Temple in Pingjiang.")

At that time, as war was breaking out, military troops were occupying the Buddhist halls, and many of the monastics were filled with grief. The Master said, "Why not rest? Why not take leave? The Master’s speech and silence were unrestrained and free-flowing, impossible to fathom.

He resigned from his duties at the monastery and stayed as a guest in the quarters of the Chief Seat (Huashouzuo) at Mount Lingyan. He spoke highly of the virtue of Governor Lu, Lord Zhou Yiqing, saying, "I shall undergo cremation; I require the Lord to serve as my witness.

On the eighth day of the ninth month of the eighteenth year, when the Lord ascended Mount Lingyan on official business, accompanied by Su, the Recorder (Lup'an) Shanchang, and Jia, the Archivist (Dianshi) Tianrui, the Master heard of the Lord's arrival and went out joyfully to welcome him. Accompanying the Lord during their night conversation, he said, "On the fourteenth day of this month, I shall undergo cremation on this very mountain. May the Lord act as my witness," and further...

"The teachings are in decline. I entrust you, Marquis, to the kings and ministers so that they may serve as external protectors of the Dharma. Be careful not to forget these words. On the thirteenth day, he again sent a poem to the Marquis, which read: "Yesterday, by the crag, I gathered firewood; [The rest of the verse follows]"

"This morning my illusory body has been transformed into dust. I earnestly entrust these words to you, O worthy lord: 'In the azure void, the clouds have cleared, leaving but a single sliver of the moon. Although the lord received the poem, he still did not believe it deeply. He further composed a verse to bid farewell to the assembly.

That night, he requested Master Hua to pile dry firewood into a high pyre and lent him a small cell to sit in. Hua said that while he would comply with the request for the firewood, there was no cell available. Pointing to a wooden bed before him, he said to Hua, "This will suffice. Hua followed the master's instructions. On the morning of the fourteenth day—

He ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly of monks. He immediately climbed onto the wooden pyre; both sides of the platform were split with dry firewood. As soon as the wood caught fire, fierce flames blazed up. Amidst this great mass of fire, he chanted: "The incense for blessing has been here for days; This numinous sprout does not belong to the Yin and Yang seeds. Its root originally came from beyond the kalpas;

Were it not for Xiujie personally revealing it, How could it be transplanted into the midst of fire? Amidst the fierce flames, he passed his prayer beads to Huahua, saying, "Take this as a reminder. Thereupon, the fourfold assembly of monastics and laypeople was struck with wonder.

I, [Name], prostrate in worship. Wherever the smoke and flames reached, many śarīras were obtained and a wondrous fragrance was perceived. When his body was entirely consumed by fire and extinguished, there were two things that remained undestroyed: his tongue and his teeth. Upon hearing this, I was struck with incessant grief and alarm.

I have composed two verses of lamentation and shall erect a stupa at Lingyan; I beg you to compose an inscription for it. A separate verse for the assembly says: "In a previous life, he was originally a monk of Shiqiao; Thus he came among men to receive both love and hate. When love and hate are exhausted, the whole body is revealed: An iron snake chews cold ice amidst the flames."
Passing the Three Pagodas after the War:

An Account of the Occasion After the rain, the Yuanyu Lake stretches far into view; Lofty and enduring, it remains like the Lingguang Pavilion of Lu. How can one speak of the presence or absence of the power of aspiration?
I listen only to the wind-chimes as they proclaim its glory.
In the same rhyme, I reply to Jingshan:

South of the State, all worldly ties are exhausted in a single thatched hut; There is not even a single word of Buddha-dharma to allow others to pick up. The old man of Lanfeng has a fine disposition;
From time to time, his elegant verses reach the south of the water.
The great is the *caitya*, the small is the hut; this most intimate matter has never been raised.
Regarding the one thousand seven hundred wild fox kōans—whom among men today dwells in Dounan?
Zhiqingyin arrived and presented him with four verses:

"Before we meet again in the future, open your heart early; What need is there to apply the 'horizontal pivot' and press against the precipice? That which was not transmitted from the land of Zhuguo (India) is now the faith of Tangtu (China);
Within the gate of one's own house, the heavens and earth are separated."
Only after twenty years has the story reached its conclusion. Who knows that Dou Ba wears a cloth shirt? He overturns the seas and mountains to seek his karmic adversary;
he splits the void into two parts.
Great yet without exterior, small yet without interior; light and darkness both forgotten, essence and function empty. *Sattvas* revel together in the wine of *samādhi*;
the monkey naturally possesses the six supernatural powers.

Heaven has no four walls, and earth has no gates. When the thorny *vilva* fruit is picked up, it is spat out and then swallowed again. At the tip of every blade of grass lies the eye of the thousand sages;
the Patriarch’s legacy is but a single broken earthen bowl.

In response to the rhyme of Xueya’s "The Ten Thousand Phenomena of the Universe Act as Attendants": The positions of the Northern Dipper and Southern Dipper do not shift; To observe the pivot of the turning wheel, look at the very summit.
This mind is known only by the Old Barbarian.

How could one further investigate the subtle and the minute regarding the "head of the phrase"? This wondrous place is difficult even for Buddhas and patriarchs to know. A single mass of clouds does not reach it;
yet, when one turns their head, both person and environment have already become entirely different.
Do not rejoice, do not grieve. What time is now? What time was ancient? Outside of the Ninefold Elixir there is no true medicine;
exhaust the ordinary mortal frame—do not loathe the slowness.

Living in this world, it is difficult to maintain such a forced countenance; if one has true aspiration, one must reach the company of the ancients. A person at leisure possesses the very bones of one who is at leisure;
were one not a person at leisure, it would not be easy to be so.
The three realms have no home; all are but guests. Where does the Way exist that it would not be intimate? Though one’s body be covered in dust, what need is there to wash it?
To wash until no dust remains is itself the very dust.

The water moves due to the wind; stillness knows no fixed time. The mountains and clouds are high, yet they do not consider themselves majestic. When both self and other are forgotten, the traces of the mind vanish;
thus, one remains profoundly at odds with the world.
In response to the previous rhyme, for the sake of Chief Seat Zhi:
Boundless wind and moon follow me of their own accord; I have gazed upon mountains and rivers until my feet no longer move.
The vital message rests upon the head of my staff; Do not let it be easily known by others.
The hawk’s eye and dragon’s gaze penetrate the subtlest depths; before anything is even raised, he already knows it. After five years of separation, we meet again;
this single phrase, meeting the occasion, sweeps away a hundred errors.
Nowadays, the Buddha-dharma is most pitiable; it is precisely the time when the monasteries are being swept clean. Who will go to the celestial palace to inquire of Maitreya?
The time has come to benefit sentient beings—do not let it be delayed.
For several years I have not been able to behold your ice-like countenance; you are separated from me by nothing more than the waters of Yuxi.
Seeing that the time for peace and tranquility is drawing near, it should not be that you remain as idly retired as this old monk.

In the desolate wilderness there is nothing to entertain noble guests; when the Way and its arts are mutually forgotten, the heart naturally becomes close. When the ancestral pivot is raised, it encompasses seventeen hundred [patriarchs];
how many have ever failed to penetrate through the golden dust?
When Hōnen turned around at Shasō, he stepped upon a solitary peak towering ten thousand fathoms high. Do not be surprised that Nantō was so withered;
from the beginning, there has been neither compliance nor opposition.
Holding fast to Zhongwen and awakening Min—one lineage, three younger brothers— At the foot of Mount Daxiong, soaring geese are severed;
At the peak of Mount Huading, the path is impassable. The seventy-two-year-old elder stands at the corner of heaven;
The neighboring rooster crows thrice, the bell tolls for the fifth watch.
In the same rhyme, I answer my Dharma brother Yunhai of Jingde:
White rice opens wide the dish of mallow; Flowers threaded through, ink and water turn bright and fresh. Early this morning, the drum beats for a communal viewing;
It fills to the brim the boat at Huating that carries the moon.
Inscription for the Constant Mountain, Presented to the Abbot Zhen:
Ah, the Constant Mountain! Unchanging and indestructible, silent yet numinous, it stands as if severed; its beginning cannot be seen.
Who can behold its end? Drilling into it and gazing upward, it is both firm and lofty. Having reached its very base, one again penetrates its summit.
In vast openness, all is beheld; in silence, it is realized within. Flowers bloom and leaves fall; spring passes and autumn comes. In a single instant, ten thousand ages pass.
Ah, how constant is Mount Chang!

In the *Seated Meditation Inscription* shown to the Chief Librarian Lin, it says that among the four modes of deportment, sitting alone is the most peaceful. The eyes are like wooden pegs; the mouth is like a foundation stone. All external conditions are severed.

The inner mind is free from agitation; throughout the three periods of time, it remains serene. The one true reality reveals itself spontaneously: this is the very face one had before one’s parents were born.
It is clearly and constantly known—neither turned away from nor touched. I am the Buddhas, and the Buddhas are I. Apply yourself with vigorous spirit.
Do not indulge in indolence or negligence. Do not dwell in the dark prison of昏荒 (hūn-huáng) sleep. The restless monkey and wild horse of the mind race about in pursuit of external conditions;
yet the nature-body is luminously vast, and when the objective realm is naturally forgotten, one responds to circumstances with spontaneous transformation—the banner of radiant light.
The Inscription on Vacuity and Whiteness, shown to Attendant Gaǒ:

The single true Dharma-realm encompasses and gives forth the ten vacuities; it is transparently bright and clear, without a gap even as fine as a hair’s breadth. It is such that vacuity is itself reality.
It is both white and black; its nature and characteristics are equal. Its essence and function are both quiescent; it is quiescent yet constantly illuminating—thus one contemplates its boundary.
It is illuminating yet constantly quiescent—thus one contemplates its mystery. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, one never departs from this middle way.
This is called the function of non-function, the unconditioned efficacy within fervent activity. How great is the sagely achievement! If you, O practitioner, truly enter this—
Through samādhi, one attains mastery over all phenomena.
An Inscription for Master Xiang of Rui-tian:
As for me, Rui-tian, I flourish without weeding; my spiritual roots are firm and deep, and my extraordinary sprouts grow luxuriantly. I am neither a common yu-herb nor a divine zhi-mushroom.
Its fragrance rises through the four seasons; when united, its ears grow together, and when divided, they branch into two. Rain, dew, frost, and snow do not fail their proper seasons;

through reaping, harvesting, threshing, and cooking, the hunger and thirst of others are comforted. How could it be that the field itself produces this auspiciousness? It is I who bring auspiciousness to the field. Furthermore, what power do I possess?
It is the source of transformation and nourishment.
Inscription for Qingyin, Presented to Chan Master Zhizang:
The clarity of water can reflect all things; when the mind is clear, no thing can disturb it.

I have long known that those who are hidden in the Way move in harmony with the times—neither opposing nor neglecting them. It was not by eating the ferns of Mount Shouyang that one’s integrity was first revealed.
The spirit and bone of Bo Yi and Shu Qi. Alas! The azure sea is clear in autumn, and the divine mountain rises abruptly.
Regarding the inscription for the monk Dao-ren of Xiao-zang at Shaolin:
Shaolin is Xiao; his practice and understanding correspond, and he has reached both the school (Zong) and the teachings (Shuo). Beyond the three vehicles of the doctrinal teachings—
To transmit this mind alone—its fragrance linked and its flame continued—shining through antiquity and soaring through the present: to abandon it for something else would not that be self-deception?
Looking back upon oneself, nothing in the world is excluded from me. Who is the observer? What is this mind? It is like seeking traces by hacking at water.
Probing the void and grasping at the bones, the paths of thought and mind are cut off; the way of speech is severed, and all is revealed in vast openness.
The moon hangs in the Milky Way—how great is Shaolin! Honored by the successive sages, its shade extends boundlessly across the eight directions, providing shelter for ten thousand years.
Inscription on a Friend-Stone Presented to Attendant Qi:
There was one as beautiful as Qi who befriended a stone; through the utmost polishing and grinding, its luster radiated outward. How could it not have possessed that essential quality?
If one is negligent in cultivation and practice, and the days and months have already passed, what is the use of regret? For a scholar regarding the Way, how can they afford to be self-negligent?
Let this thought be ever-present: as it was for the Buddhas of the past, so shall it be for the Buddhas of the future.
This school’s seal is conferred upon the Head Seat:
Ah, this school! It is natural and wondrous; it is neither orthodox nor biased; it possesses both function and illumination, like a great mass of fire.
One must not approach it; it is like a drum smeared with poison, whereby all who hear it perish. It is a singular path of transcendence, a glorious legacy for ten thousand ages.
Vulture Peak stands overturned, and Caoxi flows against the current.
"Zhu Xianming’s Inscription for Attendant Yuan:
Before Wei-yin. "The five regions of India were before [this era]" is the second line. Who knows it to be so? Before Śākyamuni appeared.
Bodhidharma has not yet arrived; the picking of the flower is already finished. Why did he cut off his arm?

If one can penetrate and transcend at this point, the total functioning of giving and taking pervades the four quarters and eight directions, sweeping across horizontally and vertically. It is the *udumbara* flower, the nine-branched luxuriant grass; the blue sky is vast and profound.
The red sun shines brightly.
An Inscription for the Listening-Pines Pavilion, presented to Zen Head Priest Wen:
The pine itself has no sound; it resounds because of the wind. It is like the grand music performed upon Mount Dongting. My ears are fundamentally still.
When things come, there is a response; the essence of mind leaves behind hearing. In silent self-realization, since that [object] is without action, how could this [mind] receive anything?
When one faculty returns to its source, the six functions remain as they were: the pine is green and the wind is cool; such are their sounds and forms.
Who designs and who plans? Sound does not sound itself; form does not form itself. It is through my seeing and hearing that your virtue is revealed.
Since your virtue does not exist inherently, my mind is likewise empty. I cleanse both ears and listen to this pine wind.
Inscription for the North Window, Presented to Chan Master Min:
Beneath the north window dwells the personage of Xi Wang; Silent and vast, bright and radiant. A pure breeze comes from the wild expanse;

The zither has no strings, yet the pines resound of themselves. Sometimes in *dhyāna*, sometimes in *dhāraṇī*; Seeking not truth, severing not delusion. Forgetting subject and object, extinction is attained.
A reflected image! A fellow carrying a shoulder-pole is difficult to approach; if you attempt to enter the gate, he will snap your backbone.
This inscription for the West Chamber was presented to Xixin by Shilixin.
The direct pointing of the single transmission from Shaoshi in the West has been the mind-sealing the mind, like water entering water. For the descendants of later generations...

Taking the crooked for the straight, one cannot distinguish east from west; how then could one know south from north? Without faith, nothing is established; the Way resides therein. To spiritualize and clarify it, all becomes vast and unobstructed. For this reason, this hall is inscribed with "West" from within. Should anyone ask what this means: [The Master] said: "If you can see the moon in the water without seeing the moon itself, you have attained the Way. He then recited a verse: "The moon in the water is not the moon; The moon in the sky is not the moon. If you wish to see the true moon, Look at the moon in the water. He then asked: "What is the meaning of 'The moon in the water is not the moon'? [The Master] said: "It is because the moon in the water is not the moon that it is called the moon. He then asked: "What is the meaning of 'The moon in the sky is not the moon'? [The Master] said: "It is because the moon in the sky is not the moon that it is called the moon. He received a blow from a single palm.
Puzhi Ming showed that Yi Benzhong was truly a man of the Way;
he wove *pú* grass to support his parents, directly embodying the Buddha-dharma. Yunmen entrusted him with the Dharma, for there was indeed a reason for this transmission.
